verses.sa:
मैत्रेय उवाच।
॥ अथ चतुर्थांशे प्रथमोऽध्यायः ॥
(वैवस्वतमनुवंशवर्णनम्)
मैत्रेय उवाच
भगवन् यन्नरैः कार्यं साधुकर्मण्यवस्थितैः ।
तन्मह्यं गुरुणाख्यातं नित्यनैमित्तिकात्मकम् ॥
verses.rom:
maitreya uvacha|
|| atha chaturthamshe prathamo'dhyayah ||
(vaivasvatamanuvamshavarnanam)
maitreya uvacha
bhagavan yannaraih karyam sadhukarmanyavasthitaih |
tanmahyam gurunakhyatam nityanaimittikatmakam ||

verses.sa:
वर्णधर्मास्तथाख्याता धर्मा ये चाश्रमेषु च ।
श्रोतुमिच्छाम्यहं वंशं राज्ञां तद्ब्रूहि मे गुरो ॥
verses.rom:
varnadharmastathakhyata dharma ye chashrameshu cha |
shrotumichchhamyaham vamsham rajnam tadbruhi me guro ||

verses.sa:
श्रीपराशर उवाच
मैत्रेय श्रूयताम् अयम् अनेक-यज्व-शूर-वीर-धीर-भूपाल-अलङ्कृतो ब्रह्मादिः मानवो वंशः ॥
verses.rom:
shriparashara uvacha
maitreya shruyatam ayam aneka-yajva-shura-vira-dhira-bhupala-alankrito brahmadih manavo vamshah ||

verses.sa: तदस्य वंशस्य आनुपूर्वीम् अशेष-वंश-पाप-प्रणाशनाय मैत्रेयैतां कथां शृणु ॥
verses.rom: tadasya vamshasya anupurvim ashesha-vamsha-papa-pranashanaya maitreyaitam katham shrinu ||

verses.sa: तद्यथा सकलजगताम् आदिः अनादिभूतः सः ऋग्यजुस्सामादिमयो भगवान् विष्णुः तस्य ब्रह्मणो मूर्तं रूपं हिरण्यगर्भो ब्रह्माण्डभूतो ब्रह्मा भगवान् प्राग्बभूव ॥
verses.rom: tadyatha sakalajagatam adih anadibhutah sah rigyajussamadimayo bhagavan vishnuh tasya brahmano murtam rupam hiranyagarbho brahmandabhuto brahma bhagavan pragbabhuva ||

verses.sa: ब्रह्मणश्च दक्षिण-अङ्गुष्ठ-जन्मा दक्षप्रजापतिः दक्षस्यापि अदितिः अदितेः विवस्वान् विवस्वतो मनुः ॥
verses.rom: brahmanashcha dakshina-angushtha-janma dakshaprajapatih dakshasyapi aditih aditeh vivasvan vivasvato manuh ||

verses.sa: मनोः इक्ष्वाकु-नृग-धृष्ट-शर्याति-नरिष्यन्त-प्रांशु-नाभाग-दिष्ट-करूष-पृषध्र-आख्या दश पुत्रा बभूवुः ॥
इष्टिं च मित्रावरुणयोर्मनुः पुत्रकामः चकार ॥
तत्र तावदपह्नुते होतुः अपचारात् इला नाम कन्या बभूव ॥
verses.rom: tatra tavadapahnute hotuh apacharat ila nama kanya babhuva ||

verses.sa: सैव च मित्रावरुणयोः प्रसादात् सुद्युम्नो नाम मनोः पुत्रो मैत्रेय आसीत् ॥
verses.rom: saiva cha mitravarunayoh prasadat sudyumno nama manoh putro maitreya asit ||

verses.sa: पुनश्च ईश्वरकोपात् स्त्री सती सा तु सोमसूनोः बुधस्याश्रमसमीपे बभ्राम ॥
verses.rom: punashcha ishvarakopat stri sati sa tu somasunoh budhasyashramasamipe babhrama ||

verses.sa: सानुरागाच्च तस्यां बुधः पुरूरवसम् आत्मजम् उत्पादयामास ॥
verses.rom: sanuragachcha tasyam budhah pururavasam atmajam utpadayamasa ||

verses.sa: जातेऽपि तस्मिन् अमिततेजोभिः परमर्षिभिः इष्टिमय ऋङ्मयो यजुर्मयः साममयोऽथर्वणमयः सर्ववेदमयो मनोमयो ज्ञानमयो न किञ्चिन्मयोऽन्नमयो भगवान् यज्ञपुरुषस्वरूपी सुद्युम्नस्य पुंस्त्वमभिलषद्भिर्यथावदिष्टः तत्प्रसादात् इला पुनरपि सुद्युम्नोऽभवत् ॥
verses.rom: jate'pi tasmin amitatejobhih paramarshibhih ishtimaya rinmayo yajurmayah samamayo'tharvanamayah sarvavedamayo manomayo jnanamayo na kinchinmayo'nnamayo bhagavan yajnapurushasvarupi sudyumnasya pumstvamabhilashadbhiryathavadishtah tatprasadat ila punarapi sudyumno'bhavat ||

verses.sa: तस्यापि उत्कल-गयत्-विनतसंज्ञाः त्रयः पुत्रा बभूवुः ॥
सुद्युम्नस्तु स्त्रीपूर्वकत्वात् राज्यभागं न लेभे ॥
तत्पित्रा तु वसिष्ठवचनात् प्रतिष्ठानं नाम नगरं सुद्युम्नाय दत्तं तच्चासौ पुरूरवसे प्रादात् ॥
verses.rom: tatpitra tu vasishthavachanat pratishthanam nama nagaram sudyumnaya dattam tachchasau pururavase pradat ||

verses.sa: तदन्वयाश्च क्षत्त्रियास्सर्वे दिक्षु अभवन् । पृषध्रस्तु मनुपुत्रो गुरुगोवधात् शूद्रत्वम् अगमत् ॥
verses.rom: tadanvayashcha kshattriyassarve dikshu abhavan | prishadhrastu manuputro gurugovadhat shudratvam agamat ||

verses.sa: मनोः पुत्रः करूषः, करूषात् कारूषाः क्षत्रिया महाबलपराक्रमा बभूवुः ॥
verses.rom: manoh putrah karushah, karushat karushah kshatriya mahabalaparakrama babhuvuh ||

verses.sa: दिष्टपुत्रस्तु नाभागो वैश्यतामगमत् तस्मात् बलन्धनः पुत्रोऽभवत् ॥
verses.rom: dishtaputrastu nabhago vaishyatamagamat tasmat balandhanah putro'bhavat ||

verses.sa: बलन्धनात् वत्सप्रीतिः उदारकीर्त्तिः ॥
वत्सप्रीतेः प्रांशुरभवत् ॥
प्रजापतिश्च प्रांशोरेकोऽभवत् ॥
ततश्च खनित्रः ॥
तस्माच्चक्षुषः ॥
चक्षुषाच्च अतिबलपराक्रमो विंशोऽभवत् ॥
ततो विविंशकः ॥
तस्माच्च खनिनेत्रः ॥
ततश्चातिविभूतिः ॥
अतिविभूतेः अतिबलपराक्रमः करन्धमः पुत्रोऽभवत् ॥
तस्मादपि अविक्षित् ॥

अविक्षितोऽपि अतिबलपराक्रमः पुत्रो मरुत्तो नामा अभवत् ।
यस्य इमौ अद्यापि श्लोकौ गीयेत् ॥
verses.rom:
avikshito'pi atibalaparakramah putro marutto nama abhavat |
yasya imau adyapi shlokau giyet ||

verses.sa:
मरुत्तस्य यथा यज्ञस्तथा कस्याभवद्भुवि ।
सर्वं हिरण्मयं यस्य यज्ञवस्त्वतिशोभनम् ॥
verses.rom:
maruttasya yatha yajnastatha kasyabhavadbhuvi |
sarvam hiranmayam yasya yajnavastvatishobhanam ||

verses.sa:
अमाद्यदिन्द्रस्सोमेन दक्षिणाभिर्द्विजातयः ।
मरुतः परिवेष्टारस्सदस्याश्च दिवौकसः ॥
स मरुत्तश्चक्रवर्त्ती नरिष्यन्तनामानं पुत्रमवाप ॥
तस्माच्च दमः ॥
दमस्य पुत्रो राजवर्द्धनो जज्ञे ॥
राजवर्द्धनात् सुवृद्धिः ॥
सुवृद्धेः केवलः ॥
केवलात् सुधृतिरभूत् ॥
ततश्च नरः ॥
तस्माच्चन्द्रः ॥
ततः केवलोऽभूत् ॥
केवलाद्बन्धुमान् ॥
बन्धुमतो वेगवान् ॥
वेगवतो बुधः ॥
ततश्च तृणबिन्दुः ॥
तस्याप्येका कन्या इलविला नाम ॥
ततश्चालम्बुषा नाम वराप्सरास्तृणबिन्दुं भेजे ॥
तस्यामप्यस्य विशालो जज्ञे यः पुरीं विशालं निर्ममे ॥
verses.rom: tasyamapyasya vishalo jajne yah purim vishalam nirmame ||

verses.sa: हेमचन्द्रश्च विशालस्य पुत्रोऽभवत् ॥
ततश्चन्द्रः ॥
तत्तनयो धूम्राक्षः ॥
तस्यापि सृञ्जयोऽभूत् ॥
सृञ्जयात् सहदेवः ॥
ततश्च कृशाश्वो नाम पुत्रोऽभवत् ॥
सोमदत्तः कृशाश्वाज्जज्ञे योऽश्वमेधानां शतमाजहार ॥
तत्पुत्रो जनमेजयः ॥
जनमेजयात् सुमतिः ॥
एते वैशालिका भूभृतः ॥
श्लोकोऽप्यत्र गीयते ॥

तृणबिन्दोः प्रसादेन सर्वे वैशालिका नृपाः ।
दीर्घायुषो महात्मानो वीर्यवन्तोऽतिधार्मिकाः ॥
verses.rom:
trinabindoh prasadena sarve vaishalika nripah |
dirghayusho mahatmano viryavanto'tidharmikah ||

verses.sa: शर्यातेः कन्या सुकन्या नामाभवत् यामुपयेमे च्यवनः ॥
verses.rom: sharyateh kanya sukanya namabhavat yamupayeme chyavanah ||

verses.sa: आनर्तनामा परमधार्मिकः शर्यातिपुत्रोऽभवत् ॥
आनर्तस्यापि रेवतनामा पुत्रो जज्ञे योऽसौ आनर्तविषयं बुभुजे पुरीं च कुशस्थलीमध्युवास ॥
verses.rom: anartasyapi revatanama putro jajne yo'sau anartavishayam bubhuje purim cha kushasthalimadhyuvasa ||

verses.sa: रेवतस्यापि रैवतः पुत्रः ककुद्मिनामा धर्मात्मा भ्रातृशतस्य ज्योष्ठोऽभवत् ॥
verses.rom: revatasyapi raivatah putrah kakudminama dharmatma bhratrishatasya jyoshtho'bhavat ||

verses.sa: तस्य रेवती नाम कन्याभवत् ॥
स तामादाय कस्येयमर्हतीति भगवन्तमब्जयोनिं प्रष्टुं ब्रह्मलोकं जगाम ॥
verses.rom: sa tamadaya kasyeyamarhatiti bhagavantamabjayonim prashtum brahmalokam jagama ||

verses.sa: तावच्च ब्रह्मणोऽन्तिके हाहाहूहूसंज्ञाभ्यां गन्धर्वाभ्यामतितानं नाम दिव्यं गान्धर्वमगीयत ॥
verses.rom: tavachcha brahmano'ntike hahahuhusamjnabhyam gandharvabhyamatitanam nama divyam gandharvamagiyata ||

verses.sa: तच्च त्रिमार्गपरिवृत्तैरनेकयुगपरिवृत्तिं तिष्ठन्नपि रैवतः शृण्वन् मुहूर्तमिव मेने ॥
verses.rom: tachcha trimargaparivrittairanekayugaparivrittim tishthannapi raivatah shrinvan muhurtamiva mene ||

verses.sa: गीतावसाने च भगवन्तमब्जयोनिं प्रणम्य रैवतः कन्यायोग्यं वरमपृच्छत् ॥
verses.rom: gitavasane cha bhagavantamabjayonim pranamya raivatah kanyayogyam varamaprichchhat ||

verses.sa: ततश्चासौ भगवानकथयत् कथय योऽभिमतस्ते वर इति ॥
verses.rom: tatashchasau bhagavanakathayat kathaya yo'bhimataste vara iti ||

verses.sa:
पुनश्च प्रणम्य भगवते तस्मै यथाभिमतानात्मनस्स वरान् कथयामास ।
क एषां भगवतोऽभिमत इति यस्मै कन्यामिमां प्रयच्छामीति ॥
verses.rom:
punashcha pranamya bhagavate tasmai yathabhimatanatmanassa varan kathayamasa |
ka esham bhagavato'bhimata iti yasmai kanyamimam prayachchhamiti ||

verses.sa: ततः किञ्चिदवनतशिराः सस्मितं भगवानब्जयोनिराह ॥
य एते भवतोऽभिमता नैतेषां साम्प्रतं पुत्रपौत्रापत्यापत्यसन्तति अस्त्यवनीतले ॥
verses.rom: ya ete bhavato'bhimata naitesham sampratam putrapautrapatyapatyasantati astyavanitale ||

verses.sa: बहूनि तवात्रैव गान्धर्वं शृण्वतश्चतुर्यगान्यतीतानि ॥
साम्प्रतं महीतलेऽष्टाविंशतितममनोश्चतुर्युगमतीतप्रायं वर्तते ॥
आसन्नो हि कलिः ॥
अन्यस्मै कन्यारत्नमिदं भवतैकाकिनाभिमताय देयम् ॥
भवतोऽपि पुत्र-मित्र-कलत्र-मन्त्रि-भृत्य-बन्धु-बल-कोशादयः समस्ताः कालेनैतेन अत्यन्तमतीताः ॥
ततः पुनरप्युत्पन्नसाध्वसो राजा भगवन्तं प्रणम्य पप्रच्छ ॥
verses.rom: tatah punarapyutpannasadhvaso raja bhagavantam pranamya paprachchha ||

verses.sa: भगवन्नेवमवस्थिते मयेयं कस्मै देयेति ॥
ततस्स भगवान् किञ्चिदवनम्रकन्धरः कृताञ्जलिर्भूत्वा सर्वलोकगुरुरम्भोजयोनिराह ॥

ब्रह्मोवाच
न ह्यादिमध्यान्तमजस्य यस्य विद्मो वयं सर्वमयस्य धातुः ।
न च स्वरूपं न परं स्वभावं न चैव सारं परमेश्वरस्य ॥
verses.rom:
brahmovacha
na hyadimadhyantamajasya yasya vidmo vayam sarvamayasya dhatuh |
na cha svarupam na param svabhavam na chaiva saram parameshvarasya ||

verses.sa:
कलामुहूर्तादिमयश्च कालो न यद्विभूतेः परिणामहेतुः ।
अजन्मनाशस्य सदैकमूर्तेरनामरूपस्य सनातनस्य ॥
verses.rom:
kalamuhurtadimayashcha kalo na yadvibhuteh parinamahetuh |
ajanmanashasya sadaikamurteranamarupasya sanatanasya ||

verses.sa:
यस्य प्रसादादहमच्युतस्य भूतः प्रजासृष्टिकरोऽन्तकारी ।
क्रोधाच्च रुद्रः स्थितिहेतुभूतो यस्माच्च मध्ये पुरुषः परस्मात् ॥
verses.rom:
yasya prasadadahamachyutasya bhutah prajasrishtikaro'ntakari |
krodhachcha rudrah sthitihetubhuto yasmachcha madhye purushah parasmat ||

verses.sa:
तद्रूपमास्थाय सृजत्यजो यः स्थितौ च योऽसौ पुरुषस्वरूपी ।
रुद्रस्वरूपेण च योऽत्ति विश्वं धत्ते तथानन्तवपुस्समस्तम् ॥
verses.rom:
tadrupamasthaya srijatyajo yah sthitau cha yo'sau purushasvarupi |
rudrasvarupena cha yo'tti vishvam dhatte tathanantavapussamastam ||

verses.sa:
पाकाय योऽग्नित्वमुपैति लोकान् बिभर्ति पृथ्वीवपुरव्ययात्मा ।
शक्रादिरूपी परिपाति विश्वमर्केन्दुरूपश्च तमो हिनस्ति ॥
verses.rom:
pakaya yo'gnitvamupaiti lokan bibharti prithvivapuravyayatma |
shakradirupi paripati vishvamarkendurupashcha tamo hinasti ||

verses.sa:
करोति चेष्टाश्श्वसनस्वरूपी लोकस्य तृप्तिं च जलान्नरूपी ।
ददाति विश्वस्थितिसंस्थितस्तु सर्वावकाशं च नभस्स्वरूपी ॥
verses.rom:
karoti cheshtashshvasanasvarupi lokasya triptim cha jalannarupi |
dadati vishvasthitisamsthitastu sarvavakasham cha nabhassvarupi ||

verses.sa:
यस्सृज्यते सर्गकृदात्मनैव यः पाल्यते पालयिता च देवः ।
विश्वात्मकस्संह्रियतेऽन्तकारी पृथक् त्रयस्यास्य च योऽव्ययात्मा ॥
verses.rom:
yassrijyate sargakridatmanaiva yah palyate palayita cha devah |
vishvatmakassamhriyate'ntakari prithak trayasyasya cha yo'vyayatma ||

verses.sa:
यस्मिञ्जगद्यो जगदेतदाद्यो यश्चाश्रितोऽस्मिञ्जगति स्वयम्भूः ।
स सर्वभूतप्रभवो धरित्र्यां स्वांशेन विष्णुर्नृपतेऽवतीर्णः ॥
verses.rom:
yasminjagadyo jagadetadadyo yashchashrito'sminjagati svayambhuh |
sa sarvabhutaprabhavo dharitryam svamshena vishnurnripate'vatirnah ||

verses.sa:
कुशस्थली या तव भूप रम्या पुरी पुराभूदमरावतीव ।
सा द्वारका सम्प्रति तत्र चास्ते स केशवांशो बलदेवनामा ॥
verses.rom:
kushasthali ya tava bhupa ramya puri purabhudamaravativa |
sa dvaraka samprati tatra chaste sa keshavamsho baladevanama ||

verses.sa:
तस्मै त्वमेनां तनयां नरेन्द्र प्रयच्छ मायामनुजाय जायाम् ।
श्लाघ्यो वरोऽसौ तनया तवेयं स्त्रीरत्नभूता सदृशो हि योगः ॥
verses.rom:
tasmai tvamenam tanayam narendra prayachchha mayamanujaya jayam |
shlaghyo varo'sau tanaya taveyam striratnabhuta sadrisho hi yogah ||

verses.sa:
पराशर उवाच
इतीरितोऽसौ कमलोद्भवेन भुवं समासाद्य पतिः प्रजानाम् ।
ददर्श ह्रस्वान् पुरुषान् विरूपानल्पौजसस्स्वल्पविवेकवीर्यान् ॥
verses.rom:
parashara uvacha
itirito'sau kamalodbhavena bhuvam samasadya patih prajanam |
dadarsha hrasvan purushan virupanalpaujasassvalpavivekaviryan ||

verses.sa:
कुशस्थलीं तां च पुरीमुपेत्य दृष्ट्वान्यरूपां प्रददौ स कन्याम् ।
सीरायुधाय स्फटिकाचलाभवक्षःस्थलायातुलधीर्नरेन्द्रः ॥
verses.rom:
kushasthalim tam cha purimupetya drishtvanyarupam pradadau sa kanyam |
sirayudhaya sphatikachalabhavakshahsthalayatuladhirnarendrah ||

verses.sa:
उच्चप्रमाणामिति तामवेक्ष्य स्वलाङ्गलाग्रेण च तालकेतुः ।
विनम्रयामास ततश्च सापि बभूव सद्यो वनिता यथान्या ॥
verses.rom:
uchchapramanamiti tamavekshya svalangalagrena cha talaketuh |
vinamrayamasa tatashcha sapi babhuva sadyo vanita yathanya ||

verses.sa:
तां रेवतीं रैवतभूपकन्यां सीरायुधोऽसौ विधिनोपयेमे ।
दत्त्वाथ कन्यां स नृपो जगाम हेमालयं वै तपसे धृतात्मा ॥
verses.rom:
tam revatim raivatabhupakanyam sirayudho'sau vidhinopayeme |
dattvatha kanyam sa nripo jagama hemalayam vai tapase dhritatma ||

verses.sa:
॥ इति श्रीविष्णुमहापुराणे चतुर्थांशे प्रथमोऽध्यायः ॥
।

prose.en:
Maitreya said:—"O venerable sir, you have described to me the permanent and occasional observances to be observed by those pious individuals who are diligent in their devotions. You have also described to me the duties which appertain to several castes and several orders of men. I wish you to relate to me now the dynasties of the kings who have ruled over the earth".

Parāçara said:— Hear O Maitreya, I shall describe to you the family of Manu beginning with Brahmā and comprising a number of pious, high-minded and heroic princes; It is said, that never does his family become extinct who daily calls to his mind the family of Manu springing from Brahmā. Hear, therefore, O Maitreya, an account of the origin of his family, hearing which all sins shall be removed.

From the mundane egg originated Brahmā, who was Hiranyagarbha, the form of that supreme Brahmā which consists of Vishnu as identical with Rig, Yajur and Sama Vedas—the first, uncreated cause of all worlds. From the right thumb of Brahmā originated the Patriarch Daksha whose daughter was Aditi, who was the mother of the sun. From the sun sprang Manu whose sons were Ikshawaku, Nriga, Dwrishta, Saryati, Narishyanta, Pransu, Nabhaga, Nedishta, Karusha, and Prishadhra. Being desirous of having offspring formerly Manu celebrated a sacrifice in honour of Mitra and Varuna; but the ceremony being unsuccessful on account of some irregularity from the presiding priest a daughter Ilā was born. But by the mercy of the two deities however, her sex was changed and she became a man under the name of Sudyumna. And he again became a woman under an imprecation (from Siva) near the hermitage of Buddha, the son of the moon.

One day while she was walking near the hermitage of Buddha, he became attached to her and begot on her a son named Pururavas. After his birth, the noble Rishis, desiring to restore Sudyumna to his sex, prayed to the glorious Vishnu who is the essence of the four Vedas, of mind, of every thing and of nothing and who is the sacrificed male. By his mercy Ilā once more became Sudyumna, in which character he had three sons, Utkala, Gaya and Vinata.

On account of his having been formerly born a female he did not receive any portion of his paternal kingdom. His father however at the request of Vasistha conferred upon him the city of Pratishtā, and he gave it to Pururavas.

Of the other sons of Manu, Prishadhra, on account of the sin consequent upon slaying a cow, was degraded to the condition of a Sudra. From Karusha sprang the heroic persons named Kārushas. The son of Nedistha, named Nābhaga became a Vaiçya; his son was Bhalandana, whose son was the well-known Vatsapri; his son was Pransu, whose son was Prajani, whose son was Khanitra, whose son was the brave Chakshupa, whose son was Vinsa, whose son was Vivinsati, whose son was Khaninetra, whose son was the powerful, rich, and heroic Karandhama, whose son was Avikshit, whose son was the powerful Marutta, regarding whom this celebrated verse is recited—"Who else on this earth has been able to celebrate a sacrifice like one celebrated by Marutta?" All the implements and utensils were made of gold. Indra was intoxicated with the drinking of Soma juice and all the Brāhmans were greatly pleased on having liberal presents. In his sacrifice the winds were the guards and the other celestials were the courtiers. Marutta was a lord paramount; he had a son named Narishyanta; his son was Dama; his son was Rayavarddana; his son was Suddhriti; his son was Nara; his son was Kevala; his son was Banduhmat; his son was Vegavat; his son was Budha; his son was Trinavindu, who had a daughter under name of Ilavita. Being enamored of Trinavindhu, the nymph Alambushā bore him a son named Visāla by whom the city Vaisāli was founded.

Vinata had a son whose name was Hemchandra; his son was Suchandra; his son was Dhumraswa; his son was Srinjaya; his son was Sahadeva; his son was Krisaswa; his son was Somadatta, who performed ten times the sacrifice of a horse; his son was Janemajaya, whose son was Sunati. These kings are known as Vaisālas, of them it is said—"By the mercy of Trinavindhu all the kings of Vaisāli were long-lived, magnanimous and just and brave".

Saryati had a daughter named Sukanyā. Chyavana married her. He had a pious son named Anartta, who had a son called Revata who governed the country called after the name of his father Anartta and lived at the capital called Kusasthali. The son of this king was Raivata or Kakudmin, the eldest of a hundred bretheren. He had a daughter named Revati. He repaired with her to the region of Brahmā to consult with the god springing from lotus upon whom to confer her. When he reached there the Gandharvas, Haha and Huha, were singing before Brahmā and Raviata waited till they had finished. And the ages passed away during the performance seemed to him as a moment. When they had finished singing Raivata laid himself low before Brahmā and asked him about a fit bridegroom. Brahmā said—"Whom should you wish for a son-in-law?" And bowing again Raivata mentioned to him various persons whom he liked. Nodding his head smiling graciously Brahmā said to him—"Of those whom you have mentioned there is no trace of their family on earth Many ages have passed away whilst you were listening to the songs of Gandharvas. Now the twenty-eighth great age of the present Manu is well-nigh gone. Kali is fast approaching. You alone give away this jewel of a daughter to somebody; all thy friends, ministers, servants, wife, kinsmen, armies, wealth have along since been taken away by the hand of Time".

That king, being terrified again, said, bowing, to Brahmā "O lord, such being the circumstance, upon whom shall I confer this daughter?" Thereupon nodding, the preceptor of the seven worlds—the god, whose throne is lotus, said to the king, standing humbly before—"The being, whose beginning, middle or end we do not know, who exists in all, who is the creator, whose real and infinite nature and essence we do not know is (Vishnu). His power cannot be measured by time, consisting of moments and hours and years; he has no birth or death—all objects are his form—he is eternal—he has no form or name. By the mercy of that imperishable being I am the agent of creation—Rudra is the agent of destruction and Vishnu is the agent of preservation. He, assuming my form creates the universe; in his own essence he provides for its duration; in the form of Rudra he devours all things; and with the body of Ananta he upholds them, In the person of Indra and other celestials he protects mankind and as the sun and moon he dispels darkness. Assuming the nature of fire he bestows warmth and maturity, and in that of earth he nourishes all beings. In the shape of air he gives activity, in the shape of water he gives satisfaction and in the shape of sky he provides space for all objects. He, being creator, creates himself; he, being preserver, preserves himself; he, being destroyer, destroys his own universal form. He is imperishable; there is nothing distinct from him. In him is the world; he is the world; and he, the primeval self-born, is again present in the world. O king, the glorious Vishnu has incarnated a portion of himself on earth. O king, your picturesque city Kusasthali, like the city of Indra, is now called Dwārakā. There reigns a portion of Kesava in the person of Baladeva. O king, confer this daughter of thine upon him, who appears under the guise of a man. He is an excellent bridegroom for this gem of a daughter and she is a fit bride".

Parāçara said:—Being thus advised by the deity springing from lotus, the king returned to earth and beheld mankind, greatly reduced in size and vigour and weakened in intellect. Thereupon that king, having incomparable wisdom, repairing to his own city Kusathali which he saw greatly changed, gave his daughter to Baladeva whose breast was as fair and radiant as crystal. And beholding that damsel of excessive height the king, whose banner is a palm tree, shortened her with the end of his ploughshare. Being thus shortened she became like other women. Balarāma thus married duly Revali, the daughter of Raivata. And the king, too giving away daughter, retired to the mountain Himalaya and engaged in penances with a subdued mind.

verses.sa:
॥ अथ द्वितीयोऽध्यायः ॥
(इक्ष्वाकुवंशवर्णना सौभरिचरित्रञ्च)
श्रीपराशर उवाच
यावच्च ब्रह्मलोकात् सः ककुद्मी रैवतो नाभ्येति तावत् पुण्यजनसंज्ञा राक्षसाः ताम् अस्य पुरीं कुशस्थलीं निजघ्नुः ॥
verses.rom:
|| atha dvitiyo'dhyayah ||
(ikshvakuvamshavarnana saubharicharitrancha)
shriparashara uvacha
yavachcha brahmalokat sah kakudmi raivato nabhyeti tavat punyajanasamjna rakshasah tam asya purim kushasthalim nijaghnuh ||

verses.sa: तच्चास्य भ्रातृशतं पुण्यजनत्रासात् दिशो भेजे ॥
तदन्वयाश्च क्षत्रियाः सर्वदिक्षु अभवन् ॥
धृष्टस्यापि धार्ष्टकं क्षत्रमभवत् ॥
नाभागस्यात्मजो नाभागसंज्ञोऽभवत् ॥
तस्याप्यम्बरीषः ॥
अम्बरीषस्यापि विरूपोऽभवत् ॥
विरूपात् पृषदश्वो जज्ञे ॥
ततश्च रथीतरः ॥

अत्रायं श्लोकः –
एते क्षत्रप्रसूता वै पुनश्चाङ्गिरसाः स्मृताः ।
रथीतराणां प्रवराः क्षत्रोपेता द्विजातयः ॥
verses.rom:
atrayam shlokah –
ete kshatraprasuta vai punashchangirasah smritah |
rathitaranam pravarah kshatropeta dvijatayah ||

verses.sa: क्षुवतश्च मनोः इक्ष्वाकुः पुत्रो जज्ञे घ्राणतः ॥
verses.rom: kshuvatashcha manoh ikshvakuh putro jajne ghranatah ||

verses.sa: तस्य पुत्रशतप्रधाना विकुक्षिनिमिदण्डाख्याः त्रयः पुत्रा बभूवुः ॥
verses.rom: tasya putrashatapradhana vikukshinimidandakhyah trayah putra babhuvuh ||

verses.sa: शकुनिप्रमुखाः पञ्चाशत् पुत्राः उत्तरापथरक्षितारो बभूवुः ॥
चत्वारिंशदष्टौ च दक्षिणापथभूपालाः ॥
स चेक्ष्वाकुः अष्टकायाः श्राद्धम् उत्पाद्य श्राद्धार्हं मांसमानयेति विकुक्षिम् आज्ञापयामास ॥
verses.rom: sa chekshvakuh ashtakayah shraddham utpadya shraddharham mamsamanayeti vikukshim ajnapayamasa ||

verses.sa: स तथेति गृहीताज्ञो विधृतशरासनो वनमभ्येत्य, अनेकशो मृगान् हत्वा, श्रान्तः अतिक्षुत्परीतो विकुक्षिः एकं शशम् अभक्षयत् । शेषं च मांसमानीय पित्रे निवेदयामास ॥
verses.rom: sa tatheti grihitajno vidhritasharasano vanamabhyetya, anekasho mrigan hatva, shrantah atikshutparito vikukshih ekam shasham abhakshayat | shesham cha mamsamaniya pitre nivedayamasa ||

verses.sa: इक्ष्वाकुकुलाचार्यो वसिष्ठस्तत्प्रोक्षणाय चोदितः प्राह - “अलमनेन अमेध्येन आमिषेण । दुरात्मना तव पुत्रेण एतन्मांसम् उपहतं यतोऽनेन शशो भक्षितः” ॥
verses.rom: ikshvakukulacharyo vasishthastatprokshanaya choditah praha - “alamanena amedhyena amishena | duratmana tava putrena etanmamsam upahatam yato'nena shasho bhakshitah” ||

verses.sa: ततश्चासौ विकुक्षिः गुरुणा एवम् उक्तः शशादसंज्ञाम् अवाप, पित्रा च परित्यक्तः ॥
verses.rom: tatashchasau vikukshih guruna evam uktah shashadasamjnam avapa, pitra cha parityaktah ||

verses.sa: पितर्युपरते च असौ अखिलामेतां पृथ्वीं धर्मतः शशास ॥
verses.rom: pitaryuparate cha asau akhilametam prithvim dharmatah shashasa ||

verses.sa: शशादस्य तस्य पुरञ्जयो नाम पुत्रोऽभवत् ॥
तस्येदं चान्यत् ॥
पुरा हि त्रेतायां देवासुरयुद्धम् अतिभीषणम् अभवत् ॥
verses.rom: pura hi tretayam devasurayuddham atibhishanam abhavat ||

verses.sa: प्रसन्नश्च देवानाम् अनादिनिधनः अखिलजगत्परायणो नारायणः प्राह ॥
verses.rom: prasannashcha devanam anadinidhanah akhilajagatparayano narayanah praha ||

verses.sa: “ज्ञातमेतन्मया युष्माभिः यदभिलषितं तदर्थमिदं श्रूयताम् ॥
पुरञ्जयो नाम राजर्षेः शशादस्य तनयः क्षत्रियवरो यः, तस्य शरीरेऽहमंशेन स्वयमेव अवतीर्य, तान् अशेषान् असुरान् निहनिष्यामि, तद्भवद्भिः पुरञ्जयः असुरवधार्थम् उद्योगं कार्यताम्” इति ॥
verses.rom: puranjayo nama rajarsheh shashadasya tanayah kshatriyavaro yah, tasya sharire'hamamshena svayameva avatirya, tan asheshan asuran nihanishyami, tadbhavadbhih puranjayah asuravadhartham udyogam karyatam” iti ||

verses.sa: एतच्च श्रुत्वा प्रणम्य भगवन्तं विष्णुममराः पुरञ्जयसकाशम् आजमुः ऊचुश्चैनम् ॥
verses.rom: etachcha shrutva pranamya bhagavantam vishnumamarah puranjayasakasham ajamuh uchushchainam ||

verses.sa: “भो भो क्षत्रियवर्य अस्माभिः अभ्यर्थितेन भवता अस्माकम् अरातिवधोद्यतानां कर्तव्यं साहाय्यम् इच्छामः तद्भवता अस्माकम् अभ्यागतानां प्रणयभङ्गो न कार्य” इत्युक्तः पुरञ्जयः प्राह ॥
verses.rom: “bho bho kshatriyavarya asmabhih abhyarthitena bhavata asmakam arativadhodyatanam kartavyam sahayyam ichchhamah tadbhavata asmakam abhyagatanam pranayabhango na karya” ityuktah puranjayah praha ||

verses.sa: “त्रैलोक्यनाथो योऽयं युष्माकमिन्द्रः शतक्रतुः अस्य यदि अहं स्कन्धाधिरूढो युष्माकम् अरातिभिः सह योत्स्ये तदहं भवतां सहायः स्याम” ॥
verses.rom: “trailokyanatho yo'yam yushmakamindrah shatakratuh asya yadi aham skandhadhirudho yushmakam aratibhih saha yotsye tadaham bhavatam sahayah syama” ||

verses.sa: इत्याकर्ण्य समस्तदेवैः इन्द्रेण च बाढमित्येवं समन्वीप्सितम् ॥
verses.rom: ityakarnya samastadevaih indrena cha badhamityevam samanvipsitam ||

verses.sa: ततश्च शतक्रतोः वृषरूपधारिणः ककुदि स्थितः अतिरोषसमन्वितो भगवतः चराचरगुरोः अच्युतस्य तेजसा आप्यायितो देवासुरसङ्ग्रामे समस्तानेव असुरान् निजघान ॥
verses.rom: tatashcha shatakratoh vrisharupadharinah kakudi sthitah atiroshasamanvito bhagavatah characharaguroh achyutasya tejasa apyayito devasurasangrame samastaneva asuran nijaghana ||

verses.sa: यतश्च वृषभककुदि स्थितेन राज्ञा दैतेयबलं निषूदितम् अतश्चासौ ककुत्स्थसंज्ञाम् अवाप ॥
verses.rom: yatashcha vrishabhakakudi sthitena rajna daiteyabalam nishuditam atashchasau kakutsthasamjnam avapa ||

verses.sa: ककुत्स्थस्याप्यनेनाः पुत्रोऽभवत् ॥
पृथुरनेनसः ॥
पृथोर्विष्टराश्वः ॥
तस्यापि चान्द्रो युवनाश्वः ॥
चान्द्रस्य तस्य युवनाश्वस्य शावस्तः यः पुरीं शावस्तीं निवेशयामास ॥
verses.rom: chandrasya tasya yuvanashvasya shavastah yah purim shavastim niveshayamasa ||

verses.sa: शावस्तस्य बृहदश्वः ॥
तस्यापि कुवलयाश्वः ॥
योऽसौ उदकस्य महर्षेः अपकारिणं धुन्धुनामानम् असुरं वैष्णवेन तेजसा आप्यायितः पुत्रसहस्रैः एकविंशद्भिः परिवृतो जघान धुन्धुमारसंज्ञाम् अवाप ॥
verses.rom: yo'sau udakasya maharsheh apakarinam dhundhunamanam asuram vaishnavena tejasa apyayitah putrasahasraih ekavimshadbhih parivrito jaghana dhundhumarasamjnam avapa ||

verses.sa: तस्य च तनयास्समस्ता एव धुन्धुमुखनिःश्वासाग्निना विप्लुष्टा विनेशुः ॥
verses.rom: tasya cha tanayassamasta eva dhundhumukhanihshvasagnina viplushta vineshuh ||

verses.sa: दृढाश्वचन्द्राश्वकपिलाश्वाश्च त्रयः केवलं शेषिताः ॥
दृढाश्वात् हर्यश्वः ॥
तस्माच्च निकुम्भः ॥
निकुम्भस्यामिताश्वः ॥
ततश्च कृशाश्वः ॥
तस्माच्च प्रसेनजित् ॥
प्रसेनजितो युवनाश्वोऽभवत् ॥
तस्य च अपुत्रस्य अतिनिर्वेदात् मुनीनाम् आश्रममण्डले निवसतो दयालुभिः मुनिभिः अपत्योत्पादनाय इष्टिः कृता ॥
verses.rom: tasya cha aputrasya atinirvedat muninam ashramamandale nivasato dayalubhih munibhih apatyotpadanaya ishtih krita ||

verses.sa: तस्यां च मध्यरात्रौ निवृत्तायां मन्त्रपूतजलपूर्णं कलशं वेदिमध्ये निवेश्य ते मुनयः सुषुपुः ॥
verses.rom: tasyam cha madhyaratrau nivrittayam mantraputajalapurnam kalasham vedimadhye niveshya te munayah sushupuh ||

verses.sa: सुप्तेषु तेषु अतीव तृट्परीतः स भूपालः तमाश्रमं विवेश ॥
verses.rom: supteshu teshu ativa tritparitah sa bhupalah tamashramam vivesha ||

verses.sa: सुप्तांश्च तान् ऋषीन् नैव उत्थापयामास ॥
तच्च कलशम् अपरिमेयमाहात्म्यमन्त्रपूतं पपौ ॥
प्रबुद्धाश्च ऋषयः पप्रच्छुः “केनैतन्मन्त्रपूतं वारि पीतम् ॥
अत्र हि राज्ञो युवनाश्वस्य पत्नी महाबलपराक्रमं पुत्रं जनयिष्यति” । इत्याकर्ण्य स राजा अजानता मया पीतमित्याह ॥
verses.rom: atra hi rajno yuvanashvasya patni mahabalaparakramam putram janayishyati” | ityakarnya sa raja ajanata maya pitamityaha ||

verses.sa: गर्भश्च युवनाश्वस्योदरे अभवत् क्रमेण च ववृधे ॥
verses.rom: garbhashcha yuvanashvasyodare abhavat kramena cha vavridhe ||

verses.sa: प्राप्तसमयश्च दक्षिणं कुक्षिमवनिपतेर्निर्भिद्य निश्चक्राम ॥
स चासौ राजा ममार ॥
जातो नामैष कं धास्यतीति ते मुनयः प्रोचुः ॥
verses.rom: jato namaisha kam dhasyatiti te munayah prochuh ||

verses.sa: अथागत्य देवराजोऽब्रवीत् मामयं धास्यतीति ॥

ततो मान्धातृनामा सोऽभवत् ।
वक्त्रे चास्य प्रदेशिनी देवेन्द्रेण न्यस्ता तां पपौ ॥
verses.rom:
tato mandhatrinama so'bhavat |
vaktre chasya pradeshini devendrena nyasta tam papau ||

verses.sa: तां चामृतस्राविणीम् आस्वाद्य अह्नैव स व्यवर्धत ॥
verses.rom: tam chamritasravinim asvadya ahnaiva sa vyavardhata ||

verses.sa: ततस्तु मान्धाता चक्रवर्ती सप्तद्वीपां महीं बुभुजे ॥
verses.rom: tatastu mandhata chakravarti saptadvipam mahim bubhuje ||

verses.sa: तत्रायं श्लोकः ॥

यावत्सूर्य उदेत्यस्तं यावच्च प्रतितिष्ठति ।
सर्वं तद्यौवनाश्वस्य मान्धातुः क्षेत्रमुच्यते ॥
verses.rom:
yavatsurya udetyastam yavachcha pratitishthati |
sarvam tadyauvanashvasya mandhatuh kshetramuchyate ||

verses.sa: मान्धाता शतबिन्दोर्दुहितरं बिन्दुमतीम् उपयेमे ॥
पुरुकुत्सम् अम्बरीषं मुचुकुन्दं च तस्यां पुत्रत्रयम् उत्पादयामास ॥
verses.rom: purukutsam ambarisham muchukundam cha tasyam putratrayam utpadayamasa ||

verses.sa: पञ्चाशद्दुहितरः तस्यामेव तस्य नृपतेः बभूवुः ॥
तस्मिन्नन्तरे बह्वृचश्च सौभरिर्नाम महर्षिः अन्तर्जले द्वादशाब्दं कालमुवास ॥
verses.rom: tasminnantare bahvrichashcha saubharirnama maharshih antarjale dvadashabdam kalamuvasa ||

verses.sa: तत्र चान्तर्जले सम्मदो नाम अतिबहुप्रजः अतिमात्रप्रमाणः मीनाधिपतिः आसीत् ॥
verses.rom: tatra chantarjale sammado nama atibahuprajah atimatrapramanah minadhipatih asit ||

verses.sa: तस्य च पुत्रपौत्रदौहित्राः पृष्ठतोऽग्रतः पार्श्वयोः पक्षपुच्छशिरसां चोपरि भ्रमन्तः तेनैव सदा अहर्निशम् अतिनिर्वृत्ता रेमिरे ॥
verses.rom: tasya cha putrapautradauhitrah prishthato'gratah parshvayoh pakshapuchchhashirasam chopari bhramantah tenaiva sada aharnisham atinirvritta remire ||

verses.sa: स च अपत्य-स्पर्श-उपचीयमान-प्रहर्ष-प्रकर्षो बहुप्रकारं तस्य ऋषेः पश्यतः तैः आत्मजपुत्रपौत्रदौहित्रादिभिः सह अनुदिनं सुतरां रेमे ॥
verses.rom: sa cha apatya-sparsha-upachiyamana-praharsha-prakarsho bahuprakaram tasya risheh pashyatah taih atmajaputrapautradauhitradibhih saha anudinam sutaram reme ||

verses.sa: “अहो धन्योऽयमीदृशम् अनभिमतं योन्यन्तरम् अवाप्य एभिः आत्मजपुत्रपौत्रदौहित्रादिभिः सह रममाणोऽतीव अस्माकं स्पृहाम् उत्पादयति ॥
verses.rom: “aho dhanyo'yamidrisham anabhimatam yonyantaram avapya ebhih atmajaputrapautradauhitradibhih saha ramamano'tiva asmakam spriham utpadayati ||

verses.sa: वयमप्येवं पुत्रादिभिस्सह ललितं रंस्यामहे” इत्येवमभिकाङ्क्षन् स तस्मादन्तर्जलान्निष्क्रम्य सन्तानाय निवेष्टुकामः कन्यार्थं मान्धातारं राजानमगच्छत् ॥
verses.rom: vayamapyevam putradibhissaha lalitam ramsyamahe” ityevamabhikankshan sa tasmadantarjalannishkramya santanaya niveshtukamah kanyartham mandhataram rajanamagachchhat ||

verses.sa: आगमनश्रवणसमनन्तरं चोत्थाय तेन राज्ञा सम्यगर्घ्यादिना सम्पूजितः कृतासनपरिग्रहः सौभरिरुवाच राजानम् ॥
verses.rom: agamanashravanasamanantaram chotthaya tena rajna samyagarghyadina sampujitah kritasanaparigrahah saubhariruvacha rajanam ||

verses.sa:
सौभरिरुवाच
निवेष्टुकामोऽस्मि नरेन्द्र कन्यां प्रयच्छ मे मा प्रणयं विभाङ्क्षीः ।
न ह्यर्थिनः कार्यवशादुपेताः ककुत्स्थवंशे विमुखाः प्रयान्ति ॥
verses.rom:
saubhariruvacha
niveshtukamo'smi narendra kanyam prayachchha me ma pranayam vibhankshih |
na hyarthinah karyavashadupetah kakutsthavamshe vimukhah prayanti ||

verses.sa:
अन्येऽपि सन्त्येव नृपाः पृथिव्यां मान्धातरेषां तनयाः प्रसूताः ।
किं त्वर्थिनामर्थितदानदीक्षाकृतव्रतं श्लाघ्यमिदं कुलं ते ॥
verses.rom:
anye'pi santyeva nripah prithivyam mandhataresham tanayah prasutah |
kim tvarthinamarthitadanadikshakritavratam shlaghyamidam kulam te ||

verses.sa:
शतार्धसंख्यास्तव सन्ति कन्यास्तासां ममैकां नृपते प्रयच्छ ।
यत्प्रार्थनाभङ्गभयाद्बिभेमि तस्मादहं राजवरातिदुःखात् ॥
verses.rom:
shatardhasamkhyastava santi kanyastasam mamaikam nripate prayachchha |
yatprarthanabhangabhayadbibhemi tasmadaham rajavaratiduhkhat ||

verses.sa:
श्रीपराशर उवाच ।
इति ऋषिवचनमाकर्ण्य स राजा जराजर्जरितदेहम् ऋषिमालोक्य प्रत्याख्यानकातरः तस्माच्च शापभीतो बिभ्यत्किञ्चिदधोमुखः चिरं दध्यौ च ॥
verses.rom:
shriparashara uvacha |
iti rishivachanamakarnya sa raja jarajarjaritadeham rishimalokya pratyakhyanakatarah tasmachcha shapabhito bibhyatkinchidadhomukhah chiram dadhyau cha ||

verses.sa:
सौभरिरुवाच
नरेन्द्र कस्मात्समुपैषि चिन्तामसह्यमुक्तं न मयात्र किञ्चित् ।
यावश्यदेया तनया तयैव कृतार्थता नो यदि किं न लब्धा ॥
verses.rom:
saubhariruvacha
narendra kasmatsamupaishi chintamasahyamuktam na mayatra kinchit |
yavashyadeya tanaya tayaiva kritarthata no yadi kim na labdha ||

verses.sa:
श्रीपराशर उवाच
अथ तस्य भगवतः शापभीतः सप्रश्रयः तमुवाच असौ राजा ॥
verses.rom:
shriparashara uvacha
atha tasya bhagavatah shapabhitah saprashrayah tamuvacha asau raja ||

verses.sa:
राजोवाच
“भगवन् अस्मत्कुलस्थितिरियं, य एव कन्याया अभिरुचितोऽभिजनवान् वरः, तस्मै कन्यां प्रदीयते । भगवद्याच्ञा चास्मन्मनोरथानाम् अपि अतिगोचरवर्त्तिनी कथमप्येषा सञ्जाता । तदेवमुपस्थिते न विद्मः किं कुर्म इत्येतन्मया चिन्त्यत” इत्यभिहिते च तेन भूभुजा मुनिरचिन्तयत् ॥
verses.rom:
rajovacha
“bhagavan asmatkulasthitiriyam, ya eva kanyaya abhiruchito'bhijanavan varah, tasmai kanyam pradiyate | bhagavadyachna chasmanmanorathanam api atigocharavarttini kathamapyesha sanjata | tadevamupasthite na vidmah kim kurma ityetanmaya chintyata” ityabhihite cha tena bhubhuja munirachintayat ||

verses.sa: “अयम् अन्यः अस्मत्प्रत्याख्यानोपायो – वृद्धोऽयम् अनभिमतः स्त्रीणां किमुत कन्याकानाम् इत्यमुना सञ्चिन्त्य एतदभिहितम् । एवमस्तु तथा करिष्यामि” इति सञ्चिन्त्य मान्धातारमुवाच ॥
verses.rom: “ayam anyah asmatpratyakhyanopayo – vriddho'yam anabhimatah strinam kimuta kanyakanam ityamuna sanchintya etadabhihitam | evamastu tatha karishyami” iti sanchintya mandhataramuvacha ||

verses.sa: “यद्येवं तदादिश्यताम् अस्माकं प्रवेशाय कन्यान्तःपुरवर्षवरः । यदि कन्यैव काचिन्मामभिलषति तदाहं दारसङ्ग्रहं करिष्यामि । अन्यथा चेत् तदलम् अस्माकम् एतेन अतीतकालारम्भणेन” इत्युक्त्वा विरराम ॥
verses.rom: “yadyevam tadadishyatam asmakam praveshaya kanyantahpuravarshavarah | yadi kanyaiva kachinmamabhilashati tadaham darasangraham karishyami | anyatha chet tadalam asmakam etena atitakalarambhanena” ityuktva virarama ||

verses.sa: ततश्च मान्धात्रा मुनिशापशङ्कितेन कन्यान्तःपुरवर्षधरः समाज्ञप्तः ॥
तेन सह कन्यान्तःपुरं प्रविशन्नेव भगवान् अखिलसिद्धगन्धर्वेभ्यः अतिशयेन कमनीयं रूपमकरोत् ॥
verses.rom: tena saha kanyantahpuram pravishanneva bhagavan akhilasiddhagandharvebhyah atishayena kamaniyam rupamakarot ||

verses.sa: प्रवेश्य च तमृषिम् अन्तःपुरे वर्षवरः ताः कन्याः प्राह ॥
verses.rom: praveshya cha tamrishim antahpure varshavarah tah kanyah praha ||

verses.sa: भवतीनां जनयिता महाराजः समाज्ञापयति ॥
“अयमस्मान् ब्रह्मर्षिः कन्यार्थं समभ्यागतः ॥

मया चास्य प्रतिज्ञातं – यद्यस्मत्कन्या या काचिद्भगवन्तं वरयति, तत्कन्याच्छन्दे नाहं परिपन्थानं करिष्यामि” । इत्याकर्ण्य सर्वा एव ताः कन्याः सानुरागाः सप्रमदाः करेणव इव इभयूथपतिं तमृषिम् अहमहमिकया वरयाम्बभूवुः ऊचुश्च ॥
verses.rom: maya chasya pratijnatam – yadyasmatkanya ya kachidbhagavantam varayati, tatkanyachchhande naham paripanthanam karishyami” | ityakarnya sarva eva tah kanyah sanuragah sapramadah karenava iva ibhayuthapatim tamrishim ahamahamikaya varayambabhuvuh uchushcha ||

verses.sa:
अलं भगिन्योऽहमिमं वृणोमि वृणोम्यहं नैष तवानुरूपः ।
ममैष भर्त्ता विधिनैव सृष्टस्सृष्टाहमस्योपशमं प्रयाहि ॥
verses.rom:
alam bhaginyo'hamimam vrinomi vrinomyaham naisha tavanurupah |
mamaisha bhartta vidhinaiva srishtassrishtahamasyopashamam prayahi ||

verses.sa:
वृतो मयायं प्रथमं मयायं गृहं विशन्नेव विहन्यसे किम् ।
मया मयेति क्षितिपात्मजानां तदर्थमत्यर्थकलिर्बभूव ॥
verses.rom:
vrito mayayam prathamam mayayam griham vishanneva vihanyase kim |
maya mayeti kshitipatmajanam tadarthamatyarthakalirbabhuva ||

verses.sa:
यदा मुनिस्ताभिरतीव हार्दाद्वृतस्स कन्याभिरनिन्द्यकीर्तिः ।
तदा स कन्याधिकृतो नृपाय यथावदाचष्ट विनम्रमूर्त्तिः ॥
verses.rom:
yada munistabhirativa hardadvritassa kanyabhiranindyakirtih |
tada sa kanyadhikrito nripaya yathavadachashta vinamramurttih ||

verses.sa:
श्रीपराशर उवाच
तदवगमात् “किमेतत्, कथमेतत्, किं किं करोमि, किं मयाभिहितम्” इत्याकुलमतिः अनिच्छन्नपि कथमपि राजा अनुमेने ॥
verses.rom:
shriparashara uvacha
tadavagamat “kimetat, kathametat, kim kim karomi, kim mayabhihitam” ityakulamatih anichchhannapi kathamapi raja anumene ||

verses.sa: कृतानुरूपविवाहश्च महर्षिः सकला एव ताः कन्याः स्वमाश्रमम् अनयत् ॥
verses.rom: kritanurupavivahashcha maharshih sakala eva tah kanyah svamashramam anayat ||

verses.sa: तत्र च अशेषशिल्पकल्पप्रणेतारं धातारमिवान्यं विश्वकर्माणम् आहूय सकलकन्यानाम् एकैकस्याः प्रोत्फुल्लपङ्कजाः कूजत्-कलहंस-कारण्डवादि-विहङ्गम-अभिराम-जलाशयाः सोपधानाः सावकाशाः साधुशय्यापरिच्छदाः प्रासादाः क्रियन्ताम् इत्यादिदेश ॥
verses.rom: tatra cha asheshashilpakalpapranetaram dhataramivanyam vishvakarmanam ahuya sakalakanyanam ekaikasyah protphullapankajah kujat-kalahamsa-karandavadi-vihangama-abhirama-jalashayah sopadhanah savakashah sadhushayyaparichchhadah prasadah kriyantam ityadidesha ||

verses.sa: ततः परमर्षिणा सौभरिणाज्ञप्तः तेषु गृहेषु अनिवार्यानन्दनामा महानिधिः आसाञ्चक्रे ॥
verses.rom: tatah paramarshina saubharinajnaptah teshu griheshu anivaryanandanama mahanidhih asanchakre ||

verses.sa: ततः अनवरतेन भक्ष्य-भोज्य-लेह्यादि-उपभोगैः आगतानुगतभृत्यादीन् अहर्निशम् अशेषगृहेषु ताः क्षितीशदुहितरो भोजयामासुः ॥
verses.rom: tatah anavaratena bhakshya-bhojya-lehyadi-upabhogaih agatanugatabhrityadin aharnisham asheshagriheshu tah kshitishaduhitaro bhojayamasuh ||

verses.sa: एकदा तु दुहितृस्नेहाकृष्टहृदयः स महीपतिः अतिदुःखिताः ता उत सुखिता वा इति विचिन्त्य तस्य महर्षेः आश्रमसमीपम् उपेत्य स्फुरदंशुमालाललामां स्फटिकमयप्रासादमालाम् अतिरम्योपवनजलाशयां ददर्श ॥
verses.rom: ekada tu duhitrisnehakrishtahridayah sa mahipatih atiduhkhitah ta uta sukhita va iti vichintya tasya maharsheh ashramasamipam upetya sphuradamshumalalalamam sphatikamayaprasadamalam atiramyopavanajalashayam dadarsha ||

verses.sa: प्रविश्य चैकं प्रासादम् आत्मजां परिष्वज्य कृतासनपरिग्रहः प्रवृद्धस्नेहनयनाम्बुगर्भनयनः अब्रवीत् ॥
verses.rom: pravishya chaikam prasadam atmajam parishvajya kritasanaparigrahah pravriddhasnehanayanambugarbhanayanah abravit ||

verses.sa: “अप्यत्र वत्से भवत्याः सुखम् उत किञ्चिदसुखम् । अपि ते महर्षिः स्नेहवान् उत न स्मर्यते अस्मद्गृहवास” इत्युक्ता तं तनया पितरमाह ॥
verses.rom: “apyatra vatse bhavatyah sukham uta kinchidasukham | api te maharshih snehavan uta na smaryate asmadgrihavasa” ityukta tam tanaya pitaramaha ||

verses.sa: “तात अतिरमणीयः प्रासादः अत्र, अतिमनोज्ञम् उपवनम्, एते कल-वाक्य-विहङ्गम-अभिरुताः प्रोत्फुल्ल-पद्माकर-जलाशयाः, मनो-अनुकूल-भक्ष्य-भोज्यानुलेपन-वस्त्र-भूषणादि-भोगः, मृदूनि शयनासनानि सर्वसम्पत्समेतं मे गार्हस्थ्यम् ॥
verses.rom: “tata atiramaniyah prasadah atra, atimanojnam upavanam, ete kala-vakya-vihangama-abhirutah protphulla-padmakara-jalashayah, mano-anukula-bhakshya-bhojyanulepana-vastra-bhushanadi-bhogah, mriduni shayanasanani sarvasampatsametam me garhasthyam ||

verses.sa: तथापि केन वा जन्मभूमिर्न स्मर्यते ॥
त्वत्प्रसादात् इदमशेषम् अतिशोभनम् ॥
किं त्वेकं ममैतद्दुःखकारणं यदस्मद्गृहान्महर्षिः अयं मद्भर्त्ता न विष्क्रामति ममैव केवलमतिप्रीत्या समीपपरिवर्ती नान्यासाम् अस्मद्भगिनीनाम् ॥
verses.rom: kim tvekam mamaitadduhkhakaranam yadasmadgrihanmaharshih ayam madbhartta na vishkramati mamaiva kevalamatipritya samipaparivarti nanyasam asmadbhagininam ||

verses.sa: एवं च मम सोदर्योऽतिदुःखिता इत्येवम् अतिदुःखकारणम्” इत्युक्तः तया, द्वितीयं प्रासादमुपेत्य स्वतनयां परिष्वज्यो उपविष्टः तथैव पृष्टवान् ॥
verses.rom: evam cha mama sodaryo'tiduhkhita ityevam atiduhkhakaranam” ityuktah taya, dvitiyam prasadamupetya svatanayam parishvajyo upavishtah tathaiva prishtavan ||

verses.sa: तयापि च “सर्वमेतत् प्रासादादि-उपभोग-सुखं भृशम् आख्यातं ममैव केवलमतिप्रीत्या पार्श्वपरिवर्त्ती नान्यासाम् अस्मद्भगिनीनाम्” इत्येवमादि श्रुत्वा समस्तप्रासादेषु राजा प्रविवेश तनयां तनयां तथैवापृच्छत् ॥
verses.rom: tayapi cha “sarvametat prasadadi-upabhoga-sukham bhrisham akhyatam mamaiva kevalamatipritya parshvaparivartti nanyasam asmadbhagininam” ityevamadi shrutva samastaprasadeshu raja pravivesha tanayam tanayam tathaivaprichchhat ||

verses.sa: सर्वाभिश्च ताभिः तथैवाभिहितः परितोष-विस्मय-निर्भर-विवश-हृदयो भगवन्तं सौभरिम् एकान्तावस्थितम् उपेत्य कृतपूजः अब्रवीत् ॥
verses.rom: sarvabhishcha tabhih tathaivabhihitah paritosha-vismaya-nirbhara-vivasha-hridayo bhagavantam saubharim ekantavasthitam upetya kritapujah abravit ||

verses.sa: “दृष्टस्ते भगवन् सुमहानेष सिद्धिप्रभावः, नैवंविधम् अन्यस्य कस्यचित् अस्माभिः विभूतिभिः विलसितम् उपलक्षितं यदेतद्भगवतः तपसः फलम्” इत्यभिपूज्य तमृषिं तत्रैव तेन ऋषिवर्येण सह किञ्चित्कालम् अभिमतोपभोगान् बुभुजे स्वपुरं च जगाम ॥
verses.rom: “drishtaste bhagavan sumahanesha siddhiprabhavah, naivamvidham anyasya kasyachit asmabhih vibhutibhih vilasitam upalakshitam yadetadbhagavatah tapasah phalam” ityabhipujya tamrishim tatraiva tena rishivaryena saha kinchitkalam abhimatopabhogan bubhuje svapuram cha jagama ||

verses.sa: कालेन गच्छता तस्य तासु राजतनयासु पुत्रशतं सार्धमभवत् ॥
verses.rom: kalena gachchhata tasya tasu rajatanayasu putrashatam sardhamabhavat ||

verses.sa: अनुदिनानुरूढस्नेहप्रसरश्च स तत्र अतीव ममताकृष्टहृदयोऽभवत् ॥

“अप्येतेऽस्मत्पुत्राः कलभाषिणः पद्भ्यां गच्छेयुः, अप्येते यौवनिनो भवेयुः, अपि कृतदारानेतान् पश्येयम्, अप्येषां पुत्रा भवेयुः, अप्येतत्पुत्रान् पुत्रसमन्वितान् पश्यामि” इत्यादिमनोरथान् अनुदिनं कालसम्पत्तिप्रवृद्धान् उपेक्ष्य एतच्चिन्तयामास ॥
verses.rom: “apyete'smatputrah kalabhashinah padbhyam gachchheyuh, apyete yauvanino bhaveyuh, api kritadaranetan pashyeyam, apyesham putra bhaveyuh, apyetatputran putrasamanvitan pashyami” ityadimanorathan anudinam kalasampattipravriddhan upekshya etachchintayamasa ||

verses.sa: “अहो मे मोहस्यातिविस्तारः ॥

मनोरथानां न समाप्तिरस्ति वर्षायुतेनापि तथाब्दलक्षैः ।
पूर्णेषु पूर्णेषु मनोरथानामुत्पत्तयस्सन्ति पुनर्नवानाम् ॥
verses.rom:
manorathanam na samaptirasti varshayutenapi tathabdalakshaih |
purneshu purneshu manorathanamutpattayassanti punarnavanam ||

verses.sa:
पद्भ्यां गता यौवनिनश्च जाता दारैश्च संयोगमिताः प्रसूताः ।
दृष्टाः सुतास्तत्तनयप्रसूतिं द्रष्टुं पुनर्वाञ्छति मेऽन्तरात्मा ॥
verses.rom:
padbhyam gata yauvaninashcha jata daraishcha samyogamitah prasutah |
drishtah sutastattanayaprasutim drashtum punarvanchhati me'ntaratma ||

verses.sa:
द्रक्ष्यामि तेषामिति चेत् प्रसूतिं मनोरथो मे भविता ततोऽन्यः ।
पूर्णेऽपि तत्राप्यपरस्य जन्म निवार्यते केन मनोरथस्य ॥
verses.rom:
drakshyami teshamiti chet prasutim manoratho me bhavita tato'nyah |
purne'pi tatrapyaparasya janma nivaryate kena manorathasya ||

verses.sa:
आमृत्युतो नैव मनोरथानामन्तोऽस्ति विज्ञातमिदं मयाद्य ।
मनोरथासक्तिपरस्य चित्तं न जायते वै परमार्थसङ्गि ॥
verses.rom:
amrityuto naiva manorathanamanto'sti vijnatamidam mayadya |
manorathasaktiparasya chittam na jayate vai paramarthasangi ||

verses.sa:
स मे समाधिर्जलवासमित्रमत्स्यस्य सङ्गात् सहसैव नष्टः ।
परिग्रहः सङ्गकृतो मयायं परिग्रहोत्था च ममातिलिप्सा ॥
verses.rom:
sa me samadhirjalavasamitramatsyasya sangat sahasaiva nashtah |
parigrahah sangakrito mayayam parigrahottha cha mamatilipsa ||

verses.sa:
दुःखं यदैवैकशरीरजन्म शतार्धसङ्ख्याकमिदं प्रसूतम् ।
परिग्रहेण क्षितिपात्मजानां सुतैरनेकैर्बहुलीकृतं तत् ॥
verses.rom:
duhkham yadaivaikasharirajanma shatardhasankhyakamidam prasutam |
parigrahena kshitipatmajanam sutairanekairbahulikritam tat ||

verses.sa:
सुतात्मजैस्तत्तनयैश्च भूयो भूयश्च तेषां च परिग्रहेण ।
विस्तारमेष्यत्यतिदुःखहेतुः परिग्रहो वै ममताभिधानः ॥
verses.rom:
sutatmajaistattanayaishcha bhuyo bhuyashcha tesham cha parigrahena |
vistarameshyatyatiduhkhahetuh parigraho vai mamatabhidhanah ||

verses.sa:
चीर्णं तपो यत्तु जलाश्रयेण तस्यर्द्धिरेषा तपसोऽन्तरायः ।
मत्स्यस्य सङ्गादभवच्च यो मे सुतादिरागो मुषितोऽस्मि तेन ॥
verses.rom:
chirnam tapo yattu jalashrayena tasyarddhiresha tapaso'ntarayah |
matsyasya sangadabhavachcha yo me sutadirago mushito'smi tena ||

verses.sa:
निस्सङ्गता मुक्तिपदं यतीनां सङ्गादशेषाः प्रभवन्ति दोषाः ।
आरूढयोगो विनिपात्यतेऽधः सङ्गेन योगी किमुताल्पबुद्धिः ॥
verses.rom:
nissangata muktipadam yatinam sangadasheshah prabhavanti doshah |
arudhayogo vinipatyate'dhah sangena yogi kimutalpabuddhih ||

verses.sa:
अहं चरिष्यामि तदात्मनोऽर्थे परिग्रहग्राहगृहीतबुद्धिः ।
यदा हि भूयः परिहीनदोषो जनस्य दुःखैर्भविता न दुःखी ॥
verses.rom:
aham charishyami tadatmano'rthe parigrahagrahagrihitabuddhih |
yada hi bhuyah parihinadosho janasya duhkhairbhavita na duhkhi ||

verses.sa:
सर्वस्य धातारमचिन्त्यरूपमणोरणीयांसमतिप्रमाणम् ।
सितासितं चेश्वरमीश्वराणामाराधयिष्ये तपसैव विष्णुम् ॥

तस्मिन्नशेषौजसि सर्वरूपिण्यव्यक्तविस्पष्टतनावनन्ते ।
ममाचलं चित्तमपेतदोषं सदास्तु विष्णावभवाय भूयः ॥
verses.rom:
tasminnasheshaujasi sarvarupinyavyaktavispashtatanavanante |
mamachalam chittamapetadosham sadastu vishnavabhavaya bhuyah ||

verses.sa:
समस्तभूतादमलादनन्तात् सर्वेश्वरादन्यदनादिमध्यात् ।
यस्मान्न किञ्चित् तमहं गुरूणां परं गुरुं संश्रयमेमि विष्णुम् ॥
verses.rom:
samastabhutadamaladanantat sarveshvaradanyadanadimadhyat |
yasmanna kinchit tamaham gurunam param gurum samshrayamemi vishnum ||

verses.sa:
श्रीपराशर उवाच
इत्यात्मानम् आत्मनैव अभिधाय असौ सौभरिः अपहाय पुत्रगृहासनपरिच्छदादिकम् अशेषमर्थजातं सकलभार्यासमन्वितो वनं प्रविवेश ॥
verses.rom:
shriparashara uvacha
ityatmanam atmanaiva abhidhaya asau saubharih apahaya putragrihasanaparichchhadadikam asheshamarthajatam sakalabharyasamanvito vanam pravivesha ||

verses.sa: तत्राप्यनुदिनं वैखानसनिष्पाद्यम् अशेषक्रियाकलापं निष्पाद्य क्षपितसकलपापः परिपक्वमनोवृत्तिः आत्मनि अग्नीन् समारोप्य भिक्षुः अभवत् ॥
verses.rom: tatrapyanudinam vaikhanasanishpadyam asheshakriyakalapam nishpadya kshapitasakalapapah paripakvamanovrittih atmani agnin samaropya bhikshuh abhavat ||

verses.sa: भगवति आसज्य अखिलं कर्मकलापं हित्व अनन्तम् अजम् अनादिनिधनम् अविकारमरणादिधर्मम् अवाप परमनन्तं परवताम् अच्युतं पदम् ॥
verses.rom: bhagavati asajya akhilam karmakalapam hitva anantam ajam anadinidhanam avikaramaranadidharmam avapa paramanantam paravatam achyutam padam ||

verses.sa: इत्येतन्मान्धातृदुहितृसम्बन्धादाख्यातम् ॥

यश्चैतत् सौभरिचरितम् अनुस्मरति पठति पाठयति शृणोति श्रावयति धरति अवधारयति लिखति लेखयति शिक्षयति अध्यापयति उपदिशति वा तस्य षड् जन्मानि दुस्सन्ततिः असद्धर्मो वाङ्मनसयोः असन्मार्गाचरणम् अशेषहेतुषु वा ममत्वं न भवति ॥
verses.rom: yashchaitat saubharicharitam anusmarati pathati pathayati shrinoti shravayati dharati avadharayati likhati lekhayati shikshayati adhyapayati upadishati va tasya shad janmani dussantatih asaddharmo vanmanasayoh asanmargacharanam asheshahetushu va mamatvam na bhavati ||

verses.sa: ॥ इति श्रीविष्णुमहापुराणे चतुर्थांशे द्वितीयोऽध्यायः ॥

prose.en:
Whilst Kakudmin Raivata was absent in the region of Brahmā, Rākshasas named Punyjanas devastated his capital Kusasthali. His hundred brothers, afraid of the enemies, fled in different directions and their descendants the Kshatriyas settled all over the country.

From Dhristha originated the Kshatriya race of Dharshtaka; the son of Nabhaga was Nābhaga; his son was Ambarisa; his son was Virupa; his son was Prishadāswa; his son was Rathinara, of whom it is said—"These princes of Rathinara family, although Kshatriyas by birth, were called Angerasas or sons of Angera and were Brāhmans and Kshatriyas".

As Manu was sneezing Ikshawku was born from his nostril. He had a hundred sons of whom the three well-known were Vikukshi, Nimi and Danda. These and fifty under Sakuni were the rulers of the north. Forty-eight were the rulers of the south.

Being engaged in the celebration of an ancestral rite upon Ashtaka day Ikshawku ordered Vikukshi to bring him flesh suitable for the offering. The prince, therefore, went into woods and slew many a deer and other wild animals for the purpose. Being exhausted with hunting he was hungry; accordingly he sat down and ate a hare. And being refreshed he carried the rest of the game to his father. Vaisishtha, the family priest of Ikshawakus, was invited to consecrate the food; but he said that it was impure on account of Vikuksh's having eaten a hare from amongst it. Being thus informed by his spiritual preceptor the father abandoned his son who, in consequence thereof, received the epithet Sasāda (hare-eater). On the demise of his father he piously ruled over the earth. A son, Puranjaya by name, was born to him.

There took place a dreadful conflict in the Treta yuga between the gods and demons in which the former were defeated. They accordingly repaired to Vishnu for help and propitiated him by their adorations. Being propitiated the primeval deity, the eternal ruler of the universe, Nārāyana said to them—"What you have desired is known to me. Hear how your desires shall be fulfilled. There is a foremost Kshatriya king named Puranjaya, son of the royal saint Sasāda. Infusing a portion of myself into his body I shall descend on earth and slay all the demons. Do you so endeavour that Putanjaya might engage in the work of the destruction of Asuras". Hearing those words the celestials bowed unto the glorious Vishnu and went to Paranjaya and addressed him, saying, "O foremost of Kshatriyas, we have come to thee to secure thy help in the destruction of our enemies in which we have been engaged. It will not behove thee to neglect our friendship who have come here". Being thus addressed Puranjaya said—"If Indra, the lord of the three worlds, the king of you all, who is known as the performer of hundred sacrifices, agrees to carry me upon his shoulders, I shall then fight with your enemies and help you". The celestials and Indra immediately said "so be it".

Thereupon Satakratu assumed the shape of a bull and the king mounted upon his shoulder. And being invigorated by the power of the undecaying God, the lord of all moveable and and immoveable things, he slew all the Asuras in the battle between the gods and demons. And in consequence of his destroying the Asura army whilst seated upon the hump of the bull he obtained the appellation Kakutstha. The son of Kakutstha was Anenas, whose son was Pritha, whose son was Viswagaswa, whose son was Arda, whose son was Yuvanāswa, whose son was Sravasta, by whom the city of Srāvasti was founded. The son of Sravasta was Vrihadawa whose son was Kuvalayaswa. This prince, invigorated by the energy of Vishnu, slew the Asura Dhundhu, who had disturbed the pious sage Uttanka, and he was accordingly named Dhundhumara (slayer of Dhundhu). Whilst fighting with the demon he was attended by his twenty one thousand sons, who all, with the exception of three, were consumed by the fiery breath of Dhundhu. These three Were Dhridhāswa, Chandrāswa and Kapilāswa. The son of Dhridhāswa was Baryāswa, whose son was Nikumbha, whose son was Sanhataswa, whose son was Krisāswa, whose son was Basenajit, whose son was another Yuvanāswa.

Being aggrieved in consequence of having no son he lived in the hermitage of saints. And being worked up with compassion of sages engaged in the performance of a religious ceremony for this offspring. When half the night had passed away they finished the ceremony and having placed a vessel of consecrated water upon the altar they slept.

When they had slept the king, distressed with thirst, entered the cottage and did not like to disturb the rishis. He then drank the water in the vessel consecrated and rendered efficacious by sacred texts.

When the Rishis got up in the morning, they said—"Who has drunk this consecrated water? Drinking this the wife of the king Yuvanāswa would have given birth to a valiant son". Hearing this the king said—"I have unknowingly drunk this water".

Accordingly a child was conceived in the belly of Yuvanāswa; it grew and in proper time it ripped open the right side of the king and was born. But the king did not die. The son being born the Rishis said—"Who will be its nurse". There appeared the king of the celestials and said "He shall have me for his nurse (mamayan dhāsyati)". He was thence called Māndhāta. Indra put his fore-finger into the mouth of the infant, who sucked it and drew it from heavenly nectar. And he grew up and became a powerful king and brought the seven continents into his subjection. It is said of him "From the rising of the setting sun all that is lighted by his rays is the land of Māndhāta the son of Yuvanāswa".

Māndhāta married Vindumati, the daughter of Sasāvindu end begot on her three sons Purukutsa, Ambarisha and Muchukunda; he had also fifty daughters.

An ascetic, named Saubhari, versed in Rig Veda lived in the waters for twelve years. There lived a huge fish, who was the sovereign, named Sammada, He had a numerous progeny. His children and grand children used to sport around him in all directions and he lived happily amongst them, playing with them day night before the ascetic. Being disturbed in his devotions that ascetic, in the waters, beholding the sport of the king of fish with his children and grand children, thought within himself—"Blessed is the being, who, although born in a degraded state, is sporting with his children and grand children. This has created envy in me and I wish to sport with my children and grand children". Having thus made up his mind the ascetic speedily came up from the water and being desirous of becoming a householder went to Māndhāta to demand one of his daughters as his wife.

Thereupon hearing of the arrival of the sage the king rose up from his seat and worshipped him with libation. Having taken a seat Saubhari said to the king—"I have made up my mind to marry. Do you, O king, give me one of your daughters as a wife. Don't disappoint my love. If any one comes to the race of Kakutstha with a desire he does not go back disappointed. O king, there are many other sovereigns on this earth who have got daughters; but thy family is renowned above all in granting liberal gifts to them who come with that purpose. O king, you have got fifty daughters—confer one of them upon me so that I may be relieved from the anxiety I feel in consequence of the fear that my request may not be granted".

Parāçara said—Hearing the words of the sage and beholding his body worn out with infirmities (he did not like to satisfy his desire)—but afraid of an imprecation he much disturbed in mind and lowering his head thought some time. The Rishi said—"What are you meditating upon, O king? I have not asked for any such thing which you cannot give. Your daughter must be given to somebody. But if you fulfill my desires what is there that cannot obtained by you?" Thereupon the king; afraid of his displeasure, said—"O illustrious sir, such is the practice in our family, that daughters must be given to such fitting persons as they shall themselves select. I did never expect that such a request would come from you—I do not know why such a desire has taken place in your mind. This has created perplexity in me and I am at a loss what to do". Hearing that the sage thought within himself—"This is merely an indirect way of not yielding to my request, I am an old man, having no attractions for women and his daughters will not accept me. Whatever it may be, I shall to that". Thinking thus, the sage said to Māndhāta—"If such be the custom of your family—give orders that I may be admitted into the interior of your palace. If any one of your daughters selects me I shall take her as my wife—if none of them be willing, I shall desist from such an attempt considering that I am too old for it". Having said this the sage was silent.

Being afraid of the imprecation of the sage, the king ordered the eunuch to conduct him to the inner apartment. As he entered, he assumed a form of beauty far exceeding that of men or gods. Addressing the princesses his guide said to them—"Your father, young ladies, sends this pious sage to you who wanted of him a bride. And the king has promised that he will give her to him who will select him". Hearing these words the princesses were all excited with desire and passion, and like a troop of female elephants encircling the lord of the herd, they all contended to have him as their husband. They said to one another—"Away away, sister, I shall take him as my husband. He has already been selected by me; he is not a meet bridegroom for you. He has been purposely created by Brahmā for me as I have been created to become his wife. As soon as he entered the house I selected him as my husband; why do you prevent him from becoming so?" Thus there arose a conflict amongst the daughters of the king, each contending that I have selected him as my husband. While that blameless sage was thus selected by all the princesses the eunuch went to the king and with down cast looks reported to him what had taken place. Having received all information, the king, perplexed the more, thought—"What is all this! What I am to do now! What is it that I have said" and then with extreme reluctance gave away all his daughters to the sage.

Thus the wished-for marriage of the great sage was accomplished and he took away all the princesses to his hermitage. Thereupon he ordered Viswakarmā like second Brahmā, the inventor of art, to construct separate palaces for each of his wives, to furnish each palace with elegant couches and seats and furniture and to attach to them spacious yards, groves with reservoirs of water where the wild ducks and swans should sport amidst beds of lotuses. Thereupon the celestial architect carried out the orders of the sage. And at the behest of the great sage, Saubhari, the divine and inexhaustible treasure Nanda lived there permanently.

Thereupon the princesses entertained there day and night all their guests and dependant with richest and choicest viands.

Once on a time the king, attracted by his affection for the daughters, went to the hermitage of the great ascetic to learn whether his daughters were in poverty or happiness. Repairing there he beheld a number of crystal palaces, brilliant as the rays of the sun and picturesque gardens and tanks. Entering one of the palaces and embracing his daughter, the king said to her with tears of affection and delight in his eyes—"Dear child, tell me how are you here. Are you happy here or not? Does the great sage treat you kindly? Do you remember thy early home?" Being thus addressed the daughter said to her father—"O father, this palace is picturesque surrounded by charming gardens with birds emitting sweet notes, and tanks abounding in full-blown lotuses. I have got here rich viands, fragrant unguents, precious ornaments, costly clothes, soft beds and every other thing that wealth can give. But still then, why should I not remember my early home. By thy favour I have obtained all these things. But there is one source of my grief—my husband never goes out of my house. He is solely attached to me and is always at my side; he never goes to my sisters; for this my sisters are sorry; this is the only cause of my uneasiness". Being thus addressed he went to the second palace and embracing his daughter and taking his seat he put the same question. The same account of the enjoyment of palaces and other things was given by her; she also made the same complaint that the sage was solely attached to her and paid no attention to her sisters. Hearing this the king went round all the palaces, put the same question to all his daughters and received the same reply. Having his heart filled with satisfaction and wonder he repaired to the glorious Saubhari who was alone and reverentially said to him—"O illustrious sage, marvellous is thy power—I have never seen this in any other person. Oh great is the reward of thy austere penances". Having bowed unto the sage and been welcomed by him with great reverence the king lived with him for some time and enjoying the pleasures of the place returned to his capital.

As time went on the daughters of Māndhāta bore to Saubhari one hundred and fifty sons. Gradually he became more and more attached to his children and his mind was wholly engrossed with selfish thoughts. He always used to think—"When will these sons of mine speak to me in sweet accents? When will they learn to walk? When will they attain to youth? When shall I see them wedded? When shall I behold them with their sons?" With these anticipations, he spent some time and at last thought "What exceeding folly is mine! There is no end of desires even in ten thousand or a hundred thousand years. With one desire gratified another springs up. I have seen my infants walk—I have seen their youth, their manhood, their marriage, their children, still my desires are not gratified and mind longs after seeing the descendants of their descendants. When I shall see them another desire will spring up. When that is satisfied another wish will be engendered.

"How can the growth of desires be prevented? I have now learnt that there is no end of desires till death. His mind can never be devoted to the supreme spirit who is a perpetual slave of desires. My devotions, whilst I was in the waters, were thwarted by my attachment to my friend, the fish. The outcome of that connection was my marriage and the result of that marriage is the cycle of worldly desires. Birth with one body is a source of many ills. By my marriage with the princesses I have got one hundred and fifty sons so my miseries have been multiplied to that extent. And they will be infinitely multiplied by their children, by their wives and their progeny—thus a married life is a source of individual anxiety. My devotions, which I practised in the waters, have been thwarted by my worldly wealth and I have been beguiled by the desire for the progeny which was created in me by the association with Sammada. For the ascetics separation from the world is the only way to liberation; association with others is a source of many evils. Even the most accomplished ascetic is degraded by worldly attachments what to speak of those whose observances are incomplete. Though my intellect has been possessed by the desire of married life still I shall exert myself for the salvation of my soul so that freed from human infirmities I may be released from human sufferings. For that purpose by austere penances I shall propitiate Vishnu, the creator of the universe whose form cannot be ascertained, who is smaller than the smallest, larger than the largest, the source of darkness and light—the king of gods. May my mind, freed from sins, be devoted to his body which is both descrete and indescrete substance, boundlessly mighty, at one with the universe so that I may not be born again. I seek the refuge of that Vishnu, who is the teacher of teachers, who is identical with, all beings, the pure eternal lord of all, without beginning, middle or end and besides whom there exists nothing".

verses.sa:
॥ अथ तृतीयोऽध्यायः ॥
(मान्धातृसन्ततिः, त्रिशङ्कुस्वर्गारोहणम्)
अतश्च मान्धातुः पुत्रसन्ततिरभिधीयते ॥
verses.rom:
|| atha tritiyo'dhyayah ||
(mandhatrisantatih, trishankusvargarohanam)
atashcha mandhatuh putrasantatirabhidhiyate ||

verses.sa: अम्बरीषस्य मान्धातृतनयस्य युवनाश्वः पुत्रोऽभूत् ॥
तस्मात् हारीतः यतोऽङ्गिरसो हारीताः ॥
रसातले मौनेया नाम गन्धर्वा बभूवुः षट्कोटिसंख्याताः । तैः अशेषाणि नागकुलानि अपहृतप्रधानरत्नाधिपत्यानि अक्रियन्त ॥
verses.rom: rasatale mauneya nama gandharva babhuvuh shatkotisamkhyatah | taih asheshani nagakulani apahritapradhanaratnadhipatyani akriyanta ||

verses.sa: तैश्च गन्धर्ववीर्यावधूतैः उरगेश्वरैः स्तूयमानो भगवान् अशेषदेवेशः स्तव-च्छ्रवण-उन्मीलित-उन्निद्र-पुण्डरीक-नयनो जलशयनो निद्रावसानात् प्रबुद्धः प्रणिपत्य अभिहितः । “भगवन् अस्माकम् एतेभ्यो गन्धर्वेभ्यो भयमुत्पन्नं कथम् उपशमम् एष्यति” इति ॥
verses.rom: taishcha gandharvaviryavadhutaih urageshvaraih stuyamano bhagavan asheshadeveshah stava-chchhravana-unmilita-unnidra-pundarika-nayano jalashayano nidravasanat prabuddhah pranipatya abhihitah | “bhagavan asmakam etebhyo gandharvebhyo bhayamutpannam katham upashamam eshyati” iti ||

verses.sa: आह च भगवान् अनादिनिधनपुरुषोत्तमो “योऽसौ यौवनाश्वस्य मान्धातुः पुरुकुत्सनामा पुत्रः तम् अहम् अनुप्रविश्य तानशेषान् दुष्टगन्धर्वान् उपशमं नयिष्यामि” इति ॥
verses.rom: aha cha bhagavan anadinidhanapurushottamo “yo'sau yauvanashvasya mandhatuh purukutsanama putrah tam aham anupravishya tanasheshan dushtagandharvan upashamam nayishyami” iti ||

verses.sa: तदाकर्ण्य भगवते जलशायिने कृतप्रणामाः पुनर्नागलोकमागताः पन्नगाधिपतयो नर्मदां च पुरुकुत्सानयनाय चोदयामासुः ॥
verses.rom: tadakarnya bhagavate jalashayine kritapranamah punarnagalokamagatah pannagadhipatayo narmadam cha purukutsanayanaya chodayamasuh ||

verses.sa: सा चैनं रसातलं नीतवती ॥
रसातलगतश्चासौ भगवत्तेजसा आप्यायितात्मवीर्यः सकलगन्धर्वान् निजघान ॥
पुनश्च स्वपुरम् आजगाम ॥
सकलपन्नगाधिपतयश्च नर्मदायै वरं ददुः । “यत्ते अनुस्मरणसमवेतं नामग्रहणं करिष्यति न तस्य सर्पविषभयं भविष्यति” इति ॥
verses.rom: sakalapannagadhipatayashcha narmadayai varam daduh | “yatte anusmaranasamavetam namagrahanam karishyati na tasya sarpavishabhayam bhavishyati” iti ||

verses.sa: अत्र च श्लोकः ॥

नर्मदायै नमः प्रातर्नर्मदायै नमो निशि ।
नमोऽस्तु नर्मदे तुभ्यं त्राहि मां विषसर्पतः ॥
verses.rom:
narmadayai namah pratarnarmadayai namo nishi |
namo'stu narmade tubhyam trahi mam vishasarpatah ||

verses.sa: इति उत्युच्चार्य “अहर्निशम् अन्धकारप्रवेशे वा सर्पैर्न दश्यते न चापि कृतानुस्मरणभुजो विषमपि भुक्तम् उपघाताय भवति ॥
verses.rom: iti utyuchcharya “aharnisham andhakarapraveshe va sarpairna dashyate na chapi kritanusmaranabhujo vishamapi bhuktam upaghataya bhavati ||

verses.sa: पुरुकुत्साय सन्ततिविच्छेदो न भविष्यति” इति उरगपतयो वरं ददुः ॥
verses.rom: purukutsaya santativichchhedo na bhavishyati” iti uragapatayo varam daduh ||

verses.sa: पुरुकुत्सो नर्मदायां त्रसद्दस्युम् अजीजनत् ॥
त्रसद्दस्युतः सम्भूतो अनरण्यः यं रावणो दिग्विजये जघान ॥
verses.rom: trasaddasyutah sambhuto anaranyah yam ravano digvijaye jaghana ||

verses.sa: अनरण्यस्य पृषदश्वः पृषदश्वस्य हर्यश्वः पुत्रोऽभवत् ॥
तस्य च हस्तः पुत्रोऽभवत् ॥
ततश्च सुमनाः तस्यापि त्रिधन्वा त्रिधन्वनः त्रय्यारुणिः ॥
verses.rom: tatashcha sumanah tasyapi tridhanva tridhanvanah trayyarunih ||

verses.sa: त्रय्यारुणेः सत्यव्रतः योऽसौ त्रिशङ्कुसंज्ञाम् अवाप ॥
स चाण्डालताम् उपगतश्च ॥
द्वादशवर्षिक्याम् अनावृष्ट्यां विश्वामित्रकलत्रापत्यपोषणार्थं चाण्डालप्रतिग्रहपरिहरणाय च जाह्नवीतीरन्यग्रोधे मृगमांसम् अनुदिनं बबन्ध ॥
verses.rom: dvadashavarshikyam anavrishtyam vishvamitrakalatrapatyaposhanartham chandalapratigrahapariharanaya cha jahnavitiranyagrodhe mrigamamsam anudinam babandha ||

verses.sa: स तु परितुष्टेन विश्वामित्रेण सशरीरः स्वर्गम् आरोपितः ॥
verses.rom: sa tu paritushtena vishvamitrena sasharirah svargam aropitah ||

verses.sa: त्रिशङ्कोः हरिश्चन्द्रः, तस्माच्च रोहिताश्वः, ततश्च हरितो, हरितस्य चञ्चुः, चञ्चोः विजयवसुदेवौ, रुरुको विजयात्, रुरुकस्य वृकः ॥
verses.rom: trishankoh harishchandrah, tasmachcha rohitashvah, tatashcha harito, haritasya chanchuh, chanchoh vijayavasudevau, ruruko vijayat, rurukasya vrikah ||

verses.sa: ततो वृकस्य बाहुः, योऽसौ हैहयतालजङ्घादिभिः पराजितः, अतर्वत्न्या महिष्या सह वनं प्रविवेश ॥
verses.rom: tato vrikasya bahuh, yo'sau haihayatalajanghadibhih parajitah, atarvatnya mahishya saha vanam pravivesha ||

verses.sa: तस्याश्च सपत्न्या गर्भस्तम्भनाय गरो दत्तः ॥
तेनास्या गर्भस्सप्तवर्षाणि जठर एव तस्थौ ॥
स च बाहुः वृद्धभावात् और्वाश्रमसमीपे ममार ॥
verses.rom: sa cha bahuh vriddhabhavat aurvashramasamipe mamara ||

verses.sa: सा तस्य भार्या चितां कृत्वा तमारोप्य अनुमरणकृतनिश्चया अभूत् ॥
verses.rom: sa tasya bharya chitam kritva tamaropya anumaranakritanishchaya abhut ||

verses.sa: अथ एताम् अतीतानागतवर्तमानकालत्रयवेदी भगवान् और्वः स्वाश्रमात् निर्गत्य अब्रवीत् ॥
verses.rom: atha etam atitanagatavartamanakalatrayavedi bhagavan aurvah svashramat nirgatya abravit ||

verses.sa: “अलमलम् अनेन असद्ग्राहेण अखिलभूमण्डलपतिः अतिवीर्यपराक्रमो नैकयज्ञकृत् अरातिपक्षक्षयकर्त्ता तवोदरे चक्रवर्त्ती तिष्ठति ॥
verses.rom: “alamalam anena asadgrahena akhilabhumandalapatih ativiryaparakramo naikayajnakrit aratipakshakshayakartta tavodare chakravartti tishthati ||

verses.sa: नैवम् अतिसाहसाध्यवसायिनी भवती भवतु” इत्युक्ता सा तस्मात् अनुमरणनिर्बन्धात् विरराम ॥
verses.rom: naivam atisahasadhyavasayini bhavati bhavatu” ityukta sa tasmat anumarananirbandhat virarama ||

verses.sa: तेनैव च भगवता स्वाश्रममानीता ॥
तत्र कतिपयदिनाभ्यन्तरे च सहैव तेन गरेणातितेजस्वी बालको जज्ञे ॥
verses.rom: tatra katipayadinabhyantare cha sahaiva tena garenatitejasvi balako jajne ||

verses.sa: तस्यौर्वो जातकर्मादिक्रिया निष्पाद्य सगर इति नाम चकार ॥
verses.rom: tasyaurvo jatakarmadikriya nishpadya sagara iti nama chakara ||

verses.sa: कृतोपनयनं चैनमौर्वो वेदशास्त्राणि अस्त्रं चाग्नेयं भार्गवाख्यम् अध्यापयामास ॥
verses.rom: kritopanayanam chainamaurvo vedashastrani astram chagneyam bhargavakhyam adhyapayamasa ||

verses.sa: उत्पन्नबुद्धिश्च मातरमब्रवीत् ॥
“अम्ब कथमत्र वयं, क्व वा तातोऽस्माकम्” इत्येवमादि पृच्छन्तं माता सर्वमेवावोचत् ॥
verses.rom: “amba kathamatra vayam, kva va tato'smakam” ityevamadi prichchhantam mata sarvamevavochat ||

verses.sa: ततश्च पितृराज्यापहरणात् अमर्षितो हैहयतालजङ्घादिवधाय प्रतिज्ञामकरोत् ॥
प्रायशश्च हैहयतालजङ्घान् जघान ॥
शक-यवन-काम्भोज-पारद-पह्लवाः हन्यमानाः तत्कुलगुरुं वसिष्ठं शरणं जग्मुः ॥
verses.rom: shaka-yavana-kambhoja-parada-pahlavah hanyamanah tatkulagurum vasishtham sharanam jagmuh ||

verses.sa: अथ एनान् वसिष्ठो जीवन्मृतकान् कृत्वा सगरमाह ॥
verses.rom: atha enan vasishtho jivanmritakan kritva sagaramaha ||

verses.sa: “वत्स, अलमेभिः जीवन्मृतकैः अनुसृतैः ॥
एते च मयैव त्वत्प्रतिज्ञापरिपालनाय निजधर्मद्विजसङ्गपरित्यागं कारिताः” ॥
verses.rom: ete cha mayaiva tvatpratijnaparipalanaya nijadharmadvijasangaparityagam karitah” ||

verses.sa: तथेति तद्गुरुवचनम् अभिनन्द्य तेषां वेषान्यत्वम् अकारयत् ॥
verses.rom: tatheti tadguruvachanam abhinandya tesham veshanyatvam akarayat ||

verses.sa: यवनान् मुण्डितशिरसो, अर्द्धमुण्डितान् शकान्, प्रलम्बकेशान् पारदान्, पह्लवान् श्मश्रुधरान्, निस्स्वाध्यायवषट्कारान् एतान् अन्यांश्च क्षत्रियान् चकार ॥
verses.rom: yavanan munditashiraso, arddhamunditan shakan, pralambakeshan paradan, pahlavan shmashrudharan, nissvadhyayavashatkaran etan anyamshcha kshatriyan chakara ||

verses.sa: एते चात्मधर्मपरित्यागात् ब्राह्मणैः परित्यक्ता म्लेच्छतां ययुः ॥
verses.rom: ete chatmadharmaparityagat brahmanaih parityakta mlechchhatam yayuh ||

verses.sa: सगरोऽपि स्वमधिष्ठानम् आगम्य-अस्खलित-चक्रः सप्तद्वीपवतीम् इमाम् उर्वीं प्रशशास ॥
verses.rom: sagaro'pi svamadhishthanam agamya-askhalita-chakrah saptadvipavatim imam urvim prashashasa ||

verses.sa: ॥ इति श्रीविष्णुमहापुराणे चतुर्थांशो तृतीयोऽध्यायः ॥

prose.en:
Parāçara said—Having thus thought within himself Sauvari renounced his children, his home, his splendour and wealth and repaired with his wives to the forest. Having daily performed there the observances of the ascetics called Vaikhānasas (or ascetics having families) he cleansed himself from all iniquities. When his mind was ripe and freed from passions he concentrated in his spirit the sacramental fires and became a religious mendicant. Then having made over all his actions to the glorious god he attained to the condition of Achyuta which is above change, the vicissitudes of birth, transmigration or death. Whoever shall read, hear, remember, or understand this story of Sauvari and his marriage with the daughters of Māndhāta, shall never, for eight successive births, be addicted to evil thoughts nor shall he act unrighteously, nor shall he think of improper objects—nor shall he be subject to selfishness; I shall now describe to you the progeny of Māndhāta.

The son of Ambarisha, the son of Māndhāta, was Yuvanāswa; his son was Harita from whom sprang Angirāsa Hāritas.

In the regions below the earth, the Gandharvas named Mauneyas, six million in number, had defeated the snake-gods, usurped their kingdom and stolen away all their precious jewels. Defeated by the Gandharvas the serpent chiefs addressed the lord of celestials, sleeping on the surface of the ocean of milk as he awoke from his sleep; and the blossoms of his lotus eyes opened as he listened to their hymns.

They all bowing said—"How shall we be relieved from the fear of these Gandharvas?" Where to the glorious god replied—"I shall enter into the person of Purukutsa, the son of Māndhāta, the son of Yuvanāswa and slay all the Gandharvas". On hearing these words the snake-gods bowed and went away and returning to their country sent Narmadā to secure the help of Purukutsa.

Accordingly Narmadā went to Purukutsa and led him to the regions below the earth, where, being filled with the energy of Vishnu he slew all the Gandharvas. He then returned to his own house. And the snake-gods conferred upon Narmadā a boon that whosoever should think of her, mention her name, should never have any fear from the snakes. This is the invocation: "Salutation unto Narmadā in the morning; salutation unto Narmadā at night, salutation to thee O Narmadā, save me from this serpent's poison". Whoever shall repeat this day and night shall not be bitten by a serpent in the dark or in entering a room. Nor shall he, who shall remember this, suffer from poison, when he eats even food mixed with it. They also conferred a boon on Purukutsa that none in this family shall be bitten.

Purukutsa begot on Narmadā a son, named Trasadasya, whose son was Sambbuta, whose son was Anaranja, who was killed by Rāvana when he traversed the country for conquests. Anaranja's son was Prishadaswa; his son was Haryyaswa; his son was Sumanas; his son was Tridhanwan; his son was Trayyaruna; his son was was Satyavrata who received the name of Trisanku and was degraded to the state of a Chandāla or outcast. Once on a time there was a famine for twelve years. He used to suspend flesh upon a fig-tree on the banks of the Ganges for the wife and children of Viswamitra—he did not give it with his own hands for he might not accept the present of a Chandāla. For this Viswamitra was highly pleased and took him in his living body to heaven.

The son of Trisanku was Haris Chandra, whose son was Rohitaswa, whose son was Harita, whose son was Chunchu, who had two sons named Vijaya and Sudeva. Ruruka was the son of Vijaya and his son was Vrika whose son was Bahu, This king was defeated by the tribes of Haihayas and Tālajanghas and his country was devastated by them for which he fled into woods with his wives. One of those was pregnant and the rival queen being jealous gave her poison to prevent her delivery and the child was confined in the womb for seven years. And Bahu, being stricken in years, died near the hermitage of the sage Aurva. Having constructed the funeral pile the queen was about to ascend it when the sage Aurva, who was cognisant of past, present and future came out of the cottage and prevented her saying—"Hold, hold! This is sinful; there is in thy womb a heroic king—the sovereign of many kingdoms, the offerer of many sacrifices, the slayer of his enemies and a lord paramount. Do not commit such an unrighteous act". Being addressed thus the queen gave up her intention. The sage then took her to his own cottage and after some time she gave birth to a valiant son—and with him the poison came out. And after performing ceremonies consequent upon birth, Aurva gave him, for that, the name of Sagara (from sa with and gara, poison). He then invested him with the sacred cord, taught him the Vedas and the use of all weapons and especially those of fire called after Bhārgava. When Sagara grew up he one day asked his mother, saying—"O mother why are we living here? Who is my father? Where is he?" Being thus questioned his mother related to him everything. Hearing this he was greatly enraged and promised to recover his father's kingdom and destroy the Haihayas and Tālajanghas by whom it had been devastated. When he grew up he destroyed all the Haihayas and would have also destroyed the Sakas the Yavanas, Kambojas, Paradas, and Pahnavas, had they not solicited the protection of Vasishtha, the family priest of Sagara.

Vasishtha, making them deprived of their power, although living, thus said to Sagara—"O my child, these, are already dead. What is the use of pursuing them? To keep up your vow I have made them renounce their own religion and the company of twice-born ones". Sagara reverentially obeyed the request of his spiritual guide and imposed upon them peculiar distinguishing marks. He made the Yavanas shave their heads entirely and the Sakas partially. The Paradas wore their long hair and the Pahnavas allowed their beards to grow according to his command. He withdrew from these and other Kshatriya races the privilege of offering oblations to fire and studying the Vedas. And being thus deprived from the performance of religious rites and having been abandoned by the Brāhmins they all became Mlechasas. Having thus recovered his kingdom Sagara ruled over the earth having seven continents with undisputed sway.

verses.sa:
॥ अथ चतुर्थोऽध्यायः ॥
(सगरस्य अश्वमेधयज्ञः, सौदासचरित्रम्, रामचरित्रम्)
श्रीपराशर उवाच
काश्यपदुहिता सुमतिः विदर्भराजतनया केशिनी च द्वे भार्ये सगरस्य आस्ताम् ॥
verses.rom:
|| atha chaturtho'dhyayah ||
(sagarasya ashvamedhayajnah, saudasacharitram, ramacharitram)
shriparashara uvacha
kashyapaduhita sumatih vidarbharajatanaya keshini cha dve bharye sagarasya astam ||

verses.sa: ताभ्यां चापत्यार्थम् और्वः परमेण समाधिनाराधितो वरम् अदात् ॥
verses.rom: tabhyam chapatyartham aurvah paramena samadhinaradhito varam adat ||

verses.sa: “एका वंशकरमेकं पुत्रम्, अपरा षष्टिं पुत्रसहस्राणां जनयिष्यतीति यस्या यदभिमतं तदिच्छया गृह्यताम्” इत्युक्ते केशिनी एकं वरयामास ॥
verses.rom: “eka vamshakaramekam putram, apara shashtim putrasahasranam janayishyatiti yasya yadabhimatam tadichchhaya grihyatam” ityukte keshini ekam varayamasa ||

verses.sa: सुमतिः पुत्रसहस्राणि षष्टिं वव्रे ॥
“तथा” इत्युक्ते अल्पैरहोभिः केशिनी पुत्रम् एकम् असमञ्जसनामानं वंशकरम् असूत ॥
verses.rom: “tatha” ityukte alpairahobhih keshini putram ekam asamanjasanamanam vamshakaram asuta ||

verses.sa: काश्यपतनयायाः तु सुमत्याः षष्टिः पुत्रसहस्रणि अभवन् ॥
verses.rom: kashyapatanayayah tu sumatyah shashtih putrasahasrani abhavan ||

verses.sa: तस्मात् असमञ्जसात् अंशुमान् नाम कुमारो जज्ञे ॥
verses.rom: tasmat asamanjasat amshuman nama kumaro jajne ||

verses.sa: स त्वसमञ्जसो बालो बाल्यादेव असद्वृत्तोऽभूत् ॥
पिता चास्य अचिन्तयत् “अयम् अतीतबाल्यः सुबुद्धिमान् भविष्यति” इति ॥
verses.rom: pita chasya achintayat “ayam atitabalyah subuddhiman bhavishyati” iti ||

verses.sa: अथ तत्रापि च वयसि अतीते असच्चरितमेनं पिता तत्याज ॥
verses.rom: atha tatrapi cha vayasi atite asachcharitamenam pita tatyaja ||

verses.sa: तान्यपि षष्टिः पुत्रसहस्राणि असमञ्जसचरितमेव अनुचक्रुः ॥

ततश्च असमञ्जसचरितानुकारिभिः सागरैः अपध्वस्तयज्ञादिसन्मार्गे जगति देवाः सकलविद्यामयम् असंस्पृष्टम् अशेषदोषैः भगवतः पुरुषोत्तमस्य अंशभूतं कपिलं प्रणम्य तदर्थम् ऊचुः ॥
“भगवन् एभिः सगरतनयैः असमञ्जसचरितम् अनुगम्यते ॥
verses.rom:
tatashcha asamanjasacharitanukaribhih sagaraih apadhvastayajnadisanmarge jagati devah sakalavidyamayam asamsprishtam asheshadoshaih bhagavatah purushottamasya amshabhutam kapilam pranamya tadartham uchuh ||
“bhagavan ebhih sagaratanayaih asamanjasacharitam anugamyate ||

verses.sa: कथमेभिः असद्वृत्तम् अनुसरद्भिः जगद्भविष्यतीति ॥
अत्यार्तजगत्परित्राणाय च भगवतोऽत्र शरीरग्रहणम्” इत्याकर्ण्य भगवानाह “अल्पैरैव दिनैर्विनङ्क्ष्यन्ति” इति ॥
verses.rom: atyartajagatparitranaya cha bhagavato'tra shariragrahanam” ityakarnya bhagavanaha “alpairaiva dinairvinankshyanti” iti ||

verses.sa: अत्रान्तरे च सगरो हयमेधम् आरभत ॥
तस्य च पुत्रैः अधिष्ठितम् अस्य अश्वं कोऽप्यपहृत्य भुवो बिलं प्रविवेश ॥
verses.rom: tasya cha putraih adhishthitam asya ashvam ko'pyapahritya bhuvo bilam pravivesha ||

verses.sa: ततः तत्तनयाश्च अश्वखुरगतिनिर्बन्धेन अवनीम् एकैको योजनं चख्नुः ॥
verses.rom: tatah tattanayashcha ashvakhuragatinirbandhena avanim ekaiko yojanam chakhnuh ||

verses.sa: पाताले चाश्वं परिभ्रमन्तं तम् अवनीपतितनयास्ते ददृशुः ॥
verses.rom: patale chashvam paribhramantam tam avanipatitanayaste dadrishuh ||

verses.sa: नातिदूरेऽवस्थितं च भगवन्तम् अपघने शरत्कालेऽर्कमिव तेजोभिः अवनतमूर्धम् अधश्च अशेषदिशश्च उद्भासयमानं हयहर्त्तारं कपिलर्षिम् अपश्यन् ॥
verses.rom: natidure'vasthitam cha bhagavantam apaghane sharatkale'rkamiva tejobhih avanatamurdham adhashcha asheshadishashcha udbhasayamanam hayaharttaram kapilarshim apashyan ||

verses.sa: ततश्च उद्यतायुधा “दुरात्मायम् अस्मदपकारी यज्ञविघ्नकारी हन्यतां हयहर्त्ता हन्यताम्” इति अवोचन् अभ्यधावंश्च ॥
verses.rom: tatashcha udyatayudha “duratmayam asmadapakari yajnavighnakari hanyatam hayahartta hanyatam” iti avochan abhyadhavamshcha ||

verses.sa: ततस्तेनापि भगवता किञ्चित् ईषत्परिवर्त्तितलोचनेन अवलोकिताः स्वशरीरसमुत्थेन अग्निना दह्यमाना विनेशुः ॥
verses.rom: tatastenapi bhagavata kinchit ishatparivarttitalochanena avalokitah svasharirasamutthena agnina dahyamana vineshuh ||

verses.sa: सगरोऽपि अवगम्य अश्वानुसारि तत्पुत्रबलम् अशेषं परमर्षिणा कपिलेन तेजसा दग्धं ततो अंशुमन्तम् असमञ्जसपुत्रम् अश्वानयनाय युयोज ॥
