verses.rom: sagaro'pi avagamya ashvanusari tatputrabalam ashesham paramarshina kapilena tejasa dagdham tato amshumantam asamanjasaputram ashvanayanaya yuyoja ||

verses.sa: स तु सगरतनयखातमार्गेण कपिलमुपगम्य भक्तिनम्रस्तदा तृष्टाव ॥
verses.rom: sa tu sagaratanayakhatamargena kapilamupagamya bhaktinamrastada trishtava ||

verses.sa: अथैनं भगवानाह ॥
“गच्छैनं पितामहाय अश्वं प्रापय, वरं वृणीष्व च, पुत्रक, पौत्राश्च ते स्वर्गाद्गङ्गां भुवम् आनेष्यन्त” इति ॥
verses.rom: “gachchhainam pitamahaya ashvam prapaya, varam vrinishva cha, putraka, pautrashcha te svargadgangam bhuvam aneshyanta” iti ||

verses.sa: अथांशुमानपि “स्वर्यातानां ब्रह्मदण्डहतानाम् अस्मत्पितॄणाम् अस्वर्गयोग्यानां स्वर्गप्राप्तिकरं वरम् अस्माकं प्रयच्छ” इति प्रत्याह ॥
verses.rom: athamshumanapi “svaryatanam brahmadandahatanam asmatpitrinam asvargayogyanam svargapraptikaram varam asmakam prayachchha” iti pratyaha ||

verses.sa: तदाकर्ण्य तं च भगवानाह “उक्तमेवैतत् मयाद्य पौत्रस्ते त्रिदिवाद्गङ्गां भुवम् आनेयिष्यति” इति ॥
verses.rom: tadakarnya tam cha bhagavanaha “uktamevaitat mayadya pautraste tridivadgangam bhuvam aneyishyati” iti ||

verses.sa: तदम्भसा च संस्पृष्टेषु अस्थिभस्मसु एते च स्वर्गमारोक्ष्यन्ति ॥
verses.rom: tadambhasa cha samsprishteshu asthibhasmasu ete cha svargamarokshyanti ||

verses.sa: भगवद्विष्णुपादाङ्गुष्ठनिर्गतस्य हि जलस्य एतन्माहात्म्यम् ॥

यन्न केवलमभिसन्धिपूर्वकं स्नानाद्युपभोगेषु उपकारकम् अनभिसंहितमपि अपेतप्राणस्य अस्थिचर्मस्नायुकेशाद्युपस्पृष्टं शरीरजमपि पतितं सद्यः शरीरिणं स्वर्गं नयति” इत्युक्तः प्रणम्य भवगते, अश्वमादाय पितामहयज्ञम् आजगाम ॥
verses.rom: yanna kevalamabhisandhipurvakam snanadyupabhogeshu upakarakam anabhisamhitamapi apetapranasya asthicharmasnayukeshadyupasprishtam sharirajamapi patitam sadyah sharirinam svargam nayati” ityuktah pranamya bhavagate, ashvamadaya pitamahayajnam ajagama ||

verses.sa: सगरोऽपि अश्वमासाद्य तं यज्ञं समापयामास ॥
सागरं च आत्मजप्रीत्या पुत्रत्वे कल्पितवान् ॥
तस्यांशुमतो दिलीपः पुत्रोऽभवत् ॥
दिलीपस्य भगीरथः योऽसौ गङ्गां स्वर्गादिह आनीय भागीरथीसंज्ञां चकार ॥
verses.rom: dilipasya bhagirathah yo'sau gangam svargadiha aniya bhagirathisamjnam chakara ||

verses.sa: भगीरथात् सुहोत्रः सुहोत्रात् श्रुतः, तस्यापि नाभागः ततोऽम्बरीषः, तत्पुत्रः सिन्धुद्वीपः सिन्धुद्वीपात् अयुतायुः ॥
verses.rom: bhagirathat suhotrah suhotrat shrutah, tasyapi nabhagah tato'mbarishah, tatputrah sindhudvipah sindhudvipat ayutayuh ||

verses.sa: तत्पुत्रश्च ऋतुपर्णः, योऽसौ नलसहायो अक्षहृदयज्ञोऽभूत् ॥
ऋतुपर्णपुत्रः सर्वकामः ॥
तत्तनयः सुदासः ॥
सुदासात् सौदासो मित्रसहनामा ॥
स च अटव्यां मृगयार्थी पर्यटन् व्याघ्रद्वयम् अपश्यत् ॥
verses.rom: sa cha atavyam mrigayarthi paryatan vyaghradvayam apashyat ||

verses.sa: ताभ्यां तद्वनम् अपमृगं कृतं मत्वा एकं तयोः बाणेन जघान ॥
verses.rom: tabhyam tadvanam apamrigam kritam matva ekam tayoh banena jaghana ||

verses.sa: म्रियमाणः च असौ अतिभीषणाकृतिः अतिकरालवदनो राक्षसोऽभूत् ॥
verses.rom: mriyamanah cha asau atibhishanakritih atikaralavadano rakshaso'bhut ||

verses.sa: द्वितीयोऽपि “प्रतिक्रियां ते करिष्यामि” इत्युक्त्वा अन्तर्धानं जगाम ॥
verses.rom: dvitiyo'pi “pratikriyam te karishyami” ityuktva antardhanam jagama ||

verses.sa: कालेन गच्छता सौदासो यज्ञमयजत् ॥
परिनिष्ठितयज्ञे आचार्ये वसिष्ठे निष्क्रान्ते तद्रक्षो वसिष्ठरूपम् आस्थाय “यज्ञावसाने मम नरमांसभोजनं देयमिति तत्संस्क्रियतां क्षणात् आगमिष्यामि” इत्युक्त्वा निष्क्रान्तः ॥
verses.rom: parinishthitayajne acharye vasishthe nishkrante tadraksho vasishtharupam asthaya “yajnavasane mama naramamsabhojanam deyamiti tatsamskriyatam kshanat agamishyami” ityuktva nishkrantah ||

verses.sa: भूयश्च सूदवेषं कृत्वा राजाज्ञया मानुषं मांसं संस्कृत्य राज्ञे न्यवेदयत् ॥
verses.rom: bhuyashcha sudavesham kritva rajajnaya manusham mamsam samskritya rajne nyavedayat ||

verses.sa: असावपि हिरण्यपात्रे मांसमादाय वसिष्ठागमनप्रतीक्षकोऽभवत् ॥
आगताय वसिष्ठाय निवेदितवान् ॥
स चाप्यचिन्तयत् “अहो अस्य राज्ञो दौश्शील्यं येन एतन्मांसम् अस्माकं प्रयच्छति किमेतद्द्रव्यजातम्” इति ध्यानपरोऽभवत् ॥
verses.rom: sa chapyachintayat “aho asya rajno daushshilyam yena etanmamsam asmakam prayachchhati kimetaddravyajatam” iti dhyanaparo'bhavat ||

verses.sa: अपश्यच्च तन्मांसं मानुषम् ॥
अतः क्रोधकलुषीकृतचेता राजनि शापमुत्ससर्ज ॥
“यस्मात् अभोज्यमेतत् अस्मद्विधानां तपस्विनाम् अवगच्छन्नपि भवान् मह्यं ददाति तस्मात् तवैवात्र लोलुपता भविष्यति” इति ॥
verses.rom: “yasmat abhojyametat asmadvidhanam tapasvinam avagachchhannapi bhavan mahyam dadati tasmat tavaivatra lolupata bhavishyati” iti ||

verses.sa: अनन्तरं च तेनापि “भगवता एवाभिहितो अस्मि” इत्युक्ते “किं किं मयाभिहितम्” इति मुनिः पुनरपि समाधौ तस्थौ ॥
verses.rom: anantaram cha tenapi “bhagavata evabhihito asmi” ityukte “kim kim mayabhihitam” iti munih punarapi samadhau tasthau ||

verses.sa: समाधिविज्ञानावगतार्थः च अनुग्रहं तस्मै चकार “नात्यन्तिकम् एतत् द्वादशाब्दं तव भोजनं भविष्यति” इति ॥
verses.rom: samadhivijnanavagatarthah cha anugraham tasmai chakara “natyantikam etat dvadashabdam tava bhojanam bhavishyati” iti ||

verses.sa: असावपि प्रतिगृह्योदकाञ्जलिं मुनिशापप्रदानाय उद्यतो “भगवन् अयम् अस्मद्गुरुः नार्हसि एनं कुलदेवताभूतम् आचार्यं शप्तुम्” इति मदयन्त्या स्वपत्न्या प्रसादितः । शस्याम्बुदरक्षणार्थं तच्छापाम्बु नोर्व्यां न चाकाशे चिक्षेप, किं तु तेनैव स्वपादौ सिषेच ॥
verses.rom: asavapi pratigrihyodakanjalim munishapapradanaya udyato “bhagavan ayam asmadguruh narhasi enam kuladevatabhutam acharyam shaptum” iti madayantya svapatnya prasaditah | shasyambudarakshanartham tachchhapambu norvyam na chakashe chikshepa, kim tu tenaiva svapadau sishecha ||

verses.sa: तेन च क्रोधाश्रितेनाम्बुना दग्धच्छायौ तत्पादौ कल्माषताम् उपगतौ ततः स कल्माषपादसंज्ञाम् अवाप ॥
verses.rom: tena cha krodhashritenambuna dagdhachchhayau tatpadau kalmashatam upagatau tatah sa kalmashapadasamjnam avapa ||

verses.sa: वसिष्ठशापाच्च षष्ठे षष्ठे काले राक्षसस्वभावमेत्याटव्यां पर्यटन् अनेकशो मानुषान् अभक्षयत् ॥
verses.rom: vasishthashapachcha shashthe shashthe kale rakshasasvabhavametyatavyam paryatan anekasho manushan abhakshayat ||

verses.sa: एकदा तु कञ्चिन्मुनिम् ऋतुकाले भार्यासङ्गतं ददर्श ॥
verses.rom: ekada tu kanchinmunim ritukale bharyasangatam dadarsha ||

verses.sa: तयोश्च तमतिभीषणं राक्षसस्वरूपम् अवलोक्य त्रासात् दम्पत्योः प्रधावितयोः ब्राह्मणं जग्राह ॥
verses.rom: tayoshcha tamatibhishanam rakshasasvarupam avalokya trasat dampatyoh pradhavitayoh brahmanam jagraha ||

verses.sa: ततस्सा ब्राह्मणी बहुशः तम् अभियाचितवती ॥
“प्रसीद इक्ष्वाकुकुलतिलकभूतः त्वं महाराजो मित्रसहो न राक्षसः ॥
verses.rom: “prasida ikshvakukulatilakabhutah tvam maharajo mitrasaho na rakshasah ||

verses.sa: नार्हसि स्त्रीधर्मसुखाभिज्ञो मयि अकृतार्थायाम् अस्मद्भर्त्तारं हन्तुम्” इत्येवं बहुप्रकारं तस्यां विलपन्त्यां, व्याघ्रः पशुमिवारण्येऽभिमतं तं ब्राह्मणम् अभक्षयत् ॥
verses.rom: narhasi stridharmasukhabhijno mayi akritarthayam asmadbharttaram hantum” ityevam bahuprakaram tasyam vilapantyam, vyaghrah pashumivaranye'bhimatam tam brahmanam abhakshayat ||

verses.sa: ततश्चातिकोपसमन्विता ब्राह्मणी तं राजानं शशाप ॥
“यस्मादेवं मयि अतृप्तायां त्वया अयं मत्पतिः भक्षितः तस्मात् त्वमपि कामोपभोगप्रवृत्तोऽन्तं प्राप्स्यसि” इति ॥
verses.rom: “yasmadevam mayi atriptayam tvaya ayam matpatih bhakshitah tasmat tvamapi kamopabhogapravritto'ntam prapsyasi” iti ||

verses.sa: ततस्तस्य द्वादशाब्दपर्यये विमुक्तशापस्य स्त्रीविषयाभिलाषिणो मदयन्ती तं स्मारयामास ॥
verses.rom: tatastasya dvadashabdaparyaye vimuktashapasya strivishayabhilashino madayanti tam smarayamasa ||

verses.sa: ततः परम् असौ स्त्रीभोगं तत्याज ॥
वसिष्ठश्च अपुत्रेण राज्ञा पुत्रार्थम् अभ्यर्थितो मदयन्त्यां गर्भाधानं चकार ॥
verses.rom: vasishthashcha aputrena rajna putrartham abhyarthito madayantyam garbhadhanam chakara ||

verses.sa: यदा च सप्तवर्षाण्यसौ गर्भो न जज्ञे, ततस्तं गर्भमश्मना सा देवी जघान ॥
verses.rom: yada cha saptavarshanyasau garbho na jajne, tatastam garbhamashmana sa devi jaghana ||

verses.sa: पुत्रः च अजायत ॥
तस्य च अश्मक इत्येव नामाभवत् ॥
अश्मकस्य मूलको नाम पुत्रोऽभवत् ॥
योऽसौ निःक्षत्रे क्ष्मातलेऽस्मिन् क्रियमाणे स्त्रीभिः विवस्त्राभिः परिवार्य रक्षितः ततः तं नारीकवचम् उदाहरन्ति ॥
verses.rom: yo'sau nihkshatre kshmatale'smin kriyamane stribhih vivastrabhih parivarya rakshitah tatah tam narikavacham udaharanti ||

verses.sa: मूलकात् दशरथः तस्माच् इलिविलः ततश्च विश्वसहः ॥
verses.rom: mulakat dasharathah tasmach ilivilah tatashcha vishvasahah ||

verses.sa: तस्माच्च खट्वाङ्गो योऽसौ देवासुरसङ्ग्रामे देवैः अभ्यर्थितः असुरान् जघान ॥
verses.rom: tasmachcha khatvango yo'sau devasurasangrame devaih abhyarthitah asuran jaghana ||

verses.sa: स्वर्गे च कृतप्रियैः देवैः वरग्रहणाय चोदितः प्राह ॥
verses.rom: svarge cha kritapriyaih devaih varagrahanaya choditah praha ||

verses.sa: “यद्यवश्यं वरो ग्राह्यः तन्मम आयुः कथ्यताम्” इति ॥
verses.rom: “yadyavashyam varo grahyah tanmama ayuh kathyatam” iti ||

verses.sa: अनन्तरं च तैरुक्तम् “एकमुहूर्तप्रमाणं तवायुः” इत्युक्तः अथ अस्खलितगतिना विमानेन लघिमादिगुणो मर्त्यलोकम् आगम्य इदमाह ॥
verses.rom: anantaram cha tairuktam “ekamuhurtapramanam tavayuh” ityuktah atha askhalitagatina vimanena laghimadiguno martyalokam agamya idamaha ||

verses.sa: “यथा न ब्राह्मणेभ्यः सकाशात् आत्मापि मे प्रियतरः, न च स्वधर्मोल्लङ्घनं मया कदाचिदपि अनुष्ठितं, न च सकलदेवमानुषपशुपक्षिवृक्षादिकेषु अच्युतव्यतिरेकवती दृष्टिः मम अभूत्, तथा तमेवं मुनिजनानुस्मृतं भगवन्तम् अस्खलितगतिः प्रापयेयम्” इति अशेषदेवगुरौ भगवति अनिर्द्देश्यवपुषि सत्तामात्रात्मनि आत्मानं परमात्मनि वासुदेवाख्ये युयोज । तत्रैव च लयमवाप ॥
verses.rom: “yatha na brahmanebhyah sakashat atmapi me priyatarah, na cha svadharmollanghanam maya kadachidapi anushthitam, na cha sakaladevamanushapashupakshivrikshadikeshu achyutavyatirekavati drishtih mama abhut, tatha tamevam munijananusmritam bhagavantam askhalitagatih prapayeyam” iti asheshadevagurau bhagavati anirddeshyavapushi sattamatratmani atmanam paramatmani vasudevakhye yuyoja | tatraiva cha layamavapa ||

verses.sa:
अत्रापि श्रूयते श्लोको गीतः सप्तर्षिभिः पुरा ।
खट्वाङ्गेन समो नान्यः कश्चिदुर्व्यां भविष्यति ॥
verses.rom:
atrapi shruyate shloko gitah saptarshibhih pura |
khatvangena samo nanyah kashchidurvyam bhavishyati ||

verses.sa:
येन स्वर्गादिहागम्य मुहूर्त्तं प्राप्य जीवितम् ।
त्रयोऽभिसंहिता लोका बुद्ध्या सत्येन चैव हि ॥
verses.rom:
yena svargadihagamya muhurttam prapya jivitam |
trayo'bhisamhita loka buddhya satyena chaiva hi ||

verses.sa: खट्वाङ्गात् दीर्घबाहुः पुत्रोऽभवत् ॥
ततो रघुरभवत् ॥
तस्मादपि अजः ॥
अजात् दशरथः ॥
तस्यापि भगवानब्जनाभो जगतः स्थित्यर्थम् आत्मांशेन रामलक्ष्मणभरतशत्रुघ्नरूपेण चतुर्द्धा पुत्रत्वम् आयासीत् ॥
verses.rom: tasyapi bhagavanabjanabho jagatah sthityartham atmamshena ramalakshmanabharatashatrughnarupena chaturddha putratvam ayasit ||

verses.sa: रामोपि बाल एव विश्वामित्रयागरक्षणाय गच्छन् ताटकां जघान ॥
verses.rom: ramopi bala eva vishvamitrayagarakshanaya gachchhan tatakam jaghana ||

verses.sa: यज्ञे च मारीचम् इषुवाताहतं समुद्रे चिक्षेप ॥
verses.rom: yajne cha maricham ishuvatahatam samudre chikshepa ||

verses.sa: सुबाहुप्रमुखांश्च क्षयमनयत् ॥
दर्शनमात्रेण अहल्यामपापां चकार ॥
जनकगृहे च माहेश्वरं चापम् अनायासेन बभञ्ज ॥
verses.rom: janakagrihe cha maheshvaram chapam anayasena babhanja ||

verses.sa: सीतामयोनिजां जनकराजतनयां वीर्यशुल्कां लेभे ॥
सकलक्षत्रियक्षयकारिणम् अशेषहैहयकुलधूमकेतुभूतं च परशुरामम् अपास्तवीर्यबलावलेपं चकार ॥
verses.rom: sakalakshatriyakshayakarinam asheshahaihayakuladhumaketubhutam cha parashuramam apastaviryabalavalepam chakara ||

verses.sa: पितृवचनाच्च अगणितराज्याभिलाषो भ्रातृभार्यासमेतो वनं प्रविवेश ॥
विराधखरदूषणादीन् कबन्धवालिनौ च निजघान ॥
बद्ध्वा च अम्भोनिधिम् अशेषराक्षसकुलक्षयं कृत्वा, दशाननापहृतां भार्यां तद्वधात् अपहृताकलङ्कामपि अनलप्रवेशशुद्धाम् अशेषदेवसङ्घैः स्तूयमानशीलां जनकराजकन्याम् अयोध्याम् आनिन्ये ॥
verses.rom: baddhva cha ambhonidhim ashesharakshasakulakshayam kritva, dashananapahritam bharyam tadvadhat apahritakalankamapi analapraveshashuddham asheshadevasanghaih stuyamanashilam janakarajakanyam ayodhyam aninye ||

verses.sa: ततश्चाभिषेकमङ्गलं मैत्रेय वर्षशतेनापि वक्तुं न शक्यते सङ्क्षेपेण श्रूयताम् ॥
verses.rom: tatashchabhishekamangalam maitreya varshashatenapi vaktum na shakyate sankshepena shruyatam ||

verses.sa: लक्ष्मणभरतशत्रुघ्नविभीषणसुग्रीवाङ्गदजाम्बवद्धनुमत्प्रभृतिभिः सम्पत्फुल्लवदनैः छत्रचामरादियुतैः सेव्यमानो दाशरथिः ब्रह्मेन्द्राग्नियमनिरृतिवरुणवायुकुबेरेशानप्रभृतिभिः सर्वामरैः वसिष्ठवामदेववाल्मीकिमार्कण्डेयविश्वामित्रभरद्वाजागस्त्यप्रभृतिभिः मुनिवरैः ऋग्यजुस्सामाथर्वभिः संस्तूयमानो नृत्यगीतवाद्याद्यखिललोकमङ्गलवाद्यैः वीणावेणुमृदङ्गभेरीपटहशङ्खकाहलगोमुखप्रभृतिभिः सुनादैः समस्तभूभृतां मध्ये सकललोकरक्षार्थं यथोचितम् अभिषिक्तो दाशरथिः कोसलेन्द्रो रघुकुलतिलको जानकीप्रियो भ्रातृत्रयप्रियः सिंहासनगत एकादशाब्दसहस्रं राज्यम् अकरोत् ॥
verses.rom: lakshmanabharatashatrughnavibhishanasugrivangadajambavaddhanumatprabhritibhih sampatphullavadanaih chhatrachamaradiyutaih sevyamano dasharathih brahmendragniyamanirritivarunavayukubereshanaprabhritibhih sarvamaraih vasishthavamadevavalmikimarkandeyavishvamitrabharadvajagastyaprabhritibhih munivaraih rigyajussamatharvabhih samstuyamano nrityagitavadyadyakhilalokamangalavadyaih vinavenumridangabheripatahashankhakahalagomukhaprabhritibhih sunadaih samastabhubhritam madhye sakalalokarakshartham yathochitam abhishikto dasharathih kosalendro raghukulatilako janakipriyo bhratritrayapriyah simhasanagata ekadashabdasahasram rajyam akarot ||

verses.sa: भरतोपि गन्धर्वविषयसाधनाय गच्छन् संग्रामे गन्धर्वकोटीः तिस्रो जघान ॥
verses.rom: bharatopi gandharvavishayasadhanaya gachchhan samgrame gandharvakotih tisro jaghana ||

verses.sa: शत्रुघ्नेनापि अमितबलपराक्रमो मधुपुत्रो लवणो नाम राक्षसो निहतो मथुरा च निवेशिता ॥
verses.rom: shatrughnenapi amitabalaparakramo madhuputro lavano nama rakshaso nihato mathura cha niveshita ||

verses.sa: इत्येवमाद्यतिबलपराक्रमविक्रमणैः अतिदुष्टसंहारिणो अशेषस्य जगतो निष्पादितस्थितयो रामलक्ष्मणभरतशत्रुघ्नाः पुनरपि दिवमारूढाः ॥
verses.rom: ityevamadyatibalaparakramavikramanaih atidushtasamharino asheshasya jagato nishpaditasthitayo ramalakshmanabharatashatrughnah punarapi divamarudhah ||

verses.sa: येऽपि तेषु भगवदंशेषु अनुरागिणः कोसलनगरजानपदाः तेऽपि तन्मनसः तत्सालोक्यताम् अवापुः ॥
verses.rom: ye'pi teshu bhagavadamsheshu anuraginah kosalanagarajanapadah te'pi tanmanasah tatsalokyatam avapuh ||

verses.sa: अतिदुष्टसंहारिणो रामस्य कुशलवौ द्वौ पुत्रौ, लक्ष्मणस्य अङ्गदचन्द्रकेतू, तक्षपुष्कलौ भरतस्य, सुबाहुशूरसेनौ शत्रुघ्नस्य ॥
verses.rom: atidushtasamharino ramasya kushalavau dvau putrau, lakshmanasya angadachandraketu, takshapushkalau bharatasya, subahushurasenau shatrughnasya ||

verses.sa: कुशस्य अतिथिः, अतिथेरपि निषधः पुत्रोऽभूत् ॥

निषधस्यापि अनलः, तस्मादपि नभाः, नभसः पुंडरीकः, तत्तनयः क्षेमधन्वा, तस्य च देवानीकः तस्यापि अहीनकः, अहीनकस्यापि रुरुः तस्य च पारियात्रकः, पारियात्रकात् देवलो, देवलात् वच्चलः, तस्यापि उत्कः, उत्काच्च वज्रनाभः, तस्मात् शङ्खणः, तस्मात् युषिताश्वः, ततश्च विश्वसहो जज्ञे ॥
verses.rom: nishadhasyapi analah, tasmadapi nabhah, nabhasah pumdarikah, tattanayah kshemadhanva, tasya cha devanikah tasyapi ahinakah, ahinakasyapi ruruh tasya cha pariyatrakah, pariyatrakat devalo, devalat vachchalah, tasyapi utkah, utkachcha vajranabhah, tasmat shankhanah, tasmat yushitashvah, tatashcha vishvasaho jajne ||

verses.sa: तस्मात् हिरण्यनाभो यो महायोगीश्वरात् जैमिनेः शिष्यात् याज्ञवल्क्यात् योगमवाप ॥
verses.rom: tasmat hiranyanabho yo mahayogishvarat jaimineh shishyat yajnavalkyat yogamavapa ||

verses.sa: हिरण्यनाभस्य पुत्रः पुष्यः, तस्माद् ध्रुवसन्धिः, ततः सुदर्शनः, तस्मादग्निवर्णः, ततः शीघ्रगः, तस्मादपि मरुः पुत्रोऽभवत् ॥
verses.rom: hiranyanabhasya putrah pushyah, tasmad dhruvasandhih, tatah sudarshanah, tasmadagnivarnah, tatah shighragah, tasmadapi maruh putro'bhavat ||

verses.sa: योऽसौ योगमास्थाय अद्यापि कलापग्रामम् आश्रित्य तिष्ठति ॥
verses.rom: yo'sau yogamasthaya adyapi kalapagramam ashritya tishthati ||

verses.sa: आगामियुगे सूर्यवंशक्षत्रव्रतप्रवर्तयिता भविष्यति ॥
तस्यात्मजः प्रशुश्रुतः, तस्यापि सुसन्धिः, ततश्चापि अमर्षः, तस्य च सहस्वान्, ततश्च विश्वभवः ॥
verses.rom: tasyatmajah prashushrutah, tasyapi susandhih, tatashchapi amarshah, tasya cha sahasvan, tatashcha vishvabhavah ||

verses.sa: तस्य बृहद्बलः योऽर्जुनतनयेन अभिमन्युना भारतयुद्धे क्षयम् अनीयत ॥
verses.rom: tasya brihadbalah yo'rjunatanayena abhimanyuna bharatayuddhe kshayam aniyata ||

verses.sa:
एते इक्ष्वाकुभूपालाः प्राधान्येन मयेरिताः ।
एतेषां चरितं शृण्वन् सर्वपापैः प्रमुच्यते ॥
verses.rom:
ete ikshvakubhupalah pradhanyena mayeritah |
etesham charitam shrinvan sarvapapaih pramuchyate ||

verses.sa:
॥ इति श्रीविष्णुमहापुराणे चतुर्थेंऽशे चतुर्थोऽध्यायः ॥
।
।

prose.en:
Parāçara said:—Sagara had two wives Sumati, the daughter of Kasyapa and Kesini, the daughter of king Viderbha. Having no offspring the king earnestly solicited the help of the sage Aurva who conferred upon him a boon that one wife should bear him a son who would keep up the race and the other sixty thousand sons; but he allowed them to make their election. Kesini chose to have one son and the other chose to have sixty thousand. Within a few days Kesini gave birth to a son named Asamanjas who upheld the family and Sumati the daughter of Vinata gave birth to a sixty thousand sons. Asamanjas had a son whose name was Ansumat.

Asamanjas was very wicked from his boyhood. His father hoped that with manhood he would reform his conduct. But he continued same even with age so his father renounced him. The sixty thousand sons of Sagara followed the example of their brother Asamanjas. The sons of Sagara having thus trodden the paths of virtue and piety in the world the celestials went to the ascetic Kapila, who was free from guilt, versed in learning and in whom was a portion of Vishnu. Having bowed unto him they said—"These sons of Sagara have followed the conduct of Samanjas. If they continue so how will the world be upheld? Thou art incarnate for the protection of the world". Hearing this Kapila said—"They shall soon be destroyed".

Thereupon Sagara undertook the celebration of a horse sacrifice. They were all engaged to look after the horse. Nevertheless some one stole the horse and carried it to the region below the earth. He then ordered them to search out the steed. Then following the impressions of its hoofs with perseverance they dug downwards each for a league. And coming to the region beneath they saw the horse walking freely. They saw at a distance Kapila, illuminating with the radiance of his person all the quarters, up and down like unto the autumnal sun freed from clouds. Then with uplifted weapons they rushed towards him, saying—"Slay him, slay him; this villain has spoiled our sacrifice; he has stolen our horse". Then turning his eyes a little Kapila looked towards them and with the sacred flame that came out of his body, the sons of Sagara were in no time reduced to ashes.

When Sagara came to know that all his sons, whom he had sent in quest of the horse, had been destroyed by the might of the sage Kapila he sent Asamanja's son to bring the animal. Ansumat, proceeding by the path which Sagara's sons had dug, arrived where Kapila was and reverentially bowing unto him so pleased him that he said—"Go my son and gave over the horse to your grand father; ask of me a boon; thy grand-son shall bring down the river of heaven on earth". Ansumat begged of the glorious Rishi a boon that his uncles, who had died on account of his displeasure although unworthy of it, might be raised to heaven. The Rishi said—"I have told you that your grandson shall bring down the Ganges upon earth. When the ashes and bones Sagara's sons shall be washed by her waters they shall be raised to heaven. Such is the glory of the stream that issues from the toe of Vishnu that they all, who bathe in it intentionally or accidentally, go to heaven. Even those shall go to heaven whose bones, skin, fibres, hair or any other part shall be left after death upon the earth which is contiguous to the Ganges". Thereupon reverentially bowing unto the sage and taking the steed, he went where his grandfather was celebrating the sacrifice. On receiving back the horse Sagara completed the sacrifice and in memory of his sons he gave the name of Sagara to the chasm which they had dug.

The son of Ansumat was Dilipa; his son was Bhagiratha who brought down the Ganges on earth, whence she is called Bhāgirathi. The son of Bhagiratha was Sruta, whose son was Nabhaga, whose son was Ambarisha, whose son was Sindhudwipa, whose son was Ayutaswa, whose son was Rituparna, the friend of Nala, well-skilled in dice; the son of Rituparna was Sarvakāma, whose son was Sudāsa whose son was Sandasa named also Mitrasaha.

Once going out on hunting, the son Sudāsa met with a couple of tigers who had cleared the forest of the deer. He killed of these tigers with an arrow. At the time of dying the form of the animal was changed and it assumed that of a dreadful and hideous fiend. And the second disappeared saying—"I shall take vengeance upon you".

After some time Saudāsa celebrated a sacrifice which was conducted by Vasishtha. At the end of the ceremony Vasishtha went out when the Raksha assuming the shape of Vasishtha said—"The sacrifice is finished to-day. You must give me flesh to eat; I shall just now come back". Having said this he went away and transforming himself into the shape of the cook prepared some human flesh. Saudāsa placing it on a dish of gold, waited for Vasishtha. As soon as the sage came back the king offered to him the dish. Thereat the sage thought—"Alas! what improper conduct on the part of the king that he is offering me flesh!" Then by virtue of his meditation he came to know that it was human flesh. Being worked up with ire accordingly he imprecated the king—"Since you have offered, though you know it, to such holy men as we are what should not be eaten, henceforth, your appetite shall be excited by similar food".

The king said—"It was yourself who commanded this food to be prepared". Vasishtha said—"By me, how could that have been". And being engaged in meditation again he found out the whole truth. Being pleased with the king he said—"The food to which I have doomed you shall not be your sustenance for ever; it shall be only so for twelve years". And the king, taking water in his palms addressed himself for cursing the sage but gave up his intention, being reminded by his queen Madayanti that it ill became him to imprecate a curse upon a holy teacher who was the guardian divinity of the family. Unwilling to throw the water upon the earth lest it should wither up the grain for it was filled with malediction and being equally unwilling to throw it up into the air lest it should blast the clouds and dry up their contents, he threw it upon his own feet. Scalded by the heat which was in the water on account of his angry imprecation the feet of the king became spotted black and white and he therefore obtained the name of Kalmashapāda (i.e. having spotted feet).

On account of Vasishtha's curse the king used to become a cannibal every third night and travelling through the forests devoured many men. Once on a time he saw a pious sage engaged in dalliance with his wife. And beholding that terrible Rākshasa form they fled away in fear but he got hold of the husband whilst they escaping. Thereupon the wife of the Brāhman begged of him her husband again and again—"Thou art the great king Mitrasaha, the pride of Ikshwaku race—not the Rākshasa. It is not proper for thee who knowest the nature of women, to carry off my husband and devour him". In vain did she lament in many ways; he devoured the Brāhman as a tiger devours a deer. Being worked up with ire the Brāhman's wife addressed the king and said—"Since, you have devoured my husband before I was satiated in his company, you shall die as soon as you shall associate with your queen". Having thus cursed him she entered the flames.

After the expiration of twelve years when he was freed of the curse, he, being desirous of dallying with his wife, thought of Madayanti who reminded him of the curse of Brahmani. He, therefore, abstained from conjugal intercourse. Being childless he solicited the help of Vasishtha and Madayanti became pregnant. The child was not born for seven years, and the queen divided the womb with a sharp stone and a son was born who was named Asmaka. The son of Asmaka was Mulaka. When the Kshatriyas were rooted out from the earth, he was concealed by a number of women, hence he was called Narikavachā (having woman for armour). The son of Mulaka was Dasaratha; his son was Ilavile; his son was Viswasaha; his son was Khatwanga, called also Dilipa, who, being invited by the gods in a war with the Asuras, destroyed a number of them. Being pleased thereby the celestials asked him to pray for a boon. Dilipa said—"If you press me to accept a boon, tell me what is the duration of my life". The god said "The length of your life is but an hour". Thereupon Khatwanga, who was gifted with great velocity, came down, in his easy-coursing car to the world of mortals. Having reached there, he prayed and said—"If my soul has never been dearer to me than the sacred Brāhmans; If I have never deviated from the satisfaction of duty; if I have never looked upon gods, men, animals, vegetables, and all created things as different from the imperishable, may I then attain unswervingly to that divine being, upon whom the holy sages meditate".

Having thus spoken he was united with that supreme being—Vāsudeva who is the preceptor of all the gods, who is abstract existence and whose form cannot be described. Thus he was united with Vāsudeva and obtained absorption.

A stanza was cited by the seven rishis in the days of yore—"There shall be no king on earth like Khatwanga. He came from heaven, dwelt an hour on earth, and became united with three worlds by means of his liberality and knowledge of truth".

The son of Khatwanga was Dirghābahu, whose son was Raghu, whose son was Aja, whose son was Dasaratha. The glorious god, from whose navel the lotus springs, was born for the protection of the world, as the four sons of Dasaratha—namely Rāma, Lakshmana, Bharata and Satrughna. While a boy Rāma was taken by Viswamitra to protect his sacrifice and slew Tadakā. In the sacrifice, Māricha was slain and thrown away. Suvahu and others were also slain by him. He removed the iniquity of Ahalyā by merely looking upon her. Arriving at the palace of Janaka he easily broke the bow of Maheswara, and received Sitā, self-born daughter of the king Janaka as the meed for his prowess. He humbled the pride of Parusharama—the Ketu of the Haihaya race and the slayer of all Kshatriyas. At the behest of his sire and not being sorry for the loss of kingdom he went to woods accompanied by his brother Lakshmana and his wife, where he destroyed in battle Viradha, Kara, Dusana and other Rākshasas, the headless demon Kavandha and Vali the king of monkeys. Having constructed a bridge across the deep and slain all the Rākshasas, he brought back his spouse Sitā who had been carried away by the Ten-necked Rāvana. Having purified her by the fiery ordeal, and accordingly her virtue chanted by the celestials, he returned with her to Ayodhyā.

Having slain a number of Gandharvas, Bharata became the master of their country and having slain the Rākshasa chief Lavana, the son of Madhu, Satrughna took possession of their capital Muthrā.

Having thus by their unequalled might and strength the world from the grasp of the wicked, Rāma, Lakshmana, Bharata and Satrughna went back to heaven and were followed by those inhabitants of Kosala who were one-mindedly devoted to those incarnate portions of Vishnu.

Rāma had two sons one was named Kusa and the other Lava. Lakshmana too had two sons by the name of Angada and Chandraketu. The sons of Bharata were Taksha and Pushkara. Subāhu and Surasena were the sons of Satrughna.

The son of Kusa was Atithi, whose sort was Nishadha, whose son was Nala, whose son was Nabhas, whose son was Pundarika, whose son was Kshernadhanwan, whose son was Devanika, whose son was Ahinagu, whose son was Paripatra, whose son was Dala, whose son was Chhala, whose son was Uktha, whose son was Vajranābha, whose son was Sāukanātha, whose son was Abhyuthitaswa, whose son was Viswasaha whose son was Hiranyanabha, who was a pupil of the great ascetic Jamini and imparted spiritual knowledge upon Jajnawakla. The son of this pious king was Pushya whose son was Dhruva Sandhi, whose son was Sudarsana, whose son was Agniverna, whose son was Sighra, whose son was Maru who, by virtue of his power of devotion, is still living in the village called Kalpā and who in future will be the restorer of the Kshatriya race in the solar dynasty. Maru's son was Prasusruta, whose son was Susandhi, whose son was Amarsha, whose son was Mahaswat, whose son was Visrutavat, whose son was Vrihadbala, who was slain in the great war by Abhimanyu, the son of Arjuna. These are the most illustrious kings is the race of Ikshawku. Whoever hears of account of them will be freed from all sins.

verses.sa:
॥ अथ पञ्चमोऽध्यायः ॥
(निमिचरित्रम्, निमिवंशश्च)
श्रीपराशर उवाच
इक्ष्वाकुतनयो योऽसौ निमिर्नाम, सहस्रं वत्सरं सत्रमारेभे ॥
verses.rom:
|| atha panchamo'dhyayah ||
(nimicharitram, nimivamshashcha)
shriparashara uvacha
ikshvakutanayo yo'sau nimirnama, sahasram vatsaram satramarebhe ||

verses.sa: वसिष्ठं च होतारं वरयामास ॥
तमाह वसिष्ठः, “अहम् इन्द्रेण पञ्चवर्षशतयागार्थं प्रथमं वृतः ॥
verses.rom: tamaha vasishthah, “aham indrena panchavarshashatayagartham prathamam vritah ||

verses.sa: तदनन्तरं प्रतिपाल्यताम्, आगतः तवापि ऋत्विक् भविष्यामि” इत्युक्ते स पृथिवीपतिः न किञ्चिदुक्तवान् ॥
verses.rom: tadanantaram pratipalyatam, agatah tavapi ritvik bhavishyami” ityukte sa prithivipatih na kinchiduktavan ||

verses.sa: वसिष्ठोऽप्यनेन समन्वीप्सितम् इति अमरपतेः यागम् अकरोत् ॥
verses.rom: vasishtho'pyanena samanvipsitam iti amarapateh yagam akarot ||

verses.sa: सोऽपि तत्काल एवान्यैः गौतमादिभिः यागमकरोत् ॥
समाप्ते चामरपतेः यागे, त्वरया वसिष्ठो निमियज्ञं करिष्यामि इत्याजगाम ॥
verses.rom: samapte chamarapateh yage, tvaraya vasishtho nimiyajnam karishyami ityajagama ||

verses.sa: तत्कर्मकर्तृत्वं च गौतमस्य दृष्ट्वा, स्वपते तस्मै राज्ञे मां प्रत्याख्याय, “एतदनेन गौतमाय कर्मान्तरं समर्पितं यस्मात् तस्मादयं विदेहो भविष्यति” इति शापं ददौ ॥
verses.rom: tatkarmakartritvam cha gautamasya drishtva, svapate tasmai rajne mam pratyakhyaya, “etadanena gautamaya karmantaram samarpitam yasmat tasmadayam videho bhavishyati” iti shapam dadau ||

verses.sa: प्रबुद्धश्च असौ अवनीपतिरपि प्राह ॥
“यस्मान्माम् असम्भाष्य अज्ञानत एव शयानस्य शापोत्सर्गम् असौ दुष्टगुरुः चकार, तस्मात् तस्यापि देहः पतिष्यति” इति शापं दत्त्वा देहमत्यजत् ॥
verses.rom: “yasmanmam asambhashya ajnanata eva shayanasya shapotsargam asau dushtaguruh chakara, tasmat tasyapi dehah patishyati” iti shapam dattva dehamatyajat ||

verses.sa: तच्छापाच्च मित्रावरुणयोस्तेजसि वसिष्ठस्य चेतः प्रविष्टम् ॥
उर्वशीदर्शनात् उद्भूतबीजप्रपातयोः तयोः सकाशात् वसिष्ठो देहम् अपरं लेभे ॥
verses.rom: urvashidarshanat udbhutabijaprapatayoh tayoh sakashat vasishtho deham aparam lebhe ||

verses.sa: निमेरपि तच्छरीरम् अतिमनोहरगन्धतैलगन्धादिभिः उपसंस्क्रियमाणं नैव क्लेदादिकं दोषम् अवाप, सद्यो मृत इव तस्थौ ॥
verses.rom: nimerapi tachchhariram atimanoharagandhatailagandhadibhih upasamskriyamanam naiva kledadikam dosham avapa, sadyo mrita iva tasthau ||

verses.sa: यज्ञसमाप्तौ च भागग्रहणाय देवान् आगतान् ऋत्विज ऊचुः “यजमानाय वरो दीयताम्” इति ॥
verses.rom: yajnasamaptau cha bhagagrahanaya devan agatan ritvija uchuh “yajamanaya varo diyatam” iti ||

verses.sa: देवैः छन्दितः असौ निमिराह ॥
“भगवन्तः अखिलसंसारदुःखहन्तारः ॥
न ह्येतादृगन्यद् दुःखमस्ति यच्छरीरात्मनोः वियोगे भवति ॥
verses.rom: na hyetadriganyad duhkhamasti yachchhariratmanoh viyoge bhavati ||

verses.sa: तदहमिच्छामि सकललोकलोचनेषु वस्तुं, न पुनः शरीरग्रहणं कर्तुम्” इति एवम् उक्तैः देवैः असौ अशेषभूतानां नैत्रेषु अवतारितः ॥
verses.rom: tadahamichchhami sakalalokalochaneshu vastum, na punah shariragrahanam kartum” iti evam uktaih devaih asau asheshabhutanam naitreshu avataritah ||

verses.sa: ततो भूतानि उन्मेषनिमेषं चक्रुः ॥
अपुत्रस्य च भूभुजः शरीरम् अराजकभीरवो मुनयो अरण्या ममन्थुः ॥
verses.rom: aputrasya cha bhubhujah shariram arajakabhiravo munayo aranya mamanthuh ||

verses.sa: तत्र च कुमारो जज्ञे ॥
जननात् जनकसंज्ञां च अवाप ॥
अभूत् विदेहोऽस्य पिता इति वैदेहः, मथनात् मिथिः इति ॥
verses.rom: abhut videho'sya pita iti vaidehah, mathanat mithih iti ||

verses.sa: तस्य उदावसुः पुत्रोऽभवत् ॥
उदावसोः नन्दिवर्धनः ततः सुकेतुः, तस्मात् देवरातः, ततश्च बृहदुक्थः, तस्य च महावीर्यः, तस्यापि सुधृतिः ॥
verses.rom: udavasoh nandivardhanah tatah suketuh, tasmat devaratah, tatashcha brihadukthah, tasya cha mahaviryah, tasyapi sudhritih ||

verses.sa: ततश्च धृष्टकेतुः अजायत ॥

धृष्टकेतोः हर्यश्वः, तस्य च मनुः, मनोः प्रतीकः, तस्मात् कृतरथः, तस्य च देवमीढः, तस्य च विबुधो, विबुधस्य महाधृतिः, ततश्च कृतरातः, ततो महारोमा, तस्य सुवर्णरोमा, तत्पुत्रो ह्रस्वरोमा, ह्रस्वरोम्णः सीरध्वजः अभवत् ॥
verses.rom: dhrishtaketoh haryashvah, tasya cha manuh, manoh pratikah, tasmat kritarathah, tasya cha devamidhah, tasya cha vibudho, vibudhasya mahadhritih, tatashcha kritaratah, tato maharoma, tasya suvarnaroma, tatputro hrasvaroma, hrasvaromnah siradhvajah abhavat ||

verses.sa: तस्य पुत्रार्थं यजनभुवं कृषतः सीरे सीता दुहिता समुत्पन्ना ॥
verses.rom: tasya putrartham yajanabhuvam krishatah sire sita duhita samutpanna ||

verses.sa: सीरध्वजस्य भ्राता साङ्काश्याधिपतिः कुशध्वजनामा आसीत् ॥
सीरध्वजस्य अपत्यं भानुमान्, भानुमतः, शतद्युम्नः, तस्य तु शुचिः, तस्मात् च ऊर्जनामा पुत्रो जज्ञे ॥
verses.rom: siradhvajasya apatyam bhanuman, bhanumatah, shatadyumnah, tasya tu shuchih, tasmat cha urjanama putro jajne ||

verses.sa: तस्यापि शतध्वजः, ततः कृतिः, कृतेरञ्जनः, तत्पुत्रः कुरुजित्, ततोऽरिष्टनेमिः, तस्मात् श्रुतायुः, श्रुतायुषः सुपार्श्वः, तस्मात् सृञ्जयः, ततः क्षेमावी, क्षेमाविनोऽनेनाः, तस्मात् भौमरथः, तस्य सत्यरथः, तस्मादुपगुः, उपगोः उपगुप्तः, तत्पुत्रः स्वागतः, तस्य च सुपार्श्वः, तस्यापि सुभाषः, ततः सुश्रुतः, तस्मात् सुश्रुतात् जयः, तस्य पुत्रो विजयो, विजयस्य ऋतः, ऋतात् सुनयः सुनाद् वीतहव्यः, तस्मात् धृतिः, धृतेः बहुलाश्वः, तस्य पुत्रः कृतिः ॥
verses.rom: tasyapi shatadhvajah, tatah kritih, kriteranjanah, tatputrah kurujit, tato'rishtanemih, tasmat shrutayuh, shrutayushah suparshvah, tasmat srinjayah, tatah kshemavi, kshemavino'nenah, tasmat bhaumarathah, tasya satyarathah, tasmadupaguh, upagoh upaguptah, tatputrah svagatah, tasya cha suparshvah, tasyapi subhashah, tatah sushrutah, tasmat sushrutat jayah, tasya putro vijayo, vijayasya ritah, ritat sunayah sunad vitahavyah, tasmat dhritih, dhriteh bahulashvah, tasya putrah kritih ||

verses.sa: कृतौ सन्तिष्ठतेऽयं जनकवंशः ॥
इत्येते मैथिलाः ॥
प्रायेणैते आत्मविद्याश्रयिणो भूपाला भवन्ति ॥
॥ इति श्रीविष्णुपराणे चतुर्थेंऽशे पञ्चमोऽध्यायः ॥

prose.en:
The son of Ikshawku, by name Nimi, instituted a sacrifice for a thousand years and appointed Vasishtha as the presiding priest. Vasishtha said to him—"I have been already appointed by Indra for presiding at a sacrifice for five hundred years. Wait for some time, I shall come and officiate as a priest at your sacrifice". Being thus addressed the king did not answer. And Vasishtha went away supposing that he had agreed. Nimi in the meantime engaged Gautama and other ascetics and conducted the sacrifice. After the sacrifice of the king of celestials had been finished, Vasishtha hurried on to celebrate Nimi's sacrifice and found that it was being conducted under the superintendence of Gautama. Vasishtha then imprecated a curse upon the king who was asleep, saying "Since the king, not informing me, has entrusted Gautama with the charge of the sacrifice, he shall cease to exist in a corporeal form". When Nimi got up he came to know what had happened and in return imprecated a curse upon his unjust preceptor that he should also cease to exist in a corporeal form as the punishment of uttering a curse upon him without previously communicating with him. Nimi then gave up his bodily form. The spirit of Vasishtha, also renouncing his body, was united with the spirits of Mitra and Varuna for some time, when at last on account of their lustful desire for the nymph Urvasi he was born again in a different body. Nimi's body continued to be handsome and being embalmed with fragrant oils and resins it was not decomposed and remained like the corpse of one just dead. When the gods arrived there to receive their portion on the completion of the sacrifice the priests requested them to confer blessings upon the celebrator of the sacrifice. And being ordered by the celestials for the same Nimi said—"O celestials, you remove all ills from the world. There is not in the world a greater cause of distress than the separation of soul and body. I therefore wish to dwell in the eyes of all beings and not to take up a corporeal form any more". The celestials agreed to this and Nimi was placed by them in the eyes of all living beings and therefore their eye-lids are ever opening and shutting. As Nimi had no son the sages were afraid that the earth would have no ruler. So they churned the body of the king and a son was born who was named Janaka. As his father had no body Janaka was also called Videha. He also received the name of Mithi for having been produced by mathana or agitation. The son of Janaka was Udavasu, whose son was Nandivarddana, whose son was Suketu, whose son was Devarata, whose son was Vrihaduktha, whose son was Mahavirya, whose son was Satyadhristi, whose son was Dhrishtaketu, whose son was Haryyaswa, whose son was Maru, whose son was Pratibandhaka, whose son was Krisaratha, whose son was Krita, whose son was Vibudha, whose son was Mahadhriti, whose son was Kritirāta, whose son was Mahadhriti, whose son was Suvarnaroman, whose son was Haraswaroman, whose son was Siradhwaja.

Siradhwaja ploughing the field, to make it ready for a sacrifice which he undertook in order to obtain progeny, there sprang up in the furrow a damsel who became his daughter Sitā. The brother of Siradhwaja was Kusadhwaja who was king of Kasi. His son was named Bhanumat whose son was Satadhyumna, whose son was Suchi, whose son was Urjjavaha, whose son was Satyadwaya, whose son was Kuni, whose son was Anyana, whose son was Retujit, whose son was Arishtanemi, whose son was Srutayas, whose son was Sanjaya, whose son was Kshemari, whose son was Anenas, whose son was Minaratha, whose son was Satyaratha, whose son was Upagu, whose son was Sruta, whose son was Saswata, whose son was Sudhanwan, whose son was Subhāsa, whose son was Susruta, whose son was Jaya, whose son was Rita, whose son was Sunaya, whose son was Vitahadya, whose son was Dhriti, whose son was Bahalaswa, whose son was Kriti with whom ended the family of Janaka. These are the kings of Mithilā who shall be principally well-versed in spiritual knowledge.

verses.sa:
॥ अथ षष्ठोऽध्यायः ॥
(सोमवंशवर्णनम्)
मैत्रेय उवाच
सूर्यस्य वंश्या भगवन् कथिता भवता मम ।
सोमस्याप्यखिलान् वंश्याञ्छ्रोतुमिच्छामि पार्थिवान् ॥
verses.rom:
|| atha shashtho'dhyayah ||
(somavamshavarnanam)
maitreya uvacha
suryasya vamshya bhagavan kathita bhavata mama |
somasyapyakhilan vamshyanchhrotumichchhami parthivan ||

verses.sa:
कीर्त्यते स्थिरकीर्तीनां येषामद्यापि सन्ततिः ।
प्रसादसुमुखस्तान् मे ब्रह्मन्नाख्यातुमर्हसि ॥
verses.rom:
kirtyate sthirakirtinam yeshamadyapi santatih |
prasadasumukhastan me brahmannakhyatumarhasi ||

verses.sa:
पराशर उवाच
श्रूयतां मुनिशार्दूल वंशः प्रथिततेजसः ।
सोमस्यानुक्रमात् ख्याता यत्रोर्वीपतयोऽभवन् ॥
verses.rom:
parashara uvacha
shruyatam munishardula vamshah prathitatejasah |
somasyanukramat khyata yatrorvipatayo'bhavan ||

verses.sa: अयं हि वंशः अतिबल-पराक्रम-द्युति-शील-चेष्टावद्भिः अतिगुणान्वितैः नहुष-ययाति-कार्तवीर्यार्जुनादिभिः भूपालैः अलङ्कृतः तमहं कथयामि श्रूयताम् ॥
verses.rom: ayam hi vamshah atibala-parakrama-dyuti-shila-cheshtavadbhih atigunanvitaih nahusha-yayati-kartaviryarjunadibhih bhupalaih alankritah tamaham kathayami shruyatam ||

verses.sa: अखिलजगत्स्रष्टुर्भगवतो नारायणस्य नाभिसरोजसमुद्भवाब्जयोनेर्ब्रह्मणः पुत्रोऽत्रिः ॥
अत्रेः सोमः ॥
तं च भगवान् अब्जयोनिः अशेषौषधीद्विजनक्षत्राणाम् आधिपत्ये अभ्यषेचयत् ॥
verses.rom: tam cha bhagavan abjayonih asheshaushadhidvijanakshatranam adhipatye abhyashechayat ||

verses.sa: स च राजसूयमकरोत् ॥
तत्प्रभावात् अत्युत्कृष्टाधिपत्याधिष्ठातृत्वात् च एनं मद आविवेश ॥
verses.rom: tatprabhavat atyutkrishtadhipatyadhishthatritvat cha enam mada avivesha ||

verses.sa: मदावलेपाच्च सकलदेवगुरोः बृस्पतेः तारां नाम पत्नीं जहार ॥
verses.rom: madavalepachcha sakaladevaguroh brispateh taram nama patnim jahara ||

verses.sa: बहुशश्च बृहस्पतिचोदितेन भगवता ब्रह्मणा चोद्यमानः सकलैश्च देवर्षिभिः याच्यमानोऽपि न मुमोच ॥
verses.rom: bahushashcha brihaspatichoditena bhagavata brahmana chodyamanah sakalaishcha devarshibhih yachyamano'pi na mumocha ||

verses.sa: तस्य चन्द्रस्य च बृहस्पतेः द्वेषात् उशना पार्ष्णिग्राहः अभूत् ॥
verses.rom: tasya chandrasya cha brihaspateh dveshat ushana parshnigrahah abhut ||

verses.sa: अङ्गिरसश्च सकाशात् उपलब्धविद्यो भगवान् रुद्रो बृहस्पतेः सहाय्यमकरोत् ॥
verses.rom: angirasashcha sakashat upalabdhavidyo bhagavan rudro brihaspateh sahayyamakarot ||

verses.sa: यतश्चोशना ततो जम्भकुम्भाद्याः समस्ता एव दैत्यदानवनिकाया महान्तमुद्यमं चक्रुः ॥
verses.rom: yatashchoshana tato jambhakumbhadyah samasta eva daityadanavanikaya mahantamudyamam chakruh ||

verses.sa: बृहस्पतेरपि सकलदेवसैन्ययुतः सहायः शक्रोऽभवत् ॥
एवं च तयोः अतीव उग्रसंग्रामः तारानिमित्तः तारकामयो नामाभूत् ॥
verses.rom: evam cha tayoh ativa ugrasamgramah taranimittah tarakamayo namabhut ||

verses.sa: ततश्च समस्तशस्त्राणि असुरेषु रुद्रपुरोगमा देवा, देवेषु च अशेषदानवा मुमुचुः ॥
verses.rom: tatashcha samastashastrani asureshu rudrapurogama deva, deveshu cha asheshadanava mumuchuh ||

verses.sa: एवं देवासुराहवसंक्षोभक्षुब्धहृदयम् अशेषमेव जगत् ब्रह्माणं शरणं जगाम ॥
verses.rom: evam devasurahavasamkshobhakshubdhahridayam asheshameva jagat brahmanam sharanam jagama ||

verses.sa: ततश्च भगवान् अब्जयोनिः अपि उशनसं शङ्करम् असुरान् देवांश्च निवार्य, बृहस्पतये ताराम् अदापयत् ॥
verses.rom: tatashcha bhagavan abjayonih api ushanasam shankaram asuran devamshcha nivarya, brihaspataye taram adapayat ||

verses.sa: तां च अन्तःप्रसवाम् अवलोक्य बृहस्पतिरपि आह ॥
verses.rom: tam cha antahprasavam avalokya brihaspatirapi aha ||

verses.sa: “नैष मम, क्षेत्रे भवत्या अन्यस्य सुतो धार्यः, समुत्सृज एनम्, अलमलम् अतिधार्ष्ट्येन” इति ॥
verses.rom: “naisha mama, kshetre bhavatya anyasya suto dharyah, samutsrija enam, alamalam atidharshtyena” iti ||

verses.sa: सा च तेन एवम् उक्ता अतिपतिव्रता भर्तृवचनानन्तरं तम् इषीकास्तम्बे गर्भम् उत्ससर्ज ॥
verses.rom: sa cha tena evam ukta atipativrata bhartrivachananantaram tam ishikastambe garbham utsasarja ||

verses.sa: स च उत्सृष्टमात्र एव अतितेजसा देवानां तेजांसि आचिक्षेप ॥
verses.rom: sa cha utsrishtamatra eva atitejasa devanam tejamsi achikshepa ||

verses.sa: बृहस्पतिम् इन्दुं च तस्य कुमारस्य अतिचारुतया साभिलाषौ दृष्ट्वा, देवाः समुत्पन्नसन्देहाः तारां पप्रच्छुः ॥
verses.rom: brihaspatim indum cha tasya kumarasya aticharutaya sabhilashau drishtva, devah samutpannasandehah taram paprachchhuh ||

verses.sa: “सत्यं कथय अस्माकम् इति सुभगे सोमस्य, अथ वा बृहस्पतेः अयं पुत्र” इति ॥
verses.rom: “satyam kathaya asmakam iti subhage somasya, atha va brihaspateh ayam putra” iti ||

verses.sa: एवं तैरुक्ता सा तारा ह्रिया किञ्चिन्नोवाच ॥
verses.rom: evam tairukta sa tara hriya kinchinnovacha ||

verses.sa: बहुशोऽप्यभिहिता यदासौ देवेभ्यो नाचचक्षे, ततः स कुमारः तां शप्तुम् उद्यतः प्राह ॥
verses.rom: bahusho'pyabhihita yadasau devebhyo nachachakshe, tatah sa kumarah tam shaptum udyatah praha ||

verses.sa: “दुष्टेऽम्ब कस्मान्मम तातं नाख्यासि ॥
अद्यैव ते व्यलीकलज्जावत्याः तथा शास्तिम् अहं करोमि ॥
verses.rom: adyaiva te vyalikalajjavatyah tatha shastim aham karomi ||

verses.sa: यथा च नैवम् अद्यापि अतिमन्थरवचना भविष्यसि” इति ॥
verses.rom: yatha cha naivam adyapi atimantharavachana bhavishyasi” iti ||

verses.sa: अथ भगवान् पितामहः तं कुमारं सन्निवार्य स्वयमपृच्छत् तां ताराम् ॥
verses.rom: atha bhagavan pitamahah tam kumaram sannivarya svayamaprichchhat tam taram ||

verses.sa: “कथय वत्से कस्यायमात्मजः सोमस्य वा बृहस्पतेर्वा” इत्युक्ता लज्जमानाह “सोमस्य” इति ॥
verses.rom: “kathaya vatse kasyayamatmajah somasya va brihaspaterva” ityukta lajjamanaha “somasya” iti ||

verses.sa: ततः प्रस्फुरद्-उच्छ्वासित-अमल-कपोल-कान्तिः भगवान् उडुपतिः कुमारमालिङ्ग्य “साधु साधु वत्स प्राज्ञोऽसि” इति ‘बुध’ इति तस्य च नाम चक्रे ॥
verses.rom: tatah prasphurad-uchchhvasita-amala-kapola-kantih bhagavan udupatih kumaramalingya “sadhu sadhu vatsa prajno'si” iti ‘budha’ iti tasya cha nama chakre ||

verses.sa: तदाख्यातमेवैतत्, स च यथा इलायाम् आत्मजं पुरूरवसम् उत्पादयामास ॥
verses.rom: tadakhyatamevaitat, sa cha yatha ilayam atmajam pururavasam utpadayamasa ||

verses.sa: पुरूरवास्तु अतिदानशीलोऽतियज्वा अतितेजस्वी । यं सत्यवादिनम् अतिरूपवन्तं मनस्विनं “मित्रावरुणशापात् मानुषे लोके मया वस्तव्यम्” इति कृतमतिः ऊर्वशी ददर्श ॥
verses.rom: pururavastu atidanashilo'tiyajva atitejasvi | yam satyavadinam atirupavantam manasvinam “mitravarunashapat manushe loke maya vastavyam” iti kritamatih urvashi dadarsha ||

verses.sa: दृष्टमात्रे च तस्मिन् अपहाय मानमशेषमपास्य स्वर्गसुखाभिलाषं तन्मनस्का भूत्वा तमेव उपतस्थे ॥
verses.rom: drishtamatre cha tasmin apahaya manamasheshamapasya svargasukhabhilasham tanmanaska bhutva tameva upatasthe ||

verses.sa: सोऽपि च ताम् अतिशयित-सकल-लोक-स्त्री-कान्ति-सौकुमार्य-लावण्य-गति-विलास-हासादि-गुणाम् अवलोक्य तदायत्तचित्तवृत्तिः बभूव ॥
verses.rom: so'pi cha tam atishayita-sakala-loka-stri-kanti-saukumarya-lavanya-gati-vilasa-hasadi-gunam avalokya tadayattachittavrittih babhuva ||

verses.sa: उभयमपि तन्मनस्कम् अनन्यदृष्टि परित्यक्तसमस्तान्यप्रयोजनम् अभूत् ॥
राजा तु प्रागल्भ्यात् तामाह ॥
“सुभ्रु त्वामहमभिकामोऽस्मि, प्रसीद अनुरागमुद्वह” इत्युक्ता लज्जावखण्डितम् उर्वशी तं प्राह ॥
verses.rom: “subhru tvamahamabhikamo'smi, prasida anuragamudvaha” ityukta lajjavakhanditam urvashi tam praha ||

verses.sa: “भवत्वेवं यदि मे समयपरिपालनं भवान् करोति” इत्याख्याते पुनरपि तामाह ॥
verses.rom: “bhavatvevam yadi me samayaparipalanam bhavan karoti” ityakhyate punarapi tamaha ||

verses.sa: “आख्याहि मे समयम्” इति ॥
अथ पृष्टा पुनरप्यब्रवीत् ॥
“शयनसमीपे ममोरणकद्वयं पुत्रभूतं नापनेयम् ॥
भवांश्च मया न नग्नो द्रष्टव्यः ॥
घृतमात्रं च ममाहार” इति ॥
“एवमेव” इति भूपतिरप्याह ॥
तया सह स चावनिपतिरलकायां चैत्ररथादिवनेषु अमलपद्मखण्डेषु मानसादिसरस्सु अतिरमणीयेषु रममाणः, षष्टिवर्षसहस्राणि अनुदिनप्रवर्धमानप्रमोदः अनयत् ॥
verses.rom: taya saha sa chavanipatiralakayam chaitrarathadivaneshu amalapadmakhandeshu manasadisarassu atiramaniyeshu ramamanah, shashtivarshasahasrani anudinapravardhamanapramodah anayat ||

verses.sa: उर्वशी च तदुपभोगात् प्रतिदिनप्रवर्धमानानुरागा अमरलोकवासेऽपि न स्पृहां चकार ॥
verses.rom: urvashi cha tadupabhogat pratidinapravardhamananuraga amaralokavase'pi na spriham chakara ||

verses.sa: विना चोर्वश्या सुरलोकोऽप्सरसां सिद्धगन्धर्वाणां च नातिरमणीयोऽभवत् ॥
verses.rom: vina chorvashya suraloko'psarasam siddhagandharvanam cha natiramaniyo'bhavat ||

verses.sa: ततश्चोर्वशीपुरूरवसोः समयविद्विश्वावसुः गन्धर्वसमवेतो निशि शयनाभ्याशात् एकमुरणकं जहार ॥
verses.rom: tatashchorvashipururavasoh samayavidvishvavasuh gandharvasamaveto nishi shayanabhyashat ekamuranakam jahara ||

verses.sa: तस्याकाशे नीयमानस्योर्वशी शब्दमशृणोत् ॥
एवमुवाच च “ममानाथायाः पुत्रः केनापह्रियते, कं शरणमुपयामि” इति ॥
verses.rom: evamuvacha cha “mamanathayah putrah kenapahriyate, kam sharanamupayami” iti ||

verses.sa: तदाकर्ण्य राजा “मां नग्नं देवी वीक्ष्यति” इति न ययौ ॥
verses.rom: tadakarnya raja “mam nagnam devi vikshyati” iti na yayau ||

verses.sa: अथ अन्यमपि उरणकम् आदाय गन्धर्वा ययुः ॥
verses.rom: atha anyamapi uranakam adaya gandharva yayuh ||

verses.sa: तस्यापि अपह्रियमाणस्य आकर्ण्य शब्दमाकाशे पुनरपि “अनाथास्मि अहम् अभर्तृका कापुरुषाश्रया” इत्यार्तराविणी बभूव ॥
verses.rom: tasyapi apahriyamanasya akarnya shabdamakashe punarapi “anathasmi aham abhartrika kapurushashraya” ityartaravini babhuva ||

verses.sa: राजापि अमर्षवशात् अन्धकारमेतदिति खड्गमादाय “दुष्ट दुष्ट हतोऽसि” इति व्याहरन् अभ्यधावत् ॥
verses.rom: rajapi amarshavashat andhakarametaditi khadgamadaya “dushta dushta hato'si” iti vyaharan abhyadhavat ||

verses.sa: तावच्च गन्धर्वैरपि अतीवोज्ज्वला विद्युज्जनिता ॥
तत्प्रभया चोर्वशी राजानम् अपगताम्बरं दृष्ट्वा अपवृत्तसमया तत्क्षणादेव अपक्रान्ता ॥
verses.rom: tatprabhaya chorvashi rajanam apagatambaram drishtva apavrittasamaya tatkshanadeva apakranta ||

verses.sa: परित्यज्य तावप्युरणकौ गन्धर्वाः सुरलोकम् उपगताः ॥
राजापि च तौ मेषावादाय अतिहृष्टमनाः स्वशयनमायातो नोर्वशीं ददर्श ॥
verses.rom: rajapi cha tau meshavadaya atihrishtamanah svashayanamayato norvashim dadarsha ||

verses.sa: तां चापश्यन् व्यपगताम्बर एव उन्मत्तरूपो बभ्राम ॥
verses.rom: tam chapashyan vyapagatambara eva unmattarupo babhrama ||

verses.sa: कुरुक्षेत्रे च अम्भोजसरसि अन्याभिः चतसृभिः अप्सरोभिः समवेताम् उर्वशीं ददर्श ॥
verses.rom: kurukshetre cha ambhojasarasi anyabhih chatasribhih apsarobhih samavetam urvashim dadarsha ||

verses.sa: ततश्च उन्मत्तरूपो “जाये हे तिष्ठ, मनसि घोरे तिष्ठ, वचसि कपटिके तिष्ठ” इत्येवम् अनेकप्रकारं सूक्तमवोचत् ॥
verses.rom: tatashcha unmattarupo “jaye he tishtha, manasi ghore tishtha, vachasi kapatike tishtha” ityevam anekaprakaram suktamavochat ||

verses.sa: आह चोर्वशी ॥
“महाराज अलमनेन अविवेकचेष्टितेन ॥
अन्तर्वत्नी अहम् । अब्दान्ते भवतात्र आगन्तव्यम् । कुमारस्ते भविष्यति । एकां च निशामहं त्वया सह वत्स्यामि” इत्युक्तः प्रहृष्टः स्वपुरं जगाम ॥
verses.rom: antarvatni aham | abdante bhavatatra agantavyam | kumaraste bhavishyati | ekam cha nishamaham tvaya saha vatsyami” ityuktah prahrishtah svapuram jagama ||

verses.sa: तासां चाप्सरसाम् उर्वशी कथयामास ॥
“अयं स पुरुषोत्कृष्टो येन अहमेतावन्तं कालम् अनुरागाकृष्टमानसा सहोषिता” इति ॥
verses.rom: “ayam sa purushotkrishto yena ahametavantam kalam anuragakrishtamanasa sahoshita” iti ||

verses.sa:
एवमुक्ताः ताः च अप्सरस ऊचुः ॥
“साधु साध्वस्य रूपम् । अप्यनेन सह अस्माकमपि सर्वकालमास्या भवेद्” इति ॥
verses.rom:
evamuktah tah cha apsarasa uchuh ||
“sadhu sadhvasya rupam | apyanena saha asmakamapi sarvakalamasya bhaved” iti ||

verses.sa: अब्दे च पूर्णे स राजा तत्राजगाम ॥
verses.rom: abde cha purne sa raja tatrajagama ||

verses.sa: कुमारं च आयुषम् अस्मै च उर्वशी ददौ ॥
verses.rom: kumaram cha ayusham asmai cha urvashi dadau ||

verses.sa: दत्त्वा चैकां निशां तेन राज्ञा सहोषित्वा, पञ्च पुत्रोत्पत्तये गर्भम् अवाप ॥
verses.rom: dattva chaikam nisham tena rajna sahoshitva, pancha putrotpattaye garbham avapa ||

verses.sa: उवाच एनं राजानम् “अस्मत्प्रीत्या महाराजाय सर्व एव गन्धर्वा वरदाः संवृत्ताः । व्रियतां च वर” इति ॥
verses.rom: uvacha enam rajanam “asmatpritya maharajaya sarva eva gandharva varadah samvrittah | vriyatam cha vara” iti ||

verses.sa: आह च राजा ॥
“विजितसकलारातिः अविहतेन्द्रियसामर्थ्यो बन्धुमान् अमितबलकोशोऽस्मि, नान्यदस्माकम् उर्वशीसालोक्यात् प्राप्तव्यमस्ति, तदहमनया सहोर्वश्या कालं नेतुम् अभिलषामि” इत्युक्ते गन्धर्वा राज्ञेऽग्निस्थालीं ददुः ॥
verses.rom: “vijitasakalaratih avihatendriyasamarthyo bandhuman amitabalakosho'smi, nanyadasmakam urvashisalokyat praptavyamasti, tadahamanaya sahorvashya kalam netum abhilashami” ityukte gandharva rajne'gnisthalim daduh ||

verses.sa: ऊचुश्चैनम् “अग्निमाम्नायानुसारी भूत्वा, त्रिधा कृत्वा, उर्वशीसलोकतामनोरथम् उद्दिश्य सम्यग्यजेथाः । ततोऽवश्यम् अभिलषितम् अवाप्स्यति” इत्युक्तः तामग्निस्थालीम् आदाय जगाम ॥
verses.rom: uchushchainam “agnimamnayanusari bhutva, tridha kritva, urvashisalokatamanoratham uddishya samyagyajethah | tato'vashyam abhilashitam avapsyati” ityuktah tamagnisthalim adaya jagama ||

verses.sa: अन्तरटव्याम् अचिन्तयत् “अहो मेऽतीव मूढता किमहम् अकरवम् ॥
verses.rom: antaratavyam achintayat “aho me'tiva mudhata kimaham akaravam ||

verses.sa: वह्निस्थाली मयैषा आनीता न उर्वशी” इति ॥
verses.rom: vahnisthali mayaisha anita na urvashi” iti ||

verses.sa: अथ एनाम् अटव्यामेव अग्निस्थालीं तत्याज स्वपुरं च जगाम ॥
verses.rom: atha enam atavyameva agnisthalim tatyaja svapuram cha jagama ||

verses.sa: व्यतीतेऽर्धरात्रे विनिद्रश्च अचिन्तयत् ॥
“मम उर्वशीसालोक्यप्राप्त्यर्थम् अग्निस्थाली गन्धर्वैः दत्ता । सा च मया अटव्यां परित्यक्ता ॥
verses.rom: “mama urvashisalokyapraptyartham agnisthali gandharvaih datta | sa cha maya atavyam parityakta ||

verses.sa: तदहं तत्र तदाहरणाय यास्यामि” इत्युत्थाय तत्राप्युपगतो न अग्निस्थालीम् अपश्यत् ॥
verses.rom: tadaham tatra tadaharanaya yasyami” ityutthaya tatrapyupagato na agnisthalim apashyat ||

verses.sa: शमीगर्भं च अश्वत्थम् अग्निस्थालीस्थाने दृष्ट्वा अचिन्तयत् ॥
verses.rom: shamigarbham cha ashvattham agnisthalisthane drishtva achintayat ||

verses.sa: “मयात्र अग्निस्थाली निक्षिप्ता सा च अश्वत्थः शमीगर्भोऽभूत् ॥
verses.rom: “mayatra agnisthali nikshipta sa cha ashvatthah shamigarbho'bhut ||

verses.sa: तदेनमेव अहम् अग्निरूपमादाय, स्वपुरम् अभिगम्य, अरणीं कृत्वा, तदुत्पन्नाग्नेः उपास्तिं करिष्यामि” इति ॥
verses.rom: tadenameva aham agnirupamadaya, svapuram abhigamya, aranim kritva, tadutpannagneh upastim karishyami” iti ||

verses.sa: एवमेव स्वपुरमभिगम्य अरणिं चकार ॥
तत्प्रमाणं चाङ्गुलैः कुर्वन् गायत्रीमपठत् ॥
पठतश्च अक्षरसङ्ख्यानि एव अङ्गुलानि अरणी अभवत् ॥
verses.rom: pathatashcha aksharasankhyani eva angulani arani abhavat ||

verses.sa: तत्राग्निं निर्मथ्य, अग्नित्रयम् आम्नायानुसारी भूत्वा जुहाव ॥
verses.rom: tatragnim nirmathya, agnitrayam amnayanusari bhutva juhava ||

verses.sa: उर्वशीसालोक्यं फलम् अभिसन्धितवान् ॥
तेनैव च अग्निविधिना बहुविधान् यज्ञान् इष्ट्वा, गान्धर्वलोकान् अवाप्य, उर्वश्या सह अवियोगम् अवाप ॥
verses.rom: tenaiva cha agnividhina bahuvidhan yajnan ishtva, gandharvalokan avapya, urvashya saha aviyogam avapa ||

verses.sa: एकोऽग्निः आदौ अभवत्, एकेन त्वत्र मन्वन्तरे त्रेधा प्रवर्तिताः ॥
verses.rom: eko'gnih adau abhavat, ekena tvatra manvantare tredha pravartitah ||

verses.sa: ॥ इति श्रीविष्णुमहापुराणे चतुर्थांशे षष्ठोऽध्यायः ॥

prose.en:
Maitreya said:—"O revered sir, you have described to me the solar dynasty but I wish to hear now of the kings of the lunar dynasty, who are still well-known for their glorious deeds. It behoves you to relate it gladly to me".

Parāçara said:—O foremost of Munis, hear from me, a description of the illustrious family of the moon which has produced many well-known kings of the earth. This family is adorned with many kings gifted with regal qualities of strength, valour, magnificence, prudence and energy such as Nahusha, Yayati, Kartavirya, Yaryuna and others. Hear I shall describe this family to you.

Atri was the son of Brahmā, the creator of the universe, who originated from the lotus that grew from the navel of Nārāyana. The son of Atri was Soma whom Brahmā made the king of plants, Brāhmans and of the stars. Some celebrated a Rajshuya sacrifice and on account of the glory derived therefrom and the vast sovereignty which he had acquired he grew haughty and licentious. He carried off Tārā, the wife of Vrihaspati, the preceptor of gods.

Soma did not give up Vrihaspati's wife though he was again and again requested by him, commanded by Brahmā and remonstrated by the holy sages. Usanas, who was an enemy of Vrihaspati, took the side of Soma. Rudra, who was a pupil of Angiras, the father of Vrihaspati, assisted his fellow student. Because their preceptor Usanas joined Soma, Jambha, Kujambha, all the Daityas, Dānavas and other enemies of the celestials came to his help. Indra and all other celestials assisted Vrihaspati.

Thus there took place a terrible combat which being on account of Tāraka was called Tarakāmaya or Tarakā war. In this the celestials led by Rudra hurled their weapons upon the Asuras and the Asuras equally overwhelmed the gods with weapons. Thus in the conflict between the gods and demons the universe, greatly overwhelmed, sought protection of Brahmā. Thereupon the glorious God asked Usanas with the demons and Rudra with the celestials to desist from fighting and give back Tārā to Vrihaspati. Finding that she was pregnant Vrihaspati desired her no longer to keep her burden and in satisfaction of his orders she was delivered of a son whom she kept in a clump of long Munja grass. And the child as soon as it was born proved its character of divinity by its radiance. Beholding both Vrihaspati and Soma fascinated by the beauty of the child the celestials, to know whose son it was, asked Tārā, saying "O damsel whose son is he? Is he Vrihaspati's or Soma's". Being thus addressed Tārā was ashamed and did not answer.

Though she was repeatedly asked by the celestials she was still mute and the child, being enraged, was about to curse her, saying—"Unless, O vile woman, you immediately speak out, who is my father, I shall so punish you for your useless shame that no woman in future shall speak the truth". Brahmā again interfered and pacifying the child said, addressing Tara "Tell me my daughter, is this the child of Vrihaspati or of Soma?" "Of Soma," said Tārā flushing. Thereupon the countenance of the king of constellations became bright, and expanded with joy. He at once embraced his son and said—"Well done my boy, forsooth thou art wise". And accordingly the boy was named Budha.

I have already described how Budha begot Pururavas on Ilā. Paruravas was a prince famous for liberality, devotion, magnificence, love of truth and beauty. Having incurred the curse of Mitra and Varuna, Urvasi made up her mind to live in the land of mortals and descending there saw Pururavas. As soon as a she saw him she forgot all reserve and not caring for the comforts to heaven became greatly attached to him. And finding her far superior to all other females in beauty, elegance, symmetry, and delicacy, Pururavas was equally enamoured of her. Both the man and the woman were equally attached to each other and thought no more of any other object. The king then boldly said—"Fair woman, I love you; have pity on me and return my affection". Urvasi turning her face a little through modesty said—"I will do so, if you satisfy the conditions I propose to you".

"What are they?" asked the king "speak them out". "I have two rams" said the nymph "which I love like my children; they must be kept by my bed-side and shall not be allowed to be carried away. You must not be seen by me undressed and clarified butter alone shall be my food". The king readily agreed to these terms.

After this Pururavas and Urvasi lived together for sixty one thousand years in Alakā, sporting amidst the groves and lakes of Chaitraratha abounding in lotuses and the other forests. By these enjoyments Urvasi's attachment increased every day and she forgot all desire for residing in the region of immortals. In the absence of Urvasi heaven appeared devoid of beauty to the celestials, nymphs, genii and quiristers. Knowing the engagement that Urvasi had contracted with the king, Viswasvasu was appointed by the Gandharvas to bring about its dissolution. And coming by night to the room where they were sleeping he carried off one of the rams: Urvasi got up by its cries and exclaimed—"Ah me! who has stolen one of my children: Had I got a husband this would not have taken place. To whom shall I go for help?" The king heard the lamentations but could not go lest he might be seen undressed. The Gandharvas then took away another ram. Again hearing the sound of its being stolen away in the sky she lamented saying—"Alas I have got no husband. I have taken the shelter of a dastardly person". Thinking "it is darkness" the king took up a dagger and pursued them, saying—"stop, O wicked I shall soon slay you". Immediately the Gandharvas created a flash of brilliant lightning in the room and the king was seen undressed by Urvasi. The contract was broken and she instantly disappeared. And leaving behind the rams the Gandharvas too went to the region of the celestials. Taking the rams, the king, delighted came back to his bed-room but found no Urvasi. Not finding her he wandered naked all over the world like a maniac. At length arriving at Kurukshetra he saw Urvasi sporting with four other nymphs in a lake abounding in lotuses. Like a mad man the king neared him and exclaimed—"O my wife, wait, speak with me, O thou of an iron heart". Urvasi replied—"O great king useless is this inconsiderate attempt. I am now pregnant, go away just now and come here again after a year when I shall give you a son and remain with you for one night". Being thus solaced Pururavas came back to his capital. Urvasi then said to her mates. "This king is that excellent man bring drawn by whose attachment I lived for such a long time". Hearing this the other nymphs said, "Great is his beauty; we too with him could live happily for ever".

After the expiration of a year the king again came to that place and Urvasi gave him a son by the name of Ayus. Living with him for one night she again became pregnant to bear to him five sons. She then said to the king—"O king all the Gandharvas, on account of their regard for me, are ready to confer upon thee a boon. Do thou pray for it". The king said—"I have slain all my enemies—my faculties are all very powerful; I have friends, relations, armies and treasures; so there is nothing which I want but living with my Urvasi in the same region. So I wish to live with her always".

After he had spoken this the Gandharvas brought to him a vessel with fire and said,—"Take this fire and according to the precepts of the Vedas divide it into three parts: then offer oblation to it for Urvasi and your desires shall thus be gratified". The Gandharvas having said this, the king took the vessel and went away. Then coming to a forest he thought—"Oh, what stupid I am; I have brought this vessel but not Urvasi". Then leaving the vessel there he came back to his capital. When half the night had passed he awoke and thought—"The Gandharvas conferred upon me this vessel of fire to enable me to live with Urvasi. I have left that in the forest. I shall go there to bring it". Having said this he went there but did not find the vessel. Then beholding a young Ashwattha tree growing out of a Sami plant he argued within himself—"I left here a vessel of fire and I now see a young Ashwattha tree growing out of a Sami plant. I shall take this type of fire to my capital and having created fire by their attrition I will worship it".

Having thus made up his mind he took the plants to his city and made their wood for attrition with pieces of as many inches as there are syllables in the Gayatri. He recited that verse and rubbed together sticks of as many inches as he recited syllables in the Gayatri, Having created fire there-from he divided it into three portions according to the precepts of the Vedas and offered oblations to it with the view of obtaining re-union with Urvasi. Having performed many sacrifices with this fire he attained to the region of the Gandharvas and suffered no more separation from his beloved Urvasi. Thus fire, that was at first one, was made three-fold in the present Manwantara by the son of Ilā.

verses.sa:
॥ अथ सप्तमोऽध्यायः ॥
(जह्नोः वंशकथनम्)
श्रीपराशर उवाच
तस्यापि आयुः धीमानम् अमावसुः विश्वावसुः श्रुतायुः शतायुः अयुतायुः इति संज्ञाः षट् पुत्रा अभवन् ॥
verses.rom:
|| atha saptamo'dhyayah ||
(jahnoh vamshakathanam)
shriparashara uvacha
tasyapi ayuh dhimanam amavasuh vishvavasuh shrutayuh shatayuh ayutayuh iti samjnah shat putra abhavan ||

verses.sa: तथा अमावसोः भीमनामा पुत्रोऽभवत् ॥
भीमस्य काञ्चनः, काञ्चनात् सुहोत्रः तस्यापि जह्नुः ॥
verses.rom: bhimasya kanchanah, kanchanat suhotrah tasyapi jahnuh ||

verses.sa: योऽसौ यज्ञवाटमखिलं गङ्गाम्भसाप्लावितम् आलोक्य, क्रोधसंरक्तलोचनो भगवन्तं यज्ञपुरुषमात्मनि परमेण समाधिना समारोप्य, अखिलामेव गङ्गामपिबत् ॥
verses.rom: yo'sau yajnavatamakhilam gangambhasaplavitam alokya, krodhasamraktalochano bhagavantam yajnapurushamatmani paramena samadhina samaropya, akhilameva gangamapibat ||

verses.sa: अथैनं देवर्षयः प्रसादयामासुः ॥
दुहितृत्वे चास्य गङ्गाम् अनयन् ॥
जह्नोश्च सुमन्तः नाम पुत्रोऽभवत् ॥
तस्यापि अजकः, ततो बलाकाश्वः, तस्मात् कुशः, तस्यापि कुशाम्ब-कुशनाभा-अधूर्तरजसो वसुश्चेति चत्वारः पुत्रा बभूवुः ॥
verses.rom: tasyapi ajakah, tato balakashvah, tasmat kushah, tasyapi kushamba-kushanabha-adhurtarajaso vasushcheti chatvarah putra babhuvuh ||

verses.sa: तेषां कुशाम्बः “शक्रतुल्यो मे पुत्रो भवेत्” इति तपश्चकार ॥
verses.rom: tesham kushambah “shakratulyo me putro bhavet” iti tapashchakara ||

verses.sa: तं च उग्रतपसम् अवलोक्य, “मा भवतु अन्योऽस्मत्तुल्यवीर्य” इति आत्मनैव अस्य इन्द्रः पुत्रत्वम् अगच्छत् ॥
verses.rom: tam cha ugratapasam avalokya, “ma bhavatu anyo'smattulyavirya” iti atmanaiva asya indrah putratvam agachchhat ||

verses.sa: स गाधिर्नाम पुत्रः कौशिकोऽभवत् ॥
गाधिश्च सत्यवतीं कन्यामजनयत् ॥
तां च भार्गव ऋचीको वव्रे ॥
गाधिरपि अतिरोषणाय अतिवृद्धाय ब्राह्मणाय दातुम् अनिच्छन् एकतः श्यामकर्णानाम् इन्दुवर्चसाम् अनिलरंहसाम् अश्वानां सहस्रं कन्याशुल्कम् अयाचत ॥
verses.rom: gadhirapi atiroshanaya ativriddhaya brahmanaya datum anichchhan ekatah shyamakarnanam induvarchasam anilaramhasam ashvanam sahasram kanyashulkam ayachata ||

verses.sa: तेनापि ऋषिणा वरुणसकाशात् उपलभ्य अश्वतीर्थोत्पन्नं तादृशाश्वसहस्रं दत्तम् ॥
verses.rom: tenapi rishina varunasakashat upalabhya ashvatirthotpannam tadrishashvasahasram dattam ||

verses.sa: ततः ताम् ऋचीकः कन्याम् उपयेमे ॥
ऋचीकश्च तस्याः चरुम् अपत्यार्थं चकार ॥
तत्प्रसादितश्च तन्मात्रे क्षत्रवरपुत्रोत्पत्तये चरुमपरं साधयामास ॥
“एष चरुः भवत्या, अयमपरः चरुः त्वन्मात्रा सम्यगुपयोज्य” इत्युक्त्वा वनं जगाम ॥
verses.rom: “esha charuh bhavatya, ayamaparah charuh tvanmatra samyagupayojya” ityuktva vanam jagama ||

verses.sa: उपयोगकाले च तां माता सत्यवतीमाह ॥
“पुत्रि, सर्व एव आत्मपुत्रम् अतिगुणम् अभिलषति, न आत्म-जाया-भ्रातृ-गुणेषु अतीव आदृतो भवतीति ॥
verses.rom: “putri, sarva eva atmaputram atigunam abhilashati, na atma-jaya-bhratri-guneshu ativa adrito bhavatiti ||

verses.sa: अतोऽर्हसि ममात्मीयं चरुं दातुं मदीयं चरुम् आत्मना उपयोक्तुम् ॥
verses.rom: ato'rhasi mamatmiyam charum datum madiyam charum atmana upayoktum ||

verses.sa: मत्पुत्रेण हि सकलभूमण्डलपरिपालनं कार्यं, कियद्वा ब्राह्मणस्य बलवीर्यसम्पदा” इत्युक्ता सा स्वचरुं मात्रे दत्तवती ॥
verses.rom: matputrena hi sakalabhumandalaparipalanam karyam, kiyadva brahmanasya balaviryasampada” ityukta sa svacharum matre dattavati ||

verses.sa: अथ वनादागत्य सत्यवतीम् ऋषिरपश्यत् ॥
आह चैनाम् “अतिपापे, किमिदमकार्यं भवत्या कृतमतिरौद्रं ते वपुर्लक्ष्यते ॥
verses.rom: aha chainam “atipape, kimidamakaryam bhavatya kritamatiraudram te vapurlakshyate ||

verses.sa: नूनं त्वया त्वन्मातृसात्कृतः चरुः उपयुक्तो न युक्तमेतत् ॥
verses.rom: nunam tvaya tvanmatrisatkritah charuh upayukto na yuktametat ||

verses.sa: मया हि तत्र चरौ सकलैश्वर्यवीर्यशौर्यबलसम्पद् आरोपिता त्वदीयचरौ अपि अखिलशान्तिज्ञानतितिक्षादिब्राह्मणगुणसम्पत् ॥
verses.rom: maya hi tatra charau sakalaishvaryaviryashauryabalasampad aropita tvadiyacharau api akhilashantijnanatitikshadibrahmanagunasampat ||

verses.sa: तच्च विपरीतं कुर्वत्याः तव अतिरौद्रास्त्रधारणपालननिष्ठः क्षत्रियाचारः पुत्रो भविष्यति, तस्याश्च उपशमरुचिः ब्राह्मणाचार” इत्याकर्ण्यैव सा तस्य पादौ जग्राह ॥
verses.rom: tachcha viparitam kurvatyah tava atiraudrastradharanapalananishthah kshatriyacharah putro bhavishyati, tasyashcha upashamaruchih brahmanachara” ityakarnyaiva sa tasya padau jagraha ||

verses.sa: प्रणिपत्य चैनमाह ॥
“भगवन् मया एतदज्ञानादनुष्ठितं, प्रसादं मे कुरु, मैवंविधः पुत्रो भवतु, काममेवंविधः पौत्रो भवतु” इत्युक्ते मुनिरप्याह ॥
verses.rom: “bhagavan maya etadajnanadanushthitam, prasadam me kuru, maivamvidhah putro bhavatu, kamamevamvidhah pautro bhavatu” ityukte munirapyaha ||

verses.sa: “एवमस्तु” इति ॥
अनन्तरञ्च सा जमदग्निम् अजीजनत् ॥
तन्माता च विश्वामित्रं जनयामास ॥
सत्यवत्यपि कौशिकी नाम नदी अभवत् ॥
जमदग्निः इक्ष्वाकुवंशोद्भवस्य रेणोः तनयां रेणुकाम् उपयेमे ॥
verses.rom: jamadagnih ikshvakuvamshodbhavasya renoh tanayam renukam upayeme ||

verses.sa: तस्यां चाशेषक्षत्रहन्तारं परशुरामसंज्ञं भगवतः सकललोकगुरोः नारायणस्यांशं जमदग्निः अजीजनत् ॥
verses.rom: tasyam chasheshakshatrahantaram parashuramasamjnam bhagavatah sakalalokaguroh narayanasyamsham jamadagnih ajijanat ||

verses.sa: विश्वामित्रपुत्रस्तु भार्गव एव शुनश्शेपो देवैर्दत्तः, ततश्च देवरातनामाभवत् ॥
verses.rom: vishvamitraputrastu bhargava eva shunashshepo devairdattah, tatashcha devaratanamabhavat ||

verses.sa: ततश्च अन्ये मधुच्छन्दो धनञ्जयकृतदेवाष्टक-कच्छप-हारीतकाख्याः विश्वामित्रपुत्राः बभूवुः ॥
तेषां च बहूनि कौशिकगोत्राणि ऋष्यन्तरेषु विवाह्यानि अभवन् ॥
verses.rom: tesham cha bahuni kaushikagotrani rishyantareshu vivahyani abhavan ||

verses.sa: ॥ इति श्रीविष्णुमहापुराणे चतुर्थांशो सप्तमोऽध्यायः ॥

prose.en:
Pururavas had six sons—Ayus, Dhimat, Amāvasu, Viswavasu, Satayus, and Srutayus. The son of Amāvasu was Bhima, whose son was Kānchana, whose son was Suhotra, whose name was Jahnu. Whilst celebrating a sacrifice this king beheld the whole of the place over-flowed with the waters of the Ganga. Being offended therefore with his eyes red with anger he united the spirit of sacrifice with himself and by the power of his devotion drunk up the river. Thereupon the celestials and the sages pleased him and got back Gangā in the capacity of his daughter.

The son of Jahnu was Sumanta, whose son was Ajaka, whose son was Valakāswa, whose son was Kusa, who had four sons, Kusamba. Kusanābha, Amurttaya and Amāyasu.

Kusambha engaged in devout penances with the object of having a son equal to Indra. Beholding the intensity of his devotions, Indra himself took birth as his son lest a prince equally powerful like him might be born. He was accordingly born as Gadhi or Kausika. Gadhi had a daughter called Satyavati. Richika, one of the descendants of Bhrigu, wanted her in marriage. The king was reluctant to give his daughter in marriage to a peevish old Brāhmin and wanted from him as the bridal present a thousand fleet steeds whose colour should be white with one black ear. Having propitiated Varuna, the god of ocean, Richika obtained from him, at the holy place called Awatirtha a thousand horses. And giving them to the king he married his daughter.

In order to have a son he prepared a dish of rice, barley and pulse with butter and milk for his wife to eat. And being requested by her he made a similar mixture for her mother, by partaking of which she should give birth to a martial prince. Keeping both the dishes with his wife and giving her instructions which was intended for her and which for her mother, the sage went to the forest. At the time of taking the food her mother said to Satyabati—"Daughter, every one wants to have a son gifted with great qualities—and no body wishes to be excelled by the qualities of his mother's brother. It is therefore desirable for you to give me the food which your husband has set apart for you and to partake of that intended for me; for my son shall be the sovereign of the world. What is the use of wealth, strength and prowess for a Brahmin". Being thus addressed Satyavati gave her own food to her mother.

When the sage came back from the forest and saw Satyavati he said to her—"Sinful woman, what hast thou done? Your body appears as very fearful to me. Surely thou hast taken the food which was intended for thy mother. Thou hast committed a wrong. That food I had consecrated with the properties of power, strength and heroism; whereas your food was consecrated with the qualities of a Brāhman—gentleness, knowledge and resignation. As you have exchanged messes your son shall follow a warrior's propensities and use weapons, and fight and slay; your mother's son shall be born with the desires of a Brāhmin and shall be devoted to peace and piety". Hearing this Satyavati fell at her husband's feet and said—"I have done this through my ignorance. Be thou propitiated so that I may not have such a son. If this is inevitably let my grand son be such, not my son". Being thus addressed the sage said—"So be it".

Thereupon she gave birth Jamadagni and her mother brought forth Viswamitra. Satyavati afterwards became the Kausiki river, Jamadagni married Renukā the daughter of Renu, born in the race of Ikshwaku and begot on her a son, Parusarāma the destroyer of the Kshatriya race, who was a portion of Nārāyana, the preceptor of the universe. Sunasepha was conferred upon Viswamitra by the celestials as his son, who became known as Devarata. Viswamitra had other sons—Madhuchandra, Yaya, Kritadeva, Devashtaka, Kachapa and Hareetaka. These founded many families, all of whom were known by the name of Kausikas, and inter-married with the families of various Rishis.

verses.sa:
॥ अथ अष्टमोऽध्यायः ॥
(काश्यवंशवर्णनम्)
श्रीपराशर उवाच
पुरूरवसो ज्येष्ठः पुत्रो यस्त्वायुर्नामा स राहोर्दुहितरमुपयेमे ॥
verses.rom:
|| atha ashtamo'dhyayah ||
(kashyavamshavarnanam)
shriparashara uvacha
pururavaso jyeshthah putro yastvayurnama sa rahorduhitaramupayeme ||

verses.sa: तस्यां च पञ्च पुत्रान् उत्पादयामास ॥
नहुष-क्षत्रवृद्ध-रम्भ-रजिसंज्ञाः तथैव अनेनाः पञ्चमः पुत्रोऽभूत् ॥
क्षत्रवृद्धात्सुहोत्रः पुत्रोऽभवत् ॥
काश्य-काश-गृत्समदाः त्रयस्तस्य पुत्रा बभूवुः ॥
गृत्समदस्य शौनकः चातुर्वर्ण्यप्रवर्तयिताऽभूत् ॥
काश्यस्य काशेयः काशिराजः, तस्मात् राष्ट्रः, राष्ट्रस्य दीर्घतपाः पुत्रोऽभवत् ॥
verses.rom: kashyasya kasheyah kashirajah, tasmat rashtrah, rashtrasya dirghatapah putro'bhavat ||

verses.sa: धन्वन्तरिस्तु दीर्घतपसः पुत्रोऽभवत् ॥
स हि संसिद्ध-कार्य-करणः सकलसम्भूतिषु अशेषज्ञानविद् भगवता नारायणेन च अतीतसम्भूतौ तस्मै वरो दत्तः ॥
verses.rom: sa hi samsiddha-karya-karanah sakalasambhutishu asheshajnanavid bhagavata narayanena cha atitasambhutau tasmai varo dattah ||

verses.sa: “काशीराजगोत्रेऽवतीर्य त्वमष्टधा सम्यगायुर्वेदं करिष्यसि यज्ञभागभुग्भविष्यसि” इति ॥
तस्य च धन्वन्तरेः पुत्रः केतुमान्, केतुमतो भीमरथः, तस्यापि दिवोदासः, तस्यापि प्रतर्दनः ॥
verses.rom: tasya cha dhanvantareh putrah ketuman, ketumato bhimarathah, tasyapi divodasah, tasyapi pratardanah ||

verses.sa: स च मद्रश्रेण्य-वंश-विनाशनात् अशेषशत्रवोऽनेन जिता इति शत्रुजिदभवत् ॥
verses.rom: sa cha madrashrenya-vamsha-vinashanat asheshashatravo'nena jita iti shatrujidabhavat ||

verses.sa: तेन च प्रीतिमतात्मपुत्रो वत्सवत्सेत्यभिहितो वत्सोऽभवत् ॥
सत्यपरतया ऋतध्वजसंज्ञामवाप ॥
ततश्च कुवलयनामानमश्वं लेभे ततः कुवलयाश्व इत्यस्यां पृथिव्यां प्रथितः ॥
verses.rom: tatashcha kuvalayanamanamashvam lebhe tatah kuvalayashva ityasyam prithivyam prathitah ||

verses.sa: तस्य च वत्सस्य पुत्रोऽलर्कनामाभवत् यस्यायमद्यापि श्लोको गीयते ॥
verses.rom: tasya cha vatsasya putro'larkanamabhavat yasyayamadyapi shloko giyate ||

verses.sa:
षष्टिवर्षसहस्राणि षष्टिवर्षशतानि च ।
अलर्कादपरो नान्यो बुभुजे मेदिनीं युवा ॥
verses.rom:
shashtivarshasahasrani shashtivarshashatani cha |
alarkadaparo nanyo bubhuje medinim yuva ||

verses.sa: तस्याप्यलर्कस्य सन्नतिनामाऽभवदात्मजः ॥
सन्नतेः सुनीथस्तस्यापि सुकेतुस्तस्माच्च धर्मकेतुर्जज्ञे ॥
ततश्च सत्यकेतुस्तस्माद्विभुस्तत्तनयस्सुविभुस्ततश्च सुकुमारस्तस्यापि दृष्टकेतुस्ततश्च वीतिहोत्रस्तस्माद्भार्गो भार्गस्य भार्गभूमिस्ततश्चातुर्वर्ण्यप्रवृत्तिरित्येते काश्यपभूभृतः कथिताः ॥
verses.rom: tatashcha satyaketustasmadvibhustattanayassuvibhustatashcha sukumarastasyapi drishtaketustatashcha vitihotrastasmadbhargo bhargasya bhargabhumistatashchaturvarnyapravrittirityete kashyapabhubhritah kathitah ||

verses.sa: रजेस्तु सन्ततिः श्रूयताम् ॥
॥ इति श्रीविष्णुमाहापुराणे चतुर्थांशे अष्टमोऽध्यायः ॥

prose.en:
Ayus, the eldest son of Pururavas, married the daughter of Rahu upon whom he begot five sons, Nahusha, Kshatravridha, Rambha, Raji and Anenas.

The son of Kshatravridha was Suhotra, who had three sons, Kash, Lesa, and Ghritsamanda. The son of Ghritsamnada was Saunaka who first instituted the distinction of the four castes. The son of Kasa was Kasiraja, whose son was Dirghatama, whose son was Dhanwantari, who was not subject to human infirmities and who had been master of universal knowledge in every birth. In his past life Nārāyana had conferred upon him the boon that he should be, in his next life, born in the race of Kshatriya, should be the author of the eight fold system of medical science and should be entitled to a share of offerings made to the celestials. The son of Dhanwantari, was Kesumat, whose son was Bhimaratha, whose son was Devadasa, whose son was Pratarddana, so called from destroying the race of Bhadrasrenya. He had various other names—as Satrujit. 'The victor of enemies' on account of his having defeated all his enemies Vatsa or 'child' for his father used to call him often times by that name; Ritadhwaja 'whose emblem was truth' for he was a great observer of truth; and Kuvalayaswa for he had a horse called Kuvalaya. His son was Alarka of whom this verse is recited in the present day—"For sixty thousand and sixty hundred years, no other youthful king except Alarka governed the earth". The son of Alarka was Santati, whose son was Sunitha, whose son was Suketu, whose son was Dharmaketu, whose son was Satyaketu, whose son was Vibhu, whose son was Suvibhu, whose son was Sukumara, whose son was Dhristaketu, whose son was Vainahotra whose son was Bharga, whose son was Bhargabhumi, who laid down the rules of the four castes. These are the descendants of Kasa. We shall now enumerate the descendants of Raji.

verses.sa:
॥ अथ नवमोऽध्यायः ॥
(रजेः क्षत्रवृद्धस्य च वंशकथनम्)
श्रीपराशर उवाच
रजेस्तु पञ्च पुत्रशतानि अतुलबलपराक्रमसाराणि आसन् ॥
verses.rom:
|| atha navamo'dhyayah ||
(rajeh kshatravriddhasya cha vamshakathanam)
shriparashara uvacha
rajestu pancha putrashatani atulabalaparakramasarani asan ||

verses.sa: देवासुरसंग्रामारम्भे च परस्परवधेप्सवो देवाश्चासुराश्च ब्रह्माणमुपेत्य पप्रच्छुः ॥
verses.rom: devasurasamgramarambhe cha parasparavadhepsavo devashchasurashcha brahmanamupetya paprachchhuh ||

verses.sa: “भगवन् अस्माकमत्र विरोधे कतरः पक्षो जेता भविष्यति” इति ॥
verses.rom: “bhagavan asmakamatra virodhe katarah paksho jeta bhavishyati” iti ||

verses.sa: अथाह भगवान् ॥
“येषामर्थे रजिरात्तायुधो योत्स्याति तत्पक्षो जेता” इति ॥
अथ दैत्यैरुपेत्य रजिः आत्मसाहाय्यदानाय अभ्यर्थितः प्राह ॥
verses.rom: atha daityairupetya rajih atmasahayyadanaya abhyarthitah praha ||

verses.sa: “योत्स्येऽहं भवतामर्थे यद्यहममरजयाद्भवतामिन्द्रो भविष्यामि” इत्याकर्ण्यैतत् तैरभिहितम् ॥

“न वयमन्यथा वदिष्यामोऽन्यथा करिष्यामोऽस्माकमिन्द्रः प्रह्लादस्तदर्थमेवायमुद्यम” इत्युक्त्वा गतेष्वसुरेषु, देवैरपि असौ अवनीपतिः एवमेव उक्तः, तेनापि च तथैवोक्ते देवैः “इन्द्रस्त्वं भविष्यसि” इति समन्वीप्सितम् ॥
verses.rom: “na vayamanyatha vadishyamo'nyatha karishyamo'smakamindrah prahladastadarthamevayamudyama” ityuktva gateshvasureshu, devairapi asau avanipatih evameva uktah, tenapi cha tathaivokte devaih “indrastvam bhavishyasi” iti samanvipsitam ||

verses.sa: रजिनापि देवसैन्यसहायेनानेकैर्महास्त्रैस्तदशेषमहासुरबलं निषूदितम् ॥
अथ जितारातिपक्षश्च देवेन्द्रो रजिचरणयुगलमात्मनः शिरसा निपीड्याह ॥
verses.rom: atha jitaratipakshashcha devendro rajicharanayugalamatmanah shirasa nipidyaha ||

verses.sa: “भयत्राणात् अन्नदानात् भवान् अस्मत्पिता अशेषलोकानामुत्तमोत्तमो भवान् यस्याहं पुत्रस्त्रिलोकेन्द्रः” ॥
verses.rom: “bhayatranat annadanat bhavan asmatpita asheshalokanamuttamottamo bhavan yasyaham putrastrilokendrah” ||

verses.sa: स चापि राजा प्रहस्याह ॥
“एवमस्त्वेवमस्तु, अनतिक्रमणीया हि वैरिपक्षादपि अनेकविधचाटुवाक्यगर्भा प्रणतिः” इत्युक्त्वा स्वपुरं जगाम ॥
verses.rom: “evamastvevamastu, anatikramaniya hi vairipakshadapi anekavidhachatuvakyagarbha pranatih” ityuktva svapuram jagama ||

verses.sa: शतक्रतुरपीन्द्रत्वं चकार ॥
स्वर्याते तु रजौ नारदर्षिचोदिता रजिपुत्राः शतक्रतुमात्मपितृपुत्रं समाचाराद्राज्यं याचितवन्तः ॥
verses.rom: svaryate tu rajau naradarshichodita rajiputrah shatakratumatmapitriputram samacharadrajyam yachitavantah ||

verses.sa: अप्रदानेन च विजित्येन्द्रम् अतिबलिनः स्वयमिन्द्रत्वं चक्रुः ॥
verses.rom: apradanena cha vijityendram atibalinah svayamindratvam chakruh ||

verses.sa: ततश्च बहुतिथे काले ह्यतीते बृहस्पतिमेकान्ते दृष्ट्वा अपहृतत्रैलोक्ययज्ञभागः शतक्रतुरुवाच ॥
verses.rom: tatashcha bahutithe kale hyatite brihaspatimekante drishtva apahritatrailokyayajnabhagah shatakraturuvacha ||

verses.sa: “बदरीफलमात्रमपि अर्हसि ममाप्यायनाय पुरोडाशखण्डं दातुम्” इत्युक्तो बृहस्पतिरुवाच ॥
verses.rom: “badariphalamatramapi arhasi mamapyayanaya purodashakhandam datum” ityukto brihaspatiruvacha ||

verses.sa: “यद्येवं त्वयाहं पूर्वमेव चोदितः स्यां तन्मया त्वदर्थं किमकर्तव्यमिति अल्पैरेवाहोभिः त्वां निजं पदं प्रापयिष्यामि” इत्यभिधाय तेषामनुदिनाभिचारिकं बुद्धिमोहाय शक्रस्य तेजोऽभिवृद्धये जुहाव ॥
verses.rom: “yadyevam tvayaham purvameva choditah syam tanmaya tvadartham kimakartavyamiti alpairevahobhih tvam nijam padam prapayishyami” ityabhidhaya teshamanudinabhicharikam buddhimohaya shakrasya tejo'bhivriddhaye juhava ||

verses.sa: ते चापि तेन बुद्धिमोहेनाभिभूयमाना ब्रह्मद्विषो धर्मत्यागिनो वेदवादपराङ्मुखा बभूवुः ॥
